q: What happens to the wastewater in a septic tank?

Deep sea decomposers break down carbonate shells

q: Which of the following BEST explains why there is typically less temperature variation along the coasts of continents versus inland climates at the same latitude:

the friction between waves and the shore add heats to the area
water can absorb and release large amounts of heat with very little change in temperature
surface ocean currents along shorelines typically carry warm water

q: Destruction of Earth's ozone layer is expected to increase the incidence of all but which of the following?

q: In the United States, which of the following renewable energy sources provides the smallest annual energy output?

q: Which of the following is NOT generally characteristic of oceanic-continental plate boundaries:

q: Which of the following is the global wind system that most influences weather between 60 and 90 north and south latitudes:

q: Which of the following is NOT true of the ozone layer:

the ozone molecule has 3 oxygen atoms
in addition to chlorine, bromine is also responsible for combining with and breaking down the ozone molecule
holes in the ozone layer are produced by global warming

As air moves up the windward side of the mountain, it expands and warms
The windward side of a mountain receives a lot of rain

q: Which of the following is TRUE about Earth's atmosphere:

moist air weighs more than dry air at the same temperature
the tropopause is higher at the South Pole than at the equator

q: If you were looking at isobars on a weather map showing high latitudes and high altitudes, which of the following would indicate the fastest wind speed?
e: Squeezing a big four-millibar pressure change into just fifty kilometers creates a steep hill that sends winds zooming fastest!

q: The dynamo effect enables Earth's core to generate what?
e: Earth's swirling liquid core acts like a giant spinning engine, wrapping our whole planet in a cozy, invisible magnetic field.

q: Which of the following types of weather front is indicated by an alternating red and blue line on a weather map?
e: When warm and cold air push against each other and refuse to budge, they create a stationary front that stays glued in place.

q: What is the highest mountain in the world?
e: Mount Everest pokes straight into the clouds, standing taller than any other snowy peak on our whole planet!

q: Important mineral deposits and large reservoirs of petroleum and natural gas are associated with which of the following?
e: Continental shelves are gentle underwater ledges where ancient buried life slowly cooked into rich treasure chests of oil and gas.

q: What African country has Portuguese as its official language?
e: Mozambique speaks Portuguese as its official language because explorers from Portugal sailed in and ran the country long ago.

q: Which of the following is the global wind system that most influences weather in Denver Colorado:
e: The prevailing westerlies are giant rivers of air that blow from the west, steering storms and sunshine right over Denver!

q: What type of unconformity occurs when rocks are tiled and eroded before younger rocks are deposited?
e: When rock layers tilt at a crazy slant before new flat ones pile on top, geologists call it an angular unconformity.

q: Which of the following is primarily involved in the movement of a glacier:
e: Glaciers are massive ice rivers, and trusty gravity gives them the gentle downhill tug they need to creep forward.

q: Which of the following is a mineral?
e: While the others are rock mixtures, muscovite is a pure mineral that peels apart into neat, shiny little sheets!

q: Which of the following is NOT directly or indirectly a result of a large earthquake:
e: Shaking ground can trigger giant waves or fires, but lightning belongs to stormy clouds way up in the sky.

q: Where is Hadrian's Wall located?
e: Ancient Roman soldiers marched across northern England and built this great stone wall right near Carlisle.

q: Which of the following oceanic currents prevents the climate of Northern Europe from being much colder?
e: The Gulf Stream acts like a warm ocean river, carrying tropical heat northward to keep European winters from freezing solid.

q: Which of the following is NOT true of geodes:
a: they occur in sedimentary and certain volcanic rocks
they look like ordinary rocks from the outside
their exterior is typically made up of limestone
they are not found in the U.S.
e: Geodes hide sparkly crystal secrets all across America, so saying they are not found in the U.S. is totally untrue!

q: Which of the following is primarily responsible for the presence of carbon-14 used in radiometric dating?
e: Tiny cosmic rays zipping in from outer space strike air atoms, creating carbon-14 like magical star dust.

q: What is the capital of Laos?
e: Peaceful Vientiane sits right along the curving Mekong River, guiding Laos as its bustling capital city.

q: Which of the following sets of conditions is most conducive to ductile deformation of rock?
e: Deep underground, baking heat and crushing pressure turn stiff, stubborn rocks squishy so they bend like warm taffy instead of snapping!

q: Which of the following moves in the form of a longitudinal compression wave:
e: Sound travels by squishing air molecules together and letting them spring back, passing whispers like a friendly game of tag!

q: Chalk is a type of:
e: Chalk is actually a soft, crumbly type of limestone, built from billions of tiny seashell skeletons piling up over millions of years.

q: Savannah River National Lab scientists are studying the diversity of macroinvertebrates in local streams. Which of the following animals is a macroinvertebrate they are studying?
e: Mayflies are spineless water bugs big enough to spot with your bare eyes, making them the perfect stream macroinvertebrates!

q: An igneous rock in which individual mineral grains or crystals are visible to the naked eye most likely was formed by which of the following processes:
e: When underground melted rock takes a long, cozy nap to cool down slowly, its crystals have time to grow big and sparkly.

q: Which of the following is, to date, the most promising method of disposing of nuclear waste?
a: Storing it underground in a geologic formation
Storing it in a low-level disposal vault
Diluting it before pouring it into the ocean
e: Tucking dangerous waste deep inside ancient, sturdy underground rock keeps it safely locked away where it can do no harm.

q: Which of the following is NOT true about glaciations:
a: about 15,000 years ago, most of Wisconsin was buried under thick glacial ice
throughout history, times such as now when only minor ice sheets existed coincided with high sea levels
because of its high altitude, Mt. Everest contains a vast continental glacier
Australia does not currently contain any glaciers
e: Mount Everest has icy mountain glaciers, but only giant, flat lands like Antarctica can wear a sprawling continental ice sheet!

q: Which of the following seismic waves causes rock particles to move back and forth in the same direction as the wave is moving, much like the wave propagation in an outstretched spring that is hit on one end:
e: P-waves race forward like a squished toy spring, shoving rock back and forth in the exact same direction the wave travels!

q: A deep-ocean trench can form at which of the following tectonic plate boundaries?
e: When a heavy ocean plate slides underneath a lighter continent, it pulls the seafloor down to carve out a super-deep trench!

q: Which of the following tectonic settings is MOST conducive to geothermal power generation?
e: Where tectonic plates bump and grind, blazing heat from deep inside Earth sneaks close to the surface, making perfect natural steam power!

q: The hydrologic cycle describes the circulation of Earth's:
e: Water is Earth's greatest traveler, constantly cycling from ocean puddles up to fluffy clouds and raining back down again.

q: The Earth's mantle is thought to be composed of which of the following:
e: Earth's giant mantle is mostly made of peridotite, a heavy green rock packed with sparkly olive-colored crystals!

q: Which of the following is believed to create Earth's magnetic field:
a: the tilt in Earth's axis rocking Earth's inner core
the spinning of Earth's outer core
how fast the Earth revolves around the Sun
e: Deep down, Earth's outer core swirls with melted iron, acting like a giant spinning engine to create our magnetic field.

q: In which of the following environments would you typically find a skarn?
e: When sizzling magma pushes into nearby rocks like a nosy neighbor, its hot fluids bake everything into a brand-new rock called a skarn!

q: Which part of Earth's atmosphere is farthest from Earth's surface?
e: The exosphere floats at the very tippy-top of our atmosphere, gently waving goodbye to Earth as it blends into space.

q: Which of the following is true about divergent plate boundaries where the lithosphere is being pushed and pulled apart?
a: They only occur along the seafloor
They are sites of the most explosive volcanism known on earth
They are no longer active but there is evidence of volcanism from millions of years ago
Magma from the mantle is exposed at the surface and cools to form new lithospheric (read as: li-thoh-SFIR-ik) crust
e: As plates pull apart, hot melted rock bubbles up from below, cooling down to pave fresh new crust on Earth's surface!

q: Japan has left-hand side traffic.
e: Yes, it is true! Cars in Japan politely cruise along the left side of the road.

q: A rock formation is subjected to compressional forces at depths where ductile deformation occurs. Which of the following features will likely form?
e: Deep down where hot rock is soft and bendy, big squeezes wrinkle the stone into graceful wavy folds instead of snapping it!

q: A high-pressure weather system is typically associated with which of the following conditions:
e: Sinking heavy air gently shoos away stormy clouds, leaving behind crisp, cool air and just a few wispy, high-flying clouds.

q: Relative to conventional sources, such as liquid oil and natural gas, combustion of biomass for heat and electricity does NOT create more of which of the following?
e: Because friendly plants drink up carbon while growing, burning biomass does not add extra greenhouse gases compared to stubborn fossil fuels.

q: Most of the CO2 presently entering Earth's atmosphere is generated by human activities. Which of the following is closest to the percentage of CO2 released into the atmosphere by land and sea volcanoes combined?
e: Even our mightiest rumbling volcanoes only burp out about one percent of Earth's carbon dioxide, leaving the rest to us!

q: Which of these minerals would scratch all of the others?
e: Orthoclase is the toughest of the bunch with a hardness of six, easily scratching softer pals like gypsum, calcite, and fluorite!

q: In which of the following locations are you most likely to find sandstone rock formations?
a: Areas with a long history of earthquakes
Swamps formed within the last thousand years
Areas with a history of lava deposition
e: Long ago, sunny beaches and windy deserts piled up mountains of sand, which time gently squeezed into beautiful sandstone.

q: When geologists are studying a geologic unit that contains folds and faults, they typically assume that geologic units didn't start with folds and faults. This is an application of which of the following?
e: Mud settles flat like cozy pancake batter, so original horizontality reminds us that all folded rocks started out totally flat.

q: In what geological period did the first organisms with shells first become abundant:
e: During the bustling Cambrian period, little ocean critters finally built their very first hard, cozy shells to stay safe.

q: S-waves produced by earthquakes, do not travel through the Earth's:
e: S-waves love dancing through solid rock, but they completely stop when they bump into Earth's liquid outer core.

q: What type of ocean wave has a typical period of approximately one hundredth of a second?
e: Capillary waves are tiny, nervous little ripples made by gentle breezes that flutter by in a quick hundredth of a second.

q: Which of the following types of rocks hosts the best-preserved fossils?
e: Quiet, oxygen-free muddy waters form black shale, a cozy blanket that preserves fragile ancient fossils like tiny time capsules.

q: How many timezones does Russia have?
e: Russia is so gigantic that clocks tick through eleven different time zones as the sun rises across its land!

q: Which of the following best describes how a sedimentary rock can form:
a: slow cooling and hardening of magma
fast cooling and hardening of magma
high temperature and pressure causing recrystalization
e: Tiny bits of sand and mud get squished tight and glued together over time, turning soft layers into solid sedimentary rock.

q: Israel is 7 hours ahead of New York.
e: While New York wakes up to breakfast, clocks in Israel are already ticking toward dinner, seven whole hours ahead.

q: What is the capital of Slovakia?
e: Bratislava sits proudly along the blue Danube River, serving as the bustling, castle-topped capital of Slovakia.

q: Streams running off the terminus of glaciers have a high bed load and easily erodible banks, typically forming which of the following types of stream patterns:
e: When rushing glacial waters cut shortcuts across bendy curves, they leave behind quiet, curved oxbow channels.

q: Compared to other methods of electricity production, hydroelectric power possesses all EXCEPT which of the following advantages?
a: Low environmental impact in case of disaster
e: Dams make clean power, but if one breaks, the rushing water unleashes a giant disaster on nature.

q: Which of the following is most important for climate because it transports large amounts of heat and moisture from the ocean to land:
e: Giant seasonal winds called monsoons gulp up wet ocean air and dump life-giving rain across thirsty continents.

q: Which of the following is a mudflow that moves rapidly down the side of a volcano because of the rapid mixing of melted snow and pyroclastic material:
e: When a fiery volcano melts mountaintop snow into a speedy mudslide, that wild river of mud is called a lahar.

q: Volcanoes and earthquakes occur primarily in which of the following locations:
a: at the North and South Poles
e: Earth's crust is like giant puzzle pieces, and whenever they bump or slide at their edges, volcanoes erupt and ground rumbles!

q: Which of the following characteristics is generally NOT used for classification of ocean waves?
e: Ocean waves stretch tall and shrink constantly, so scientists cannot use ever-changing wave height to neatly sort them.

q: Which of the following does the elastic rebound theory describe?
a: The build up and release of stress during an earthquake
The fluctuations in groundwater prior to an earthquake
The formation of mountain ranges by successive earthquakes
e: Rocks bend like stiff rubber bands until they suddenly snap, releasing all that trapped stress in an earthquake's elastic rebound.

q: In which of the following locations would you typically expect the average salinity of surface sea water to be the LOWEST:
a: at the mouth of the Mississippi River
e: The mighty Mississippi River empties so much sweet, fresh water into the ocean that it completely waters down the salt!

q: The spring 2011 earthquake in Japan occurred because Japan is located on which of the following?
e: Deep below Japan, in a subduction zone, one giant puzzle piece of Earth slowly dives under another until they suddenly snap!

q: Which of the following is NOT true of tornados in the U.S.:
a: the funnel cloud typically develops out of a nimbostratus cloud
their strength is measured with Fujita Scale
supercells are the most dangerous and violent tornadoes in the U.S.
wind speeds can reach an excess of 200 mph
e: Wild tornadoes drop from towering cumulonimbus storm clouds bursting with energy, never from flat, sleepy sheets of nimbostratus clouds.

q: Which of the following bodies of water does an atoll usually enclose?
e: An atoll is a cozy ring of coral that wraps its arms around a calm, sparkly pool called a lagoon.

q: What rock type can be divided into intrusive and extrusive sub- categories?
e: Born from fiery melted rock, igneous rocks are named by cooling slowly inside Earth as intrusive or outside as extrusive.

q: Which of the following is often the LEAST reliable property of a mineral that is used in mineral identification:
e: Minerals love playing dress-up, so a single kind can wear many confusing colors and fool even careful rock collectors.

q: Where does sea ice form first?
e: Shallow water near the shore chills much faster than the deep ocean, letting icy crystals click together first.

q: Which of the following environments is most likely to host a community of methane producing organisms?
e: Deep down by scalding hydrothermal vents, tough little microbes love the toasty, sunless waters and happily burp out methane!

q: Which of the following rocks has both high porosity and high permeability?
e: Sandstone is packed with tiny open pockets and roomy passageways, letting underground water soak right in and flow freely through!

q: Which of the following depicts an accurate relationship between river water and groundwater within one watershed area?
a: River water may be polluted but groundwater lacks pollutants
They are the same, though the water may pick up slightly different chemicals and minerals as it moves through the ground
Groundwater can be contaminated by septic tanks but rivers cannot
Rivers flow into the ocean but groundwater cannot
e: River water and groundwater are the very same water playing hide-and-seek, just collecting extra minerals while journeying underground.

q: The longest-ranging ice core temperature records come from the Dome C ice core recovered in Antarctica. Which of the following is nearest to the number of years covered by the Dome C ice core?
e: This giant Antarctic ice core holds tiny trapped bubbles that whisper Earth's ancient climate secrets from 800,000 chilly years ago.

q: Which of the following sources provides the most water for drinking and industrial purposes in the US?
e: Because bubbling rivers and lakes sit right on the surface, fresh surface water is the easiest drink for cities to scoop up!

q: Which of the following is the underlying cause of most volcanoes on Earth?
e: Earth wears a cracked shell of tectonic plates, and when they bump or slide, fiery magma sneaks through to build volcanoes.

q: Which of the following is considered a mineral?
e: Because natural ice grows into orderly, solid crystals without any help from living things, it is officially a true mineral!

q: Stromatolites were once very common but are now quite rare. Which of the following is a plausible explanation?
a: Light conditions are no longer favorable for the photosynthetic organisms that form stromatolites
Ocean acidification makes the formation of stromatolites difficult
Few places are warm enough for the organisms that form stromatolites
The organisms that produce stromatolites were not able to compete effectively enough with other organisms
e: These ancient rock-making microbes were so slow and peaceful that newer, speedier sea critters easily outcompeted them for food and space.

q: Which of the following is LEAST indicated by closely spaced isobars on a weather map:
a: a steep gradient between high and low pressure areas
e: Crowded pressure lines show where wild winds blow, but they cannot tell you whether the sky will drop rain, sleet, or snow.

q: When lengthy and lasting jet contrails predominate in the sky, which of the following is the most likely forecast:
a: fair weather with increasing cirrus or cirrostratus clouds
e: When white plane trails linger like chalk marks, the high air is moist, inviting wispy cirrus clouds into a fair, sunny day.

q: What silicate group is first to crystallize from a cooling magma?
e: Nesosilicates have simple mineral shapes that love scorching heat, so they freeze into the very first crystals as magma cools.

q: Which of the following is closest to the ratio of the thickness of the mantle to that of the outer core?
e: Earth's rocky mantle and liquid outer core are like cozy cosmic twins, matching each other almost evenly at a one-to-one thickness.

q: What term describes a region where fresh water flows to the surface from underground?
e: When hidden underground water finally finds an escape and bubbles up into the warm sunshine, that fresh pool is a spring!

q: Worldwide, over 70% of the total length of beaches has retreated at a rate of 10 centimeters per year. Which of the following is primarily responsible for this dramatic change?
a: Decrease in the number of groins permitted
e: Big river dams trap sand upstream, starving our beaches of the fresh grains they need to stay wide and cozy.

q: The presence of fossilized marine organisms in rocks high above sea level is best explained by which of the following statements?
a: They were carried there by other animals
They were once beneath the sea and tectonic processes raised the sediments
They were once part of a volcanic eruption
e: Ancient seashells on mountain tops were once deep underwater before restless tectonic plates lifted the sea floor into the sky!

q: What rock type is dominant in the uppermost mantle?
e: Deep beneath our feet, Earth's upper mantle is packed full of peridotite, a dense, greenish rock that loves living in the heat.

q: Which of the following pairs of rocks are formed by volcanic froth creating a vesicular texture?
e: When volcanoes burp fizzy lava, pumice and scoria freeze into foamy rocks full of trapped gas bubbles!

q: An igneous rock has a porphyritic texture. Which of the following does this indicate about the cooling history?
a: It cooled in stages, at different levels within the crust
It cooled rapidly near the surface
It cooled on the surface and was quenched
It cooled slowly, at one time, at depth
e: This rock cooled in stages underground, growing big crystals deep down before finishing quickly near the surface.

q: Which of the following lists the four upper spheres of Earth in the correct order of their chronological development?
e: Earth first formed its rocky lithosphere, puffed out an atmosphere, poured the hydrosphere oceans, and finally welcomed the living biosphere.

q: In what geologic era are we currently living?
e: We share our home in the Cenozoic era, a wonderful age of mammals that began after the dinosaurs stepped down.

q: Biodiesel, which is another form of biomass energy, is obtained from:
a: Food products, including vegetable oils and animal fats
Combining diesel with extractions from mineral beds
Using a plant's photosynthesis (read as: fe-te-SIN-teh-sis) process
e: Leftover cooking oils and kitchen fats get a fantastic second life by being transformed into clean-burning biodiesel.

q: The ocean conveyor belt is driven by which of the following?
a: Tidal phases and the Earth's rotation
e: Wind currents and changes in heat and saltiness—called thermohaline gradients—team up to push this giant ocean river along.

q: Which of the following is LEAST likely to occur at a subduction zone?
e: Subduction zones feature plates diving deep down, so plates sliding sideways in transform faulting happen somewhere else entirely.

q: Which of the following minerals best illustrates the property of cleavage:
e: Mica shows off its cleavage by peeling into wonderfully smooth, flat sheets, just like pages in a tiny notebook.

q: Which of the following percentages best represents the amount of the Earth's freshwater supply that can be found in lakes and rivers?
e: Most freshwater hides frozen in glaciers or underground, leaving just a tiny 0.3% splashing around in our lakes and rivers.

q: What is the fifth largest country by area?
e: Brazil is so massive that it swallows nearly half of South America, making it the fifth-biggest country on our planet.

q: Which of the following locations would you study if you wanted to collect a sample of atmospheric carbon dioxide from one thousand years ago?
e: Chilly glacier ice traps ancient air in tiny, sparkling bubbles, keeping a thousand-year-old breath of our planet safe and sound.

q: The source of energy for the movements of crustal plates is currently thought to be the result of:
a: tidal motion that produces a net westward movement of landmasses
the pulling apart of the poles resulting from the Earth's rotation
convection currents produced within the mantle
e: Deep inside Earth, hot rock swirls in slow convection currents, carrying giant crust plates around like rafts.

q: Which of the following fossils is the oldest:
e: Little armored trilobites scuttled across ancient sea floors over five hundred million years ago, easily beating trees and snakes to the punch!

q: Which of the following is NOT true about the Appalachian Mountain Range:
a: it is older than the Himalayan range
the southeastern portion is undergoing accelerated mountain building
it occurs along an ancient plate boundary
e: These sleepy, ancient mountains finished growing long ago, so rain and wind are gently wearing them down instead of building them up.

q: Which of the following is NOT thought to have initiated the Permian-Triassic mass extinction?
e: Fiery volcanoes and wild climate shifts doomed ancient creatures, but a widespread disease never caused that gigantic, world-shaking extinction.

q: Which of the following is most responsible for the formation of the Great Lakes?
e: Enormous ancient glaciers crept across the land like heavy ice bulldozers, carving deep bowls that melted into the Great Lakes.

q: What was the African nation of Zimbabwe formerly known as?
e: Before choosing its proud African name, this sunny land of thundering waterfalls was called Rhodesia.

q: Which of the following best describes a carbon footprint?
a: A footprint that is left when someone steps on carbon
The emission of greenhouse gases caused by a product or individual
A monetary credit awarded to people who reduce their greenhouse gas emissions
A factor that does not merit consideration when buying energy efficient appliances
e: It is not a muddy shoe print, but the invisible trail of greenhouse gases you puff into the air whenever you use energy.

q: What's the first National Park designated in the United States?
e: Yellowstone became the very first national park in 1872, protecting bubbling geysers and wild bison for everyone to enjoy.

q: Black smokers are most likely to be found in association with what type of undersea geological site?
e: Deep underwater, where tectonic plates spread apart, these fiery chimneys puff out dark mineral water like busy underwater factories.

q: Which of the following is NOT one of the eight most common elements in the Earth's crust?
e: Even though carbon is in every living thing, rocks prefer elements like oxygen, leaving carbon off the crust's top-eight list.

q: Which of the following is believed to have led to the oxygenation of Earth's atmosphere approximately 2.4 billion years ago?
a: Increase in the photolysis [foh-TAWL-ih-sis] of water by UV radiation
e: Tiny ancient microbes learned to make food from sunlight and burped out fresh oxygen, transforming the whole planet's air forever!

q: Which of the following dinosaurs is NOT correctly matched with its description:
a: Hadrosaurus had a beak, web-feet, and a pelvis very similar to modern ducks
Brachiosaurus had tail spikes and bony plates along the length of its back
Tyrannosaurus rex was a large carnivorous dinosaur
e: Gentle giant Brachiosaurus had a super long neck for reaching treetops, not bony back plates; those belonged to spiky Stegosaurus!

q: Oceanographers use which of the following terms to describe global ocean circulation patterns?
e: Earth moves ocean water like a giant roller coaster, powered by heat and salt called the thermohaline conveyor.

q: Researchers at Oak Ridge National Lab are developing microbes that turn waste into the organic acid itaconic [IT-AH-CONIC] acid. Which of the following pH ranges best describes an aqueous solution of one-molar itaconic acid?
e: All acids sit below neutral seven on the pH scale, and this gentle acid lands safely between one and seven.

q: Which of the following is the BEST example of the chemical weathering of rock:
a: cracking of rock by plant roots
e: When rainwater trickles through limestone, it slowly dissolves the rock chemically, secretly carving out hollow underground caves.

q: The hard coral of coral reefs are primarily made of:
e: Tiny coral polyps build their cozy underwater castles using calcium carbonate, which turns as hard as limestone rock!

q: What is the official language of Bhutan?
e: High up in the peaceful mountain kingdom of Bhutan, people share stories using Dzongkha, their official language.

q: Which of the following is the general term for metamorphic rocks whose mineral crystals are oriented in parallel layers, such as in a high-grade metamorphic rock:
e: When underground pressure squishes rock minerals into neat, striped pages like a book, scientists call it foliated.

q: Which of the following is the most significant benefit of the Earth's magnetic field to life on Earth?
a: It deflects dangerous particles emitted by the sun
It is used by migrating birds to find their way
It is the source of our electric power
It helps us find mineral deposits
e: Earth's invisible magnetic bubble acts like a giant superhero shield, sweeping away harmful solar particles zooming from the sun.

q: Ethanol is being used as a way to reduce dependence on fossil fuels. Which of the following best describes the production of ethanol?
a: Distilling gases available in waste, such as methanol
Fermenting crops like corn and sugar cane
Using broken parts from cars as they get rusty
e: Hungry little yeasts gobble up sweet sugars from corn and sugarcane, fermenting them into plant-powered fuel called ethanol!

q: Which of the following is true of the Hawaiian chain of islands:
a: they show increasing age from the northwest to the southeast
they are thought to be the result of the lithosphere moving over a hot spot
they represent what could happen when plates interact at a convergent boundary
all the islands have approximately the same age
e: The Pacific plate slowly glides over a stationary hot spot of magma, creating islands one by one like fiery footprints.

q: In 1849, bones of a beluga whale were discovered in Vermont buried nearly 10 feet below the surface and over 150 miles from the nearest ocean. During which of the following time frames would the whale most likely have died?
e: When giant Ice Age glaciers melted eleven to twelve thousand years ago, the ocean flooded Vermont, letting a beluga swim far inland.

q: Which of the following processes happens at the slowest rate?
e: While ocean tides dance twice daily, mountains take millions of patient years to rise up toward the clouds.

q: Which of the following minerals, when examined at a molecular level, would appear to be a stack of loosely interacting sheets?
e: Muscovite is built like a shiny, fragile deck of cards, stacked in paper-thin sheets that peel right apart.

q: Which of the following typically occurs during El Nio?
a: Trade winds blow east to west along the equator
A band of warm water develops in the eastern Pacific
The Atlantic hurricane season is more severe
e: During El Niño, ocean winds slacken, allowing a giant blanket of warm bathwater to spread across the eastern Pacific.

q: Hurricane winds rotate in the opposite direction in the Southern Hemisphere due to:
a: The presence of less land in the Southern Hemisphere
e: Because Earth spins beneath the moving winds, the Coriolis effect steers storms in opposite directions across the equator.

q: The formation of a mirage in the desert is an example of?
e: Refraction happens when hot air bends sunbeams like bendy straws, tricking your eyes into seeing a shiny puddle of sky!

q: Seismic activity in the ocean may lead to what destructive phenomenon?
e: When the sea floor shakes in an earthquake, it shoves the ocean water above, unleashing giant waves called tsunamis!

q: Which of the following is closest to the maximum wavelength of an open ocean tsunami:
e: A tsunami wave is a stretched-out giant, with one watery crest rolling an incredible 125 miles ahead of the next!

q: Marble is a metamorphic rock that is often used for buildings and statues. What is the sedimentary rock that marble is commonly derived from?
e: Deep underground, cozy heat and squishing pressure bake crumbly limestone until it sparkles as polished, metamorphic marble.

q: What was the most populous city in the Americas in 2015?
e: São Paulo took the crown in 2015 because it was bursting with more bustling neighbors than any other city in the Americas.

q: Which of the following would be used on a weather map to indicate a cold day in winter with clear, blue skies:
e: A big capital H marks high pressure, which acts like a broom sweeping clouds away for crisp, sunny skies.

q: Which of the following is NOT typically true about fossils:
a: index fossils are not geographically widespread
fossilized marine animals have been found in the Himalayan Mountains
fossils found in tar pits are very well preserved
petrified wood is a type of fossil
e: Index fossils were famous globetrotters found all across the planet, so saying they are not widespread is totally wrong.

q: The land of Gotland is located in which European country?
e: Gotland is a sunny, medieval island floating in the Baltic Sea, and it belongs to Sweden.

q: A Beaufort number of 4 indicates:
a: a mineral similar in hardness to fluorite
e: A Beaufort four means a friendly moderate breeze is dancing by, gently rustling tree leaves and raising loose dust into the air.

q: The towns of Brugelette, Arlon and Ath are located in which country?
e: These charming, storybook towns are tucked away inside Belgium, surrounded by lush green hills and sweet chocolate shops.

q: What is the capital of Vietnam?
e: Full of ancient lakes and buzzing scooters, Hanoi is the lively heartbeat and capital city of Vietnam.

q: Which of the following is a carbonate mineral:
e: Dolomite is a carbonate mineral because its crystal family holds carbon and oxygen tightly together like best friends.

q: Which of the following is the most common group of rock-forming minerals:
e: Silicates are Earth's favorite building blocks, teaming up to make nearly all the tough rocks beneath our wandering feet.

q: What is the name of the type of concordant [kon-KOR-dent] igneous intrusion that splits apart two strata, pushing the overlying strata upwards in a dome-like structure, but has a generally horizontal base?
e: Bubbling magma squeezes between rock layers like a cheeky mushroom, puffing the roof upward into a dome called a laccolith.

q: The sedimentary layers of sandstones, shales, and limestones that make up the Grand Canyon and vast regions of the southwest United States were primarily deposited by which of the following?
e: Long ago, a shallow ocean blanketed the land, gently tucking in layers of sand and mud over millions of years.

q: Which of the following gases does NOT contribute significantly to the greenhouse effect?
e: Nitrogen fills most of our air, but it politely lets heat escape into space instead of trapping it.

q: Which of the following is when ocean tidal currents typically reach their maximum velocity:
a: midway between high and low tides
e: Midway between high and low tides, the ocean rushes fastest as water scrambles to fill or empty the shore!

q: The US state of New York has about as many inhabitants as?
e: With nearly twenty million people bustling about, New York holds almost the exact same crowd size as Romania.

q: Which of the following best represents why two igneous rocks may have the same minerals but different names?
e: Cooling fast or slow gives rocks different textures, turning the very same mineral recipe into completely different rocky cousins.

q: Which of the following are the first clearly identifiable fossils from the Precambrian Era which can still be found living along beaches of Shark Bay in western Australia:
e: Stromatolites are ancient, lumpy towers built by tiny microbes that have been happily sunbathing in Shark Bay for billions of years!

q: How many countries does Spain have a land border with?
e: Spain shares land borders with five different neighbors: Portugal, France, Andorra, tiny Gibraltar, and Morocco in North Africa.

q: All of the following countries have official claims to territory in Antartica EXCEPT:
e: The United States explores the frozen continent and builds chilly science stations, but never claimed any land for itself.

q: At any given moment, which of the following water resources holds the largest fraction of North America's freshwater?
e: Deep underground, hidden groundwater quietly holds way more freshwater than all our sparkling lakes and rushing rivers combined.

q: Surface bedrock in British Columbia often has long, parallel scratches called striations. Which of the following is most likely TRUE about these markings:
a: they were caused by seasonal freeze-thaw cycles
a glacier once moved in the direction of these scratches
a swift river once ran through these areas
the area was once a pluvial lake
e: A massive glacier once crept across the land like a giant icy sled, dragging rocks that scratched grooves in the direction it traveled!

q: What happened in 1815 to cause that year to be named "the year without a summer?"
a: a large meteor struck the Earth
there was a radical shift in the jet-stream southward
several large earthquakes occurred simultaneously around the globe
e: A giant volcano erupted and threw so much dusty ash into the sky that it blocked the warm sunshine for a whole year.

q: Which of the following most contributes to marine pollution?
e: Whenever it pours, busy rain washes land trash, dirt, and chemicals down rivers, making land runoff the ocean's biggest mess.

q: The Sonoran Desert is located in eastern Africa.
e: That is false. The cactus-filled Sonoran Desert actually basks in the warm sun of North America, not Africa.

q: Which of the following minerals will be a source of phosphate to the environment when it is weathered?
e: Apatite has a big appetite for feeding plants, crumbling under rain to share its rich supply of phosphate with the soil.

q: The hardness of a mineral determines how resistant it is to which of the following?
e: Hardness tells us how tough a mineral is when a pesky neighbor tries to scratch its shiny face.

q: The surface area of Russia is slightly larger than that of the dwarf planet Pluto.
e: It is true! Enormous Russia covers so much ground on Earth that it actually has a bit more surface area than little Pluto.

q: Stratovolcanoes are typically found in which of the following locations:
a: above hot spots in Earth's crust
e: These dramatic, cone-shaped peaks love company, popping up along continents and curved volcanic arcs where Earth's plates crunch together.

q: Igneous rocks that contain the last minerals to crystallize from magma, and consist mainly of sodium and potassium feldspars and quartz are said to have which of the following compositions?
e: Felsic rocks are the patient bakers of magma, cooling last to pack themselves full of light-colored quartz and feldspar.

q: Which of the following is NOT true about Earth's atmosphere:
a: carbon monoxide is found in trace amounts in Earth's atmosphere at sea level
nitrogen and oxygen make up nearly 99% of Earth's atmosphere at sea level
temperatures in parts of the stratosphere are nearly as warm as they are on Earth
the tropopause is lower at the equator than at the north pole
e: Warm air swells upward like baking bread near the equator, puffing the tropopause way higher there than at the chilly poles.

q: Coral reefs capture about half of all calcium flowing into the ocean every year by fixing it into:
e: Busy little corals capture floating calcium and weave it into hard calcium carbonate, building colorful underwater castles that protect the reef!

q: Which of the following is NOT the name of a river-sea interface?
e: A cenote is a secret underground sinkhole filled with freshwater, hiding inland rather than greeting the ocean like a river interface!

q: Which of the following best explains why the Mediterranean Sea is presently saltier than most marine bodies of water?
e: The thirsty sun slurps up Mediterranean water faster than clouds can rain it back, leaving an extra-salty sea behind.

q: What do the peaks and valleys in the Keeling curve represent?
a: Years of economic recession and reduced carbon emissions
Volcanic eruptions and offgassing from glacial melt
The seasonal variation of carbon uptake by land plants
e: That wavy curve shows our planet breathing, as hungry green leaves gobble up carbon each summer and rest each winter.

q: Olivine [AW-liv-een] belongs to what major mineral class?
e: This lovely green gem is built around silicon and oxygen, which happily tucks olivine right into the silicate family.

q: Radon, an element that causes lung cancer, may seep into homes and buildings and concentrate in re-circulated air. Which of the following best describes the source of most radon?
a: Chrysotile asbestos used for insulation releases radon when disturbed
Sulfuric acid in groundwater reacts with home building materials to produce radon
Garden pesticides release radon when reacting with home building materials
Uranium in surrounding rocks produces radon through radioactive decay
e: Ancient uranium resting inside underground rocks slowly breaks down, quietly releasing sneaky radon gas that creeps up toward our homes.

q: Which of the four major oceans is the shallowest, on average?
e: Cuddled beneath chilly polar ice, the cozy Arctic Ocean is the shallowest of all Earth's watery giants.

q: If the Earth's axis lost its tilt, which of the following would least likely occur?
a: Increased amount of seasonal changes across the planet
Cooler temperatures in winter and hotter temperatures in summer
Days and nights which are equal throughout the entire year across the planet
e: Without Earth's playful tilt, seasons pack up and leave, so winters never get colder and summers never get hotter!

q: Assuming all locations have similar weather conditions, at which of the following locations would you expect a barometer to yield the highest reading?
e: Key West sits right down at sea level, where a heavier blanket of air presses on the barometer.

q: Which of the following characteristics is most commonly associated with a tsunami wave as opposed to a normal ocean wave in the open ocean:
a: motion of only the uppermost layer of water
e: Out in the deep ocean, a sneaky tsunami stretches out so far that crest to crest can span three hundred miles!

q: Through what energy transfer process is ocean water below surface ice frozen?
e: Floating ice touches the water below, chilling it through conduction as heat quietly flows straight into the ice.

q: To which of the following is the ozone layer of Earth's upper atmosphere most opaque:
a: Most of the visible light spectrum.
e: High up in the sky, ozone acts like Earth's trusty sunglasses, blocking out harsh ultraviolet rays before they reach your skin.

q: A tropical storm will be declared a hurricane when:
a: it moves out of the tropics
there is evidence of eye formation and sustained wind speeds of 74 mph
e: A spinning storm earns its hurricane crown once it opens a calm eye and whips up fierce winds of seventy-four miles per hour!

q: Which of the following minerals has the highest density?
e: Platinum is the heavy champion here, packing more stuff into its tiny crystal spaces than any of the other minerals.

q: Which European city has the highest mileage of canals in the world?
e: Surprise, Birmingham actually beats Venice with more miles of winding, quiet canals flowing right through town!

q: Working in the field you encounter a series of fossil-rich sedimentary layers. You identify: paradoxides [para-DOX-ih-dees] trilobites, mucrospirifer [mah-kroh- SPEER-ih-fur] brachiopods [BRAK-ee-oh-pods], horn corals, and crinoids [CRY-noyds]. You recognize them as index fossils representing what era of geologic time?
e: These ancient shell-dwellers and swimming critters all threw a grand underwater party together during the ancient Paleozoic era!

q: According to the conveyor belt model of ocean circulation, which of the following happens when water reaches the poles?
a: The salinity of the water decreases
The density of the water increases
The density of the water decreases
The temperature of the water increases
e: Frigid polar winds chill the seawater until it packs tightly together, increasing its density so it can sink deep down.

q: Which of the following rock types would most likely be the best oil reservoir [REZ-er-vwohr]?
e: Sandstone acts like a giant stony sponge, full of cozy little pores where trapped oil can easily hide and flow.

q: Tsunamis, when seen in the deep ocean far from land, typically are about how much in amplitude?
e: Out in deep water, a giant tsunami hides as a gentle swell just one foot high before roaring near shore.

q: Which of the following is closest to the number of major and minor tectonic plates into which Earth's lithosphere is divided?
e: Earth wears its rocky crust like a cracked puzzle, gently shifting about fifteen big and medium pieces across our planet!

q: An increase in chlorine in the stratosphere is believed to be the cause of which of the following:
e: Greedy chlorine atoms gobble up protective ozone over chilly Antarctica, tearing a famous hole in our planet's sun shield.

q: What group of silicates is the most abundant group of minerals in Earth's crust?
e: Feldspars are the ultimate rock-building champions, making up more than half of the crust beneath your feet.

q: Colchester Overpass, otherwise known as "Bunny Man Bridge", is located where?
e: Deep in Fairfax County, Virginia, this spooky bridge sits nestled in the woods, wrapped in chilling old campfire tales.

q: It is the fate of all lakes and ponds on Earth to eventually become dry lands, bogs, marshes, or fens, through a process called:
e: When extra nutrients help plants take over a pond until it slowly fills up, that grand aging process is called eutrophication.

q: Which of the following is an area of high land, usually consisting of relatively flat terrain, sometimes formed by upwelling of volcanic magma, extrusion of lava, or erosion by water and glaciers?
e: Imagine a mountain that forgot its pointy peak and stayed flat on top; that high, scenic giant is a plateau!

q: Which of the following is the name for the hills made from glacial drift and deposited by meltwater from retreating glaciers?
e: Melting glaciers dump little mounds of gravel and sand like tidy backyard sandcastles, leaving behind hills called kames.

q: In the United States, where is spent nuclear fuel currently stored?
a: At a nuclear waste facility in Prairie Island, Minnesota
At a nuclear waste facility in Yucca Mountain, Nevada
At a nuclear waste facility in Waterford, Connecticut
In temporary storage at nuclear power plants around the country
e: Without one giant underground home ready yet, used fuel stays safely tucked away at local power plants all across the country.

q: Which of the following structures weakens rock, sometimes causing landslides?
e: A bedding plane is a slick seam between rock layers, making it easy for hillsides to slip and slide.

q: Which of the following degree measures is closest to the angle of repose of cinders in a cinder cone volcano?
e: Like a giant pile of sprinkles, loose volcanic rocks slide down until they settle happily at a thirty-degree tilt.

q: What accounts for the largest use of fresh water in the U.S. today?
e: Power plants work up quite a sweat making electricity, so they gulp down massive amounts of water to stay cool.

q: Which of the following is NOT an advantage of non-renewable energy sources?
e: Burning fossil fuels leaves messy puffs of smoky exhaust behind, which means low emissions is never on their list of perks.

q: Which of the following plates is NOT a past or present tectonic plate?
e: While true tectonic plates drift across the globe, Laurentian is actually an ancient continental core instead of a plate.

q: Which of the following types of tectonic plate boundary is NOT associated with magma formation?
e: At transform boundaries, giant slabs just grind sideways past each other like stubborn dancers, without melting any rock to brew magma.

q: What Texas city is nicknamed "The Yellow Rose of Texas"?
e: Since the Spanish word for yellow is amarillo, this breezy Texas town proudly wears its sweet rose nickname.

q: Scientists at Los Alamos National Lab are measuring the flux of charged particles entering Earth's upper atmosphere. Most of these charged particles come from which of the following?
e: Our sunny neighbor blows a constant, invisible breeze of charged particles across space called the solar wind.

q: Fossil fuel combustion in power plants creates heat. In order to run an electrical generator, heat is converted into what form of energy?
e: Hot steam acts like a playful shove, spinning giant turbine blades to turn heat into moving mechanical energy.

q: Most blizzards that strike the continental U.S. most directly originated in which of the following locations:
e: Chilly storm clouds brew over the icy waters of the Gulf of Alaska before swooping down to blanket towns in snow.

q: Looking at a weather map of the Northern Hemisphere, which of the following BEST describes the circulation of air around a low pressure system, designated with an "L":
a: a counterclockwise flow of air into the center
a counterclockwise flow of air out of the center
a clockwise flow of air into the center
a clockwise flow of air out of the center
e: Air rushes toward the center like water down a drain, twirling in a counterclockwise dance across the northern sky.

q: Why couldn't sailing explorers from Europe and Asia sail directly along the latitude that cuts across the middle of the North Atlantic or North Pacific to get to America?
a: Wind and water currents do not flow directly along the latitude that cuts across the middle of these oceans
Winds blow so hard near the middle of the ocean that it is impossible to maintain a straight course
Near the center of the oceans, the winds often blow in one direction, while the water currents flow in the opposite direction, making it difficult to traverse
The currents are so strong in the middle of the gyres that it is difficult to sail through them
e: Ocean breezes and rushing waters travel in big swirling loops, refusing to blow in a neat, straight line for patient sailors.

q: Which of the following is a volcano that is generally the smallest type, has very steep slopes, and would most likely result from a single violent eruption:
e: A cinder cone builds itself in one fiery sneeze, piling crumbly rocks into a steep little volcano.

q: Which of the following is the approximate percentage of silica in basaltic lava?
e: Basaltic lava is packed with about sixty percent silica, giving this dark, melted rock just enough goo to flow smoothly.

q: The greatest annual variation in the intensity of solar radiation on Earth throughout the year is in which of the following locations:
e: Middle latitude zones experience the biggest seasonal swings, dancing between bright, blazing summers and long, shadowy winters.

q: All of the following are towns/villages in the Pacific Island nation of Kiribati EXCEPT:
e: Kiribati famously named real villages London and Washington, but you will not find any town called Urutora there.

q: Which Canadian province has Charlottetown as its capital?
e: Charlottetown is the sweet seaside capital of Prince Edward Island, Canada's smallest and coziest province.

q: Which of the following is a stratovolcano?
e: Mount St. Helens is a classic stratovolcano, stacking steep layers of sticky lava and ash like a giant, grumpy mountain cake.

q: Which of the following best describes how stalagmites in caves are formed:
e: Dripping water dissolves cave stone and patiently rebuilds it mineral by mineral, using the quiet magic of chemical weathering.

q: Which of the following statements is NOT true about light pollution?
a: Using a short wavelength light at night minimizes the impact of artificial light
Some birds sing at unnatural hours in the presence of artificial light
It is caused by allowing artificial light to shine outward and upward into the sky at night, rather than focusing it downward
Brightly lit highways create nocturnal light levels that are as much as a million times brighter than normal, disorienting amphibians and other animals
e: Short wavelength blue light scatters easily and confuses sleepy wildlife, so it actually makes light pollution worse, not better!

q: Australia is greater than Greenland in size.
e: Maps can play funny tricks on our eyes, but massive Australia is actually over three times bigger than frosty Greenland!

q: Which of the following occurs at an ocean-continent convergent boundary?
a: Two tectonic plates move away from each other
Oceanic crust will subduct under continental crust
Continental crust will subduct under oceanic crust
Two tectonic plates slide past each other
e: Heavy ocean crust politely bows down, sliding under the lighter continent for a deep, warm nap inside the Earth.

q: Scientists at Oak Ridge National Lab are searching for enzymes that can break down lignin. Lignin is found in the highest quantities in what plant tissue?
e: Lignin acts like super-strong tree glue, packed tightly inside tough wood so mighty trees can stand tall against the wind.

q: Scientists at the DOE Ames Research Laboratory have been using advanced TEM to map nanocrystal magnetic fields formed in bacteria in liquids. What mineral is present in these bacteria?
e: Clever little bacteria build tiny compasses inside their bodies using magnetic bits of a mineral called magnetite.

q: Which of the following statements is NOT true regarding plate tectonics?
a: The Mid-Atlantic ridge is a divergent plate boundary
Convergent and transform boundaries are responsible for most major earthquakes
Approximately 75% of the world's volcanoes are associated with the circum-Pacific belt
The Juan de Fuca plate is diverging from the North American plate
e: The sneaky Juan de Fuca plate actually crashes under North America rather than pulling away, making that statement completely backwards!

q: Which of the following is most responsible for the change of seasons?
a: The distribution of continents and oceans
The elliptical shape of Earth's orbit
e: Our planet leans sideways like a spinning top, so different parts take turns soaking up the Sun's warm hugs all year long!

q: Without a greenhouse effect, what would be Earth's approximate average temperature in degrees Celsius?
e: Without cozy gases wrapping us like a blanket, our chilly world would freeze to a shivering minus eighteen degrees Celsius.

q: Which of the following does NOT increase ocean wave height?
a: Increased distance over which the wind blows the water
e: While howling winds whip up taller waves, a bumpy sea floor just scrambles water around instead of building giants.

q: The Burgess Shale in Canada is best known for providing scientists with fossils of which of the following?
e: These ancient Canadian rocks hide squishy, many-celled sea creatures that swam in oceans long before dinosaurs ever stomped around!

q: Marble is a metamorphic rock primarily composed of:
e: When limestone gets a super-hot underground squeeze, its tiny calcite crystals lock together to create shiny, smooth marble.

q: Which of the following does NOT affect weathering rates for a rock?
e: Rain, cracks, and the rock's own recipe decide how fast it crumbles, not the loose dirt sitting nearby.

q: What is the minimum number of seismic stations required to determine the epicenter of an earthquake?
e: You need three stations to draw overlapping circles on a map, pointing right to where the rumbling earthquake began.

q: What rock texture is characterized by broken fragments of older rocks?
e: Clastic rocks are nature's scrapbooks, packed with glued-together bits and broken pieces of older crumbled stones.

q: What is the capital of Belarus?
e: Minsk hums along as the bustling heart and capital of Belarus, keeping everything running smoothly.

q: Which of the following features is most likely to occur in deserts after heavy rainfall?
e: Ephemeral streams are surprise desert rivers that rush to life during sudden storms, then quickly vanish into thin air.

q: Both 30 north and 30 south latitude are characterized by zones of which of the following?
e: Heavy, cool air sinks down at these spots, pressing on the Earth to create sunny, dry high-pressure zones.

q: The following Spanish provinces are located in the northern area of Spain except:
e: While the others stay up north, Murcia prefers baking down under the warm sun in Spain's south!

q: Which of the following processes is responsible for generating most of the heat that powers Io's [EYE-ohs] volcanism?
e: Giant Jupiter squeezes moon Io with tidal forces like a rubber ball, creating fiery friction that fuels wild volcanoes!

q: Which of the following minerals is present in the highest concentrations in granite?
e: Sparkly quartz crystals pack tightly together, making up the biggest and toughest part of that speckled granite rock.

q: Which of the following best describes the watershed of the Mississippi River?
a: The land west of the Rocky Mountains
The land between the Rocky and Appalachian Mountains
The land between the Sierra Nevada and Rocky Mountains
The land east of the Appalachian Mountains
e: This giant river basin scoops up raindrops falling across the huge valley between the Rocky and Appalachian mountains.

q: The climate of northwestern Europe is most directly affected by the:
e: Think of the Gulf Stream as a giant, cozy river in the ocean, carrying warm tropical water to keep Europe snug and comfortable.

q: What is the ratio of iron to oxygen in the mineral hematite?
e: Inside this shiny red rock, every two iron atoms happily pair up with three oxygen atoms to make the mineral hematite.

q: Karst topography refers to landscapes that have been shaped by what agent of erosion?
e: Water acts like a patient sculptor, quietly nibbling away underground limestone to carve out the secret caves and sinkholes of karst landscapes.

q: Gothenburg is the capital of Sweden.
e: Gothenburg is a lovely harbor town, but grand Stockholm is the true capital wearing Sweden's crown.

q: The Saffir-Simpson Scale is used to classify intensities of:
e: The Saffir-Simpson scale measures the fierce winds of giant, swirling ocean storms called hurricanes to see how powerful they are.

q: Which of the following is a good way to prevent erosion?
e: Carving hills into giant flat steps keeps rainwater from rushing down, holding precious soil safely in place.

q: Which of the following bodies does NOT have an atmosphere composed predominantly of nitrogen?
e: Venus wraps itself in a thick blanket of heavy carbon dioxide rather than nitrogen, baking the rocky planet like an oven!

q: The longest place named in the United States is Lake Chargoggagoggmanchauggagoggchaubunagungamaugg, located near Webster, MA.
e: It sounds like a happy sneeze, but that whopping forty-five-letter lake in Massachusetts really holds the record for America's longest name!

q: All except which of the following indicate that glaciers modified a landscape?
a: Artes (read as: ah-RATES), cirques, and horns
e: Glaciers carve and scrape the surface like frozen bulldozers, but deep underground tectonic forces are what slowly squish and fold solid rock.

q: Scientists at Oak Ridge National Lab are studying nightshades. Which of the following chemicals is a characteristic product of certain nightshades?
e: Capsaicin is the fiery chemical hiding inside nightshade peppers that gives them their spicy kick and makes your tongue tingle!

q: Which of the following is a coarse-grained clastic rock that contains angular fragments?
e: Breccia is a rocky puzzle made of sharp, jagged fragments glued together before wind or water had time to smooth them down.

q: What is the capital of Cyprus?
e: Nicosia sits right in the sunny heart of the island, proudly leading the country as its capital.

q: In which of the geological time periods, did dinosaurs first appear:
e: Long before huge giants ruled the Earth, the very first dinosaurs tiptoed into the world during the Triassic period to start their grand adventure.

q: How many sovereign states are members of the United Nations?
e: The United Nations brings together 195 sovereign states, giving nearly every corner of our wonderful world a seat at the table!

q: Which of the following is the streak color of the mineral fluorite?
e: Fluorite can wear colorful purple or green coats, but scratching it reveals its true, secret identity: snowy white powder.

q: Which of the following minerals can create metamorphic structures known as snowball structures?
e: As shifting rocks twist and squeeze deep below, growing garnet crystals can roll like tiny dough balls, wrapping layers around themselves like little snowballs.

q: Which of the following is a high-grade foliated metamorphic rock:
e: Deep underground, wild heat and pressure squish rock until its minerals line up in bold zebra stripes, baking it into tough gneiss.

q: What is the capital of the US state Nevada?
e: Las Vegas has the dazzling neon lights, but historic little Carson City proudly wears the crown as Nevada's true capital.

q: Which of the following best describes the epicenters of earthquakes associated with mid-ocean ridge spreading centers?
e: Because the sea floor is thin and pulling apart right near the surface, earthquakes along mid-ocean ridges only rumble from shallow depths.

q: Approximately what fraction of Earth's surface is covered by oceans:
e: If you look down at our blue home from space, watery oceans cover seven-tenths of the globe, leaving just a splash of dry land.

q: Which of the following would be affected the least by the Coriolis effect?
a: Direction for a wind blowing from the north
e: Earth's big spin barely notices a tornado because this spunky twister is just too tiny and quick to be pushed!

q: What is the name of the former country that was succeeded by countries such as Serbia, Croatia and Slovenia?
e: Yugoslavia once held all those different places together under one cozy roof before it divided into countries like Serbia and Croatia.

q: Which of the following is closest to the average percent salinity of ocean water?
e: If you scooped up one hundred drops of ocean water, about three and a half drops would be pure salt!

q: Exposed Precambrian crystalline igneous and metamorphic rocks that form tectonically stable areas are which type of geologic province?
e: Like trusty armor, a shield is made of ancient, tough rocks that quietly hold continents steady without rumbling.

q: The Earth's inner core accounts for approximately what percentage of the Earth's total mass?
e: Earth's solid iron heart is surprisingly tiny, making up just two percent of our planet's giant total weight.

q: The inshore marine environment, from the surface to the sea floor, where water depths do not exceed 200 meters, is known as which of the following?
e: The neritic zone hugs the coast down to two hundred meters, creating a sunny, bustling playground for sea creatures.

q: Which is the world's longest river?
e: The sunny Nile River twists through Africa for thousands of miles, stretching farther than any other river on Earth.

q: Consider ocean water underlying sea ice with cold air above the sea ice. The rate at which heat flows out of ocean water is which of the following?
a: Directly proportional to the temperature difference between the air and the water
Directly proportional to the thickness of the ice layer
Constant once ocean water reaches -5 Celsius
Increased by the snow cover on top of the ice
e: Heat rushes out of the water much faster when there is a bigger temperature difference with the freezing air.

q: Which of the following sites is famous for its diversity of Pleistocene [PLY-stuh-seen] fossils?
e: The sticky La Brea Tar Pits trapped ancient Ice Age creatures, saving their Pleistocene fossils in a gooey time capsule!

q: What is the name for the model that describes the opening and closing of ocean basins?
e: The Wilson cycle is Earth's grand dance where oceans slowly stretch open and squeeze shut over millions of years.

q: Which of the following statements is NOT true about the Novarupa eruption of 1912?
a: It became the most powerful volcanic eruption of the 20th century
It created the world's most extensive ignimbrite [IG-nim-bryt]
e: Novarupta was a sneaky surprise! It burst from its own brand-new vent, even though nearby Mount Katmai got blamed when its peak collapsed.

q: High salinities, high oxygen, low silica, and near-freezing temperatures allow seawater to sink, driving global circulation. In which of the following seas would you expect to find this occurring?
e: Antarctica's icy Weddell Sea is so freezing and salty that its heavy water sinks to power deep ocean currents.

q: What is the approximate salinity of the ocean in parts per thousand?
e: If you scooped up a thousand drops of ocean water, about thirty-five of them would be pure, tasty salt.

q: What is the capital of the State of Washington, United States?
e: Seattle has the giant Space Needle, but lovely Olympia is the one wearing the crown as Washington's state capital.

q: Which of the following is a sedimentary rock made of microscopic fossil marine shells?
e: That soft classroom chalk is made from billions of tiny, ancient seashell skeletons squished together on the seafloor.

q: Which of the following is NOT a common mafic silicate mineral?
e: Potassium feldspar is a light-colored mineral, so it skips the dark, heavy mafic family party.

q: Compressive forces dominate which of the following tectonic plate boundaries?
e: The Arabian and Eurasian plates march toward each other, squeezing and crumpling the land in a giant rocky hug.

q: How many provinces are in the Netherlands?
e: The Netherlands bundles its tulip fields, windmills, and bicycle trails into twelve tidy provinces.

q: If you walked the full extent of each of the following lines, which would be the shortest in length?
e: Latitude loops shrink as you head toward the poles, making forty-five degrees North a much shorter walk around Earth.

q: What water cycle process causes water molecules to move from a lake and into the atmosphere?
e: Warm sunshine hugs the lake water, turning puddles into invisible vapor that floats upward through evaporation.

q: In a residence, how are appliances generally connected to the power supply?
a: In a delta to wye connection
In a wye to delta connection
e: Homes use parallel wiring so your toaster gets its own little electrical path, letting you turn off lamps without shutting down the fridge.

q: Which of the following phenomena is NOT related to burning fossil fuels?
e: Smokestacks pollute the sky, but Earth's deep magnetic poles flip because of churning molten metal inside our planet, not smoke.

q: The Intertropical Convergence Zone is the area encirling the Earth near the equator where the northeast and southeast trade winds come together. This area was known to sailors as which of the following?
e: Sailors called this sleepy zone the doldrums because the winds take a nap, leaving ships stuck floating under the tropical sun.

q: Which of the following best describes what drives plate tectonics?
a: Energy from the Sun driving ocean currents and plates
Heat from the Earth's interior driving convection in the mantle
Scientists have not yet developed a robust theory but some leading researchers are linking it to ocean currents
Earthquakes drive plate tectonics, volcanism, and global wind systems
e: Deep down, Earth's scorching heat swirls thick mantle rock like a bubbly pot of soup, carrying giant puzzle-piece continents across the globe!

q: Which of the following locations contains relatively young coasts that formed as a consequence of continental rifting:
a: southern coasts of the Aleutian Islands
e: The Gulf of California formed when land tore apart like a giant zipper, opening up brand-new coasts along the rip.

q: Brookhaven National Lab scientists are studying how sunlight can cause trace gases in the atmosphere to form aerosol particles, which can then seed the formation of clouds. What is the term for these particles?
e: Floating speckles called condensation nuclei act like cozy tiny chairs for water droplets to gather on and build fluffy clouds.

q: Fuel cells work in which of the following ways?
a: By converting chemical energy into electrical energy
By processing plant matter to generate electricity
By converting thermal energy into electrical energy
By using fossil fuels to generate mechanical energy
e: Fuel cells quietly transform stored chemical energy right into buzzing electricity, like a neat little power-making magic trick.

q: Which of the following statements is NOT true about radon?
a: Radon comes from the natural decay of radium that is found in nearly all rocks and soils
Radon migrates into homes through openings in floors and walls
Radon is the second leading cause of lung cancer in the United States
Radon exposure is greatest in homes with basements
e: Sneaky radon gas slips through cracks from the ground below, so any home can trap it, not just ones with cozy basements.

q: Barrages with built in sluices are used to harvest energy from what source?
e: Giant sea gates catch rushing ocean tides like huge revolving doors, capturing the water's natural dance to spin turbines for clean power.

q: The part of a sea, lake, or river that is close to the shore is called which of the following?
e: The sunny littoral zone hugs the shore, where light touches bottom and playful minnows weave through shallow green reeds.

q: A caldera is:
a: a huge depression formed after a magma chamber collapses
a long tube where magma pours out onto the surface
a lateral vent that spews only gases
e: After a volcano blasts out its magma, the empty ground caves in, leaving behind a giant bowl called a caldera.

q: The Pyrenees mountains are located on the border of which two countries?
e: The snowy Pyrenees stand tall like giant stone guards, neatly separating sunny Spain from its neighbor, France.

q: The energy in a thunderstorm comes from which of the following?
a: Condensation of water drops that form the cloud
Electrical energy from charged particles in the cloud
e: When floating water vapor huddles into liquid raindrops, it happily releases hidden heat that powers up the mighty storm.

q: What is the term for a contour line connecting points of equal temperature on a weather map?
e: Weather maps use isotherms as cozy ribbons, gently connecting everywhere that shares the exact same toasty or chilly temperature.

q: In what geologic era did dinosaurs live?
e: Dinosaurs spent their entire grand adventure stomping across Earth inside the Mesozoic era, the famous age of reptiles.

q: Which country ranks first in the number of historically active volcanoes?
e: Indonesia is like a fiery playground, bubbling with more active volcanoes than any other country on Earth.

q: Which of the following geological terms best refers to deposits of unsorted and unstratified sediments deposited by the movement of a glacier:
e: When a glacier melts, it dumps a jumbled, unsorted heap of rocks and dirt called till, just like an untidy toy box.

q: Which of the following geologic structures forms from sediment deposited at the mouth of a river?
e: As a wandering river slows into the sea, it drops its sandy luggage to build a fan-shaped wonderland called a delta.

q: In which of the following are the term and its description accurately matched?
a: Rockfalls - large blocks of bedrock break off a cliff face and tumble downslope
Earthslides - heavy rainfall saturates the soil, which under the extra weight breaks loose and becomes a slurry that takes everything with it
Slumps - masses of soil moving down a slip face, usually the top of the bedrock
Debris flows - the rotation of a cohesive unit of soil or rock down a slip surface
e: Rockfalls happen when heavy boulders lose their grip on a cliff and go tumbling down the mountain slope.

q: Which of the following is a layer of the Earth that is primarily characterized as rock with the properties of being hot, weak and plastic:
e: The squishy asthenosphere is so hot and soft that solid rock bends like warm silly putty right beneath our feet.

q: Which of the following is NOT true about earthquakes:
a: the focus of an earthquake is the point from which energy is released
the epicenter is the point on Earth's surface directly above the focus
lithospheric plate interactions commonly cause both earthquakes and volcanoes
primary seismic waves cause the most damage to buildings during an earthquake
e: Speedy primary waves arrive first with a tiny shake, but the slower, rolling surface waves actually cause the big building damage.

q: Which of the following best describes how volcanic glass or obsidian is formed:
a: magma cools rapidly and crystals do not form
magma cools slowly and 1 large crystal is formed
magma cools in direct contact with water
magma is heated, cooled, then reheated
e: When hot lava chills in a super-fast flash, it freezes before tiny crystals have any time to grow.

q: The early atmosphere of the Earth probably was rich in all EXCEPT which of the following gases?
e: Long ago, baby Earth was burping volcanic gases, but plant helpers had not made fresh, breathable oxygen yet.

q: Which of the following is a feature made by a continental glacier and NOT made by an alpine glacier:
e: Giant ice sheets act like rolling pins across flat land, smoothing out teardrop hills called drumlins that mountain glaciers never make.

q: In which English county is Stonehenge?
e: Those mysterious, giant standing stones keep their ancient secrets tucked safely inside the rolling green hills of Wiltshire.

q: The weather phenomenon that consists of weakened tradewinds that allow surface water from the western Pacific to move eastward, causing a sinking thermocline, is known as El Nio. This process leads to which of the following along coastal South America?
a: Colder sea surface temperatures and more precipitation
Colder sea surface temperatures and less precipitation
Warmer sea surface temperatures and more precipitation
Warmer sea surface temperatures and less precipitation
e: Warm ocean water slides eastward, heating up South America's coast and brewing up cozy, rain-filled clouds.

q: Which of the following is NOT true about ocean water:
a: cool, salty water is more dense that warm, less salty water
about 97% of Earth's surface water is salt water
about 3.5% of sea water consists of dissolved substances
the proportions of dissolved gases in the ocean are nearly the same as in the atmosphere
e: The ocean loves sipping up carbon dioxide, so its underwater gas recipe is completely different from the air we breathe.

q: How many states are in Australia?
e: Australia shares its giant island among six sunny states, leaving the rest to its wild territories and hopping kangaroos.

q: Which of the following is the most widely used form of renewable energy worldwide?
e: Rushing river water spins mighty turbines day and night, making trusty hydropower the reigning champion of clean energy around the world.

q: According to the Richter scale, which of the following is closest to the ratio of the energy released in a magnitude 10 earthquake to that released in a magnitude 8 earthquake?
e: Every step up multiplies the rumble by thirty-two, so leaping two whole numbers unleashes a whopping thousand times more energy.

q: What is the official national language of Pakistan?
e: Urdu weaves beautiful words together, serving as the proud national language that brings the people of Pakistan together.

q: Which of the following is NOT true about minerals:
a: cinnabar is the most important mercury ore mineral
pyrite is a common sulfide mineral
galena is the most important ore of lead
granite is a widespread mineral used in cement
e: Granite is actually a rock, which means it is a cozy team of different mineral buddies huddled together, not just one.

q: Which of the following best describes the magnetic field lines around a current-carrying wire?
a: Rings encircling about the core of the wire
Radial lines pointing outward from the wire
Radial lines pointing inward toward the wire
Loops connecting the top of the wire to the bottom of the wire
e: When electricity zooms through a wire, invisible magnetic fields hug it tightly in spinning, circular rings like hula hoops.

q: Which of the following is closest to average barometric pressure at sea level, in inches:
e: Earth's cozy air blanket presses down at sea level with enough gentle weight to lift mercury up to 29.92 inches.

q: The formerly East-Prussian city of Königsberg is known as which Russian City today?
e: After history reshuffled the map, the old seaside city was renamed Kaliningrad and became part of Russia.

q: Which of the following is considered a living fossil because, although fossils of it have been dated to 360 million years ago, these arthropods are still alive today:
e: Tough horseshoe crabs have scuttled across beaches wearing the same helmet shells for hundreds of millions of years!

q: Which of the following geologic intervals went from 2.6 million years ago to approximately 12,000 years ago, and is commonly referred to as the Ice Age?
e: Back during the chilly Pleistocene, giant mammoths wandered across massive sheets of ice during our world's famous Ice Age.

q: The greenhouse effect is produced primarily by the re-emission of which of the following by the atmosphere:
e: Our warm Earth gently breathes out invisible infrared heat, which atmospheric gases hug tight to keep our world cozy.

q: Which of these Japanese islands is the largest by area?
e: Shikoku is one of Japan's four mighty main islands, making it vastly bigger than those other tiny specks.

q: In which English county is the city of Portsmouth?
e: Portsmouth docks its busy ships right along the breezy southern coast of Hampshire.

q: Diatoms within sea ice are responsible for as much as 10% of the carbon dioxide fixation in the Southern Ocean. During which of the following months would you expect the organic carbon content of the sea ice to be highest?
e: December brings the sunny Antarctic summer, waking up hungry little diatoms to soak up light and pack the sea ice with carbon.

q: Piedmont glaciers, such as the Wilson-Piedmont glacier in Murdo Sound, Antarctica, are defined by which of the following characteristics?
a: They are older than other glacier types
They spread broadly into flat valleys
e: When icy mountain glaciers reach flat land, they love to stretch out wide like pancake batter pooling in a cozy valley.

q: The Japanese district Akihabara is also known by what nickname?
e: Akihabara earned the name Electric Town because its streets glow with thousands of buzzing gadgets, bright lights, and video games.

q: Hydraulic fracturing is used to release natural gas and oil from what type of geological formation?
