e: Water cracks open tight, muddy shale rock to set free the sneaky bubbles of oil and gas trapped inside.

q: Which of the following is NOT associated with active margins?
e: Plate edges crash and shake together, but hot spot volcanoes are lone rangers that bubble up far away in the peaceful middle.

q: What are the four corner states of the US?
e: Utah, Colorado, Arizona, and New Mexico touch corners like puzzle pieces, letting you stand in four states at once.

q: Which of the following statements best describes the importance of composting?
a: It is necessary for the growth of fruits and vegetables
It helps to prevent air pollution
It puts organic material back in the ground
It prevents the decomposition of organic material
e: Old banana peels and crunchy leaves break down, happily returning their rich nutrients right back into the welcoming soil.

q: Researchers at the National Energy Technology Lab are developing membranes that absorb carbon dioxide. Which of the following terms most accurately describes dissimilar molecules sticking to one another?
e: Adhesion is the friendly magic that lets two totally different molecules stick together like curious best friends!

q: The White Cliffs of Dover is located in which country?
e: These giant, chalky-white walls stand like snowy castle gates greeting travelers along the coast of the United Kingdom.

q: What is the name of the ductile [DUK-til] region of Earth's mantle that is solid but is so mechanically weak that it can flow?
e: Deep down, the asthenosphere is solid rock that stays so warm and squishy it can slowly crawl like warm silly putty.

q: Which of the following mass movement events occurs when rock layers fall down-slope along weak bedding planes?
e: When weak underground rock layers give way like a tilted playground slide, huge slabs tumble down in a sudden rockslide.

q: What is the primary reason for the movement of mass downslope during erosion?
e: Gravity is the invisible giant tugging on loose rocks, gently rolling them all tumbling down the hillside.

q: What layer of the Earth lies directly beneath the tectonic plates?
e: Giant tectonic plates glide smoothly across the asthenosphere, a soft, squishy layer of warm rock resting right beneath them.

q: Which of the following is NOT a type of fine-grained igneous rock?
e: Peridotite cools down super slowly deep underground, giving its crystals plenty of time to grow big and chunky instead of fine-grained.

q: Which of the following BEST describes earthquake aftershocks:
a: all tremors under magnitude 4 on the Richter scale
a series of smaller tremors that follow a large earthquake within days or weeks
any tremors that originate from the epicenter within a 1 year period
the tremor that occurs at the initial point of rupture
e: After a giant quake roars, the ground settles down with little rumbling hiccups over the next few days or weeks.

q: The region of the atmosphere closest to the Earth's surface is the:
e: The troposphere hugs Earth right where we breathe, tucking us in with fluffy clouds and swirling weather.

q: Which of the following is considered a non-renewable resource?
e: Uranium took billions of years to bake inside Earth, so once we use it up, it is gone for good.

q: The historical city Timbuktu is located in which West African country?
e: Timbuktu rests in Mali, where golden desert sands once welcomed ancient book lovers and camel caravans from afar.

q: The hard rock under the topsoil in eastern Washington state was laid down over millions of years by volcanic eruptions. This rock is:
e: Millions of years ago, glowing rivers of lava cooled and hardened into tough, dark basalt rock resting under the soil.

q: When the Earth's interior finally cools, which of the following will stop?
e: Our continents only drift because Earth has a warm, churning belly, so losing that inner heat stops plate tectonics in its tracks.

q: In which of the following rock types are you most likely to find cross-bedding?
e: Long ago, playful desert winds danced across sandy dunes, stacking tilted stripes that hardened into sandstone over millions of years.

q: What is the largest Muslim country in the world?
e: Spread across thousands of sunny tropical islands, Indonesia is home to the world's largest Muslim family of believers.

q: The ultimate energy source for geothermal energy is which of the following?
a: Radioactive decay of elements in the Earth's interior
Gravitational contraction of the Earth's interior
Leftover thermal energy from the formation of the Earth's interior
Energy from earthquakes in the Earth's interior
e: Deep underground, restless radioactive elements slowly decay and release heat, keeping our home planet toasty from the inside out.

q: Scientists at Oak Ridge National Lab are using X-ray diffraction to understand the structure of enzymes that pump antibiotics out of bacteria. Which of the following is TRUE of these enzymes?
a: They have become more widespread in response to antibiotic therapy
e: Clever bacteria learned to build tiny pumps that spit medicine right out, and using antibiotics caused these pumps to spread everywhere.

q: Russia shares a land border with North Korea.
e: Believe it or not, giant Russia and North Korea actually touch along a tiny border near the coast!

q: Index fossils are most useful for which of the following reasons?
a: They lived during only one short period of time
They provide high resolution carbon isotope-based date ranges
They are not prone to weathering
e: These special critters only visited Earth for a brief flash of time, making their fossils perfect bookmarks for dating rock layers.

q: Metamorphism transforms limestone into a metamorphic rock called:
e: Deep underground, the Earth gives ordinary limestone a hot, squishy hug until it bakes into smooth, sparkling marble!

q: Why do hurricanes NOT occur at the equator?
a: There is not enough land mass
The Coriolis effect is too weak
e: Mighty storms need Earth's spin to start twirling, but right at the equator, that Coriolis spin is far too weak to dance.

q: Which is the largest city in Morocco?
e: Casablanca is Morocco's grand champion of size, bustling with more busy markets and seaside homes than any other city there.

q: Which of the following is NOT prevalent at mid-ocean ridges:
e: As ocean floors gently pull apart, rocks only snap near the warm surface, so you will never find deep, shaking earthquakes here.

q: If cumulus mammatus clouds are heading in your direction, you may soon experience:
e: When strange, bubbly pouches droop from the sky, a stormy cloud is brewing up heavy rain, hail, and severe weather!

q: DOE researchers at the Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory used the Advanced Light Source to perform X-ray diffraction on a mineral grain that was 10 microns in diameter, to determine its chemical makeup. This mineral grain's size is closest to which of the following?
e: A single tiny micron holds one million picometers inside, meaning our ten-micron speck easily stretches to ten million picometers.

q: Which of the following minerals has the same chemical composition as glass?
e: Nature makes quartz from the exact same sparkling recipe of silicon and oxygen that we melt to create glass.

q: The Himalayas are an example of which of the following kinds of mountain systems?
e: Giant tectonic plates crashed in slow motion, crumpling Earth's crust into the majestic folded mountains we call the Himalayas.

q: Which of the following statements is true about primary producers in the ocean?
a: They are responsible for bringing energy from the physical world into the biological world
They are found primarily in tropical coral reef environments in equatorial waters
They are also referred to as primary consumers in an ecosystem model
They include sharks and large bony fishes
e: Tiny ocean plants catch bright sunbeams, turning pure sunshine into tasty food so physical energy can enter the living world.

q: On which continent/s is the entire country of Spain specifically located when taking into account all of its territory?
e: Most of Spain lounges in Europe, but two of its tiny sunny cities actually sit across the sea in Africa.

q: The Paleocene-Eocene [PAY-lee- uh-seen EE-uh- seen] Thermal Maximum (PETM) was an event marked by major changes on Earth that occurred about 55 million years ago. Which of the following is NOT true of the PETM?
a: Carbonate deposits in the world's oceans dissolved
Greenhouse gases such as CO2 were much lower
Deep-sea extinctions of marine organisms occurred
e: Earth got super toasty during this giant heatwave because greenhouse gases shot way up, making it false that carbon dioxide was lower.

q: What is the capital of Estonia?
e: Tallinn is Estonia's fairy-tale capital, complete with ancient stone towers, winding cobblestone streets, and cozy charm.

q: In the 2016 Global Peace Index poll, out of 163 countries, what was the United States of America ranked?
e: With conflicts abroad and worries at home, the United States landed at spot 103 on that peaceful list.

q: The geologic time scale is divided into eons, eras, periods, epochs [EH-puks], and ages. Which of the following best describes how geologic time is divided in the Phanerozoic Eon?
a: Divisions are based on time periods of equal length
Divisions are based on evidence of paleoclimates
Divisions are based on domination by groups of major fauna
Divisions are based on domination by major rock types
e: Geologists slice this time chapter by chapter based on which ruling animal families, from dinosaurs to mammals, dominated the planet.

q: The ocean crust is composed mostly of which of the following rock types?
e: Way down beneath the deep blue sea, cooled volcanic lava builds a heavy, dark blanket of basalt rock.

q: Which of the following sedimentary structures is caused by drying of soft sediments?
e: When wet, squishy mud sits baking in the sun, it shrinks and splits into puzzle-piece mudcracks.

q: Bikini Atoll is in which country?
e: This sunny ring of coral snoozes peacefully among the Marshall Islands out in the deep blue ocean.

q: Which of the following is a greenhouse gas that primarily comes from landfills, coal mines, oil and natural gas operations, and agriculture:
e: Burping cows and heaps of trash release invisible methane gas, which traps extra heat around Earth.

q: What latitude receives the most direct sunlight during the December solstice?
e: In chilly December, our tilted Earth points 23.5 degrees South straight toward the sun for maximum sunshine.

q: Extremely coarse grained igneous rocks, with minerals larger than 1 inch, are evidence of which of the following?
a: Volcanic rocks with previously formed crystals
Volcanic rocks cooled rapidly along ocean floor fissures
Magma cooling with high volatile content
Magma cooling quickly to form aplite
e: Trapped bubbly gases let minerals zip around cooling magma, helping them grow into giant crystal wonders.

q: Which of the following dominates the gasses in the Earth's atmosphere, making up some 78% of the air by volume:
e: While we love breathing oxygen, quiet nitrogen is the true heavyweight, filling nearly four-fifths of our wonderful sky.

q: Which of the following sources accounts for the largest fraction of consumed renewable energy in the US?
e: Energy from plants and wood, called biomass, leads the renewable pack by turning nature's leftovers into power.

q: Which of the following ocean life zones contains the least variety of ocean life?
e: In the freezing, sunless abyssal zone, food is so scarce that very few kinds of sea creatures can survive there.

q: Which of the following types of rock would have the greatest permeability?
e: Sandstone is packed with open spaces between sand grains, letting water easily flow right through it.

q: Which of the following most likely formed a U-shaped valley:
e: A creeping glacier acts like a giant ice scoop, carving sharp mountain valleys into wide, gentle U-shapes.

q: Which of the following is a human-made gas that, if released into the atmosphere, can directly act to destroy ozone in the stratosphere:
e: Sneaky human-made chlorofluorocarbons float high into the sky, gobbling up our planet's sunscreen called ozone.

q: How tall is One World Trade Center in New York City?
e: The mighty tower climbs to exactly 1,776 feet to celebrate the year America signed its Declaration of Independence.

q: A long stretch of beach is east facing with a southerly longshore current. The construction of an artificial groin will lead to which of the following?
a: Increased erosion on both sides of the groin
Loss of beach south of the groin
Sand bar formation south of the groin
Change in the direction of the longshore current
e: The wall traps southward-drifting sand, leaving the beach just south of it hungry and losing its sandy blanket.

q: What is the term for a water-bearing layer of permeable, undergound rock?
e: Deep below your feet, a giant rocky sponge called an aquifer happily holds underground water.

q: What is the decibel scale most often used to measure?
e: From a tiny mouse whisper to a roaring rocket, decibels measure just how loud sounds are.

q: Broome is a town in which state of Australia?
e: Broome sparkles on the sandy sunset shores of Western Australia, famous for pretty pearls and red rocks.

q: In the U.S., where is most high-level nuclear waste presently stored?
e: Instead of traveling far away, most nuclear waste stays tucked safely on-site at the power plants.

q: What is the capital city of Slovenia?
e: Slovenia's charming capital is Ljubljana, a fairy-tale city guarded by friendly green dragon statues.

q: The general paths of storm systems that travel across the continental United States are primarily driven by:
e: High in the sky, a speedy river of air called the jet stream pushes swirling storms across the country.

q: Scientists at Oak Ridge National Lab are part of a collaboration to study quark-gluon plasma. Which of the following statements is true of gluons?
e: Gluons are bosons, acting like tiny messengers that hug quarks together with the strongest force in nature!

q: Which of the following is NOT true about carbon dioxide?
a: It has been present in Earth's atmosphere for billions of years
The present amount of carbon dioxide in our atmosphere is completely due to natural causes
Increased emissions of carbon dioxide from human industrial activities are causing global climate change
On Earth, it is emitted by humans, most other animals and plants
e: Nature breathes out carbon dioxide, but our factories and cars add a huge extra blanket of it, so it is not completely natural!

q: Which of the following natural disasters is NOT commonly caused by the movement of tectonic plates?
e: While restless plates shake the ground below, hurricanes get their wild, swirling energy high above from warm ocean air instead.

q: Seoul is the capital of North Korea.
e: Seoul actually shines brightly as the capital of South Korea, while Pyongyang leads the north.

q: Which of the following mineral properties can be unreliable?
e: Color loves playing dress-up, so a sneaky pinch of impurities can easily trick you by turning the same mineral purple, green, or clear!

q: The capital of the US State Ohio is the city of Chillicothe.
e: Chillicothe had a turn long ago, but bustling Columbus wears the crown as Ohio's capital today.

q: Scientists at SLAC [slack] National Accelerator Lab determined the coat color of a mouse fossil via x-ray fluorescence imaging. The organic pigments in the fossil have long since degraded, so they inferred the distribution of pigments by observing the distribution of what entities that are chelated [KEE-lated] by the pigments?
e: The fossil's colors vanished long ago, but stubborn metal ions stayed trapped in place, revealing the ancient mouse's colorful patterns.

q: Which of the following terms best describes the cleavage of a mineral:
e: Some tidy minerals split along a single, mirror-flat sheet like a deck of cards, giving them perfect one way cleavage!

q: Knowing that the growth of lava domes is generally nonexplosive and they often grow for many months to years, which of the following best describes their magmas:
a: low viscosity and low gas content
low viscosity and high gas content
high viscosity and low gas content
high viscosity and high gas content
e: This gooey lava creeps along like thick, sticky peanut butter, quietly piling up because it has very little trapped gas to pop it!

q: Which of the following statements is NOT true about hurricanes?
a: They are intense low pressure areas
They gradually die as they move over warmer waters
They have warm air in their eyes
They generally form in the summer and early fall
e: Warm ocean water is actually a hurricane's favorite snack, making it grow bigger and stronger instead of fading away.

q: Which of the following layers within the Earth is undergoing convection?
e: Deep down, the warm, squishy asthenosphere slowly swirls like a simmering pot of soup, carrying heat in a giant churning dance!

q: Which of the following is NOT true of continental glaciers?
a: They form along mountain slopes at high elevations
Their weight depresses the underlying land
They can be found in Antarctica and Greenland
e: Continental glaciers are colossal sheets of ice that sprawl across vast lands, leaving steep mountain slopes to their smaller alpine cousins.

q: What is the capital of the U.S. state Texas?
e: While Houston is huge, lively Austin wears the crown as the capital where Texas leaders gather to make the rules.

q: The dynamic turnover of soil microbacteria plays an important role in long-term carbon sequestration and is being studied by scientists at Argonne National Lab. Which of the following is NOT a method by which carbon is removed from the soil?
e: While wind and rain carry carbon away, digestion happens inside soil critters without removing carbon from the ground.

q: Which of the following is a highly crystalline mineral with perfect cleavage:
e: Halite is ordinary rock salt, but it loves neatness, snapping into tidy, sparkling little cubes with perfectly smooth breaks!

q: Which of these is NOT a city in Saudi Arabia?
e: Glittering Dubai actually shines in the United Arab Emirates next door, not inside the kingdom of Saudi Arabia.

q: Which of the following molecules contributes the most to the absorption of UV light in the stratosphere?
e: High in the sky, ozone acts like our planet's favorite pair of sunglasses, catching most of the sun's harsh ultraviolet rays!

q: Which of the following is NOT true about magma:
a: volcanic glass results when magma cools very slowly
fluid basaltic magma typically produces the least pyroclastic material
granitic magma contains more silica and water than basaltic magma
andesitic magma is dominant in volcanoes around the Pacific Ocean Basin
e: Volcanic glass needs a super-fast freeze, cooling so quickly that shiny crystals do not even have time to grow!

q: If wind speeds in a storm are clocked in excess of 200 mph, this is most likely a measurement within a :
e: A fierce tornado spins like an unstoppable, runaway top, packing enough wild punch to whip past two hundred miles per hour!

q: Which of the following is a region of Earth's atmosphere where convection is most likely to take place:
e: The troposphere is where our weather lives, brewing clouds as warm air happily bubbles up and cooler air sinks right back down.

q: Which of the following does NOT satisfy the scientific definition of a mineral:
a: it is always an inorganic substance
it has a distinct chemical composition
it can be a solid or a molten substance
it must form by natural processes
e: To join the mineral club, you must be solid, so melted rock has to chill out first!

q: Which of the following is NOT a fossil fuel?
e: Coal and oil baked underground for millions of years, but wood comes from living trees, so it is not a fossil fuel.

q: What city  has the busiest airport in the world?
e: Atlanta, Georgia welcomes more zooming airplanes and traveling families through its gates than any other city on Earth.

q: The aurora borealis, or northern lights, would not be observed if Earth lacked which of the following?
e: Earth's magnetic field acts like an invisible shield, steering solar particles toward the poles to paint the glowing northern lights.

q: The deepest known point of the oceans is found in which of the following?
e: The mighty Pacific Ocean hides the deepest, darkest secret of all: the Mariana Trench, sinking miles beneath the waves.

q: Which islands below have been claimed by both Japan and Russia?
e: Perched like stepping stones between two big neighbors, the Kuril Islands have had both Russia and Japan claiming them as home.

q: In the deep ocean, the continuous shower of mostly organic detritus falling from the upper layers of the water column is called which of the following?
e: Down in the deep ocean, sinking bits of food drift like a gentle underwater blizzard called marine snow.

q: Which of the following is NOT something a river can do to rock?
a: Cut down through hundreds of meters of rock
e: A river can carve canyons and roll pebbles, but it is not fiery lava—it cannot melt rock!

q: Hurricanes are rated by categories on what five-point scale?
e: Weather watchers use the five-level Saffir-Simpson scale to measure a hurricane's howling winds and tell us how strong it is.

q: There are no roads in/out of Juneau, Alaska.
e: Juneau is wrapped so tightly by giant glaciers and mountains that cars cannot drive in, leaving only boats and planes.

q: Which English county will you find the University of East Anglia?
e: You will find this cheerful campus nestled happily in the county of Norfolk, surrounded by green fields and wandering bunnies.

q: Trophic levels describe energy flow in an ecosystem. Which of the following statements about trophic levels is NOT true?
a: Every organism's trophic level is determined by its feeding behavior
Every organism's trophic level remains the same throughout its life span
Energy flows from primary producers to consumers
e: Creatures can change what they eat as they grow, like a plant-munching tadpole becoming a bug-snapping frog.

q: If Yellowstone Caldera suffered a catastrophic eruption today, which of the following types of volcanic hazard is most likely to have the farthest reaching effects?
e: While heavy lava stays close to home, winds carry powdery volcanic ash thousands of miles across the sky to blanket distant towns.

q: Which geologic eon starts at the formation of the earth?
e: When baby Earth first formed as a wild, fiery ball of rock, that sizzling beginning was the Hadean eon.

q: Which of the following is a true tidal wave:
e: A tidal bore is a true tidal wave because the ocean's incoming tide actually pushes water backward up a river!

q: Which of the following lists of features is associated with a convergent plate boundary?
a: Primarily shallow earthquakes, rifting, volcanic activity
Subduction, trench, volcanic activity, shallow to deep earthquakes
e: When giant plates crash, one dives under in subduction, carving deep trenches and waking up rumbling volcanoes and earthquakes.

q: When a roller coaster executes a loop-de-loop, riders do not feel like they are falling out of the seat. From a rider's reference frame, which of the following best explains this?
a: The outward-directed centrifugal force counteracts gravity
The outward-directed centripetal force counteracts gravity
The inward-directed centrifugal force counteracts gravity
The inward-directed centripetal force counteracts gravity
e: As you loop upside down, outward centrifugal force pushes you snugly into your seat, keeping gravity from dropping you!

q: Italy and Ireland are the only countries in Europe that start with the letter I.
e: Iceland would feel very left out, because its fiery volcanoes and icy glaciers start with an I, too!

q: Which of the following is the primary reason for the decline in fish populations in New England lakes, rivers and streams:
a: destruction of native species by invasive species
e: Pollution created acid rain that fell into New England's waters, making them too sour for fish to survive.

q: Sea ice floating on the oceans is the first to melt as the Earth's climate warms. Which of the following most accurately models the impact melting sea ice has on global sea level?
a: Like the water level in a basin when you pour a glass of water into it, sea level will rise significantly
The ocean floor rocks and sediments are porous like sponges. They will absorb the additional water from the ice and sea level will not rise significantly
Like a melting ice cube sitting in a glass of water, the water and the melted cube will evaporate and sea level will drop
Like ice cubes in a glass of water, the ice has already displaced the water so as the ice melts, sea level will not rise significantly
e: Floating sea ice already pushes aside water just like ice cubes in your drink, so melting won't raise the ocean's level much.

q: Which of the following is the longest river in Europe?
e: Russia's mighty Volga River stretches for thousands of miles, making it the longest, grandest river in all of Europe.

q: Fossil fuels form through the decomposition of organic materials. You're studying a map that shows ancient environments. If you went hunting tomorrow for fossil fuels, which of these ancient habitats would you avoid?
e: Ancient deserts were too dry for lots of lush plants and critters to live, decompose, and become buried fossil fuels.

q: Burning fossil fuels is the primary source of emissions for which of the following greenhouse gases?
e: When our cars and factories burn fossil fuels, they puff out huge blankets of carbon dioxide, wrapping the planet in extra warmth.

q: What is responsible for producing ozone in the stratosphere?
a: The interaction of oxygen and ultraviolet light
The interaction of methane and ultraviolet light
e: High in the sky, energetic ultraviolet sunlight zaps regular oxygen molecules, happily piecing them together to build our protective ozone shield.

q: Which of these country's capitals starts with the letter B?
e: Lebanon's historic capital is beautiful Beirut, sitting right on the sunny blue Mediterranean Sea.

q: Which of the following types of decay occurs when a neutron is converted into a proton and an electron?
e: During beta decay, a restless neutron changes its mind and becomes a proton, zipping out a tiny electron in the process.

q: Which of the following were NOT produced by the eruption of Mount Saint Helens in 1980:
e: Mount Saint Helens blasted out thick, silica-rich lava instead of runny, basic lava during its explosive 1980 blowout.

q: Which of the following earthquakes is recognized as having the highest magnitude?
e: The mighty 1964 Alaska quake shook the earth with an astonishing 9.2 magnitude, out-rumbling all the other quakes listed.

q: Utility companies have adopted a net metering approach with consumers who have renewable sources connected to the electric network. What is net metering?
a: A program in which people pay for total energy consumption rather than per unit consumption
A program in which people donate a certain amount of funds to those who have trouble paying for their electricity bill
The power company's method to reduce consumption during peak periods
An incentive program that credits or pays customers who wish to supplement the utility's electricity with their own sources
e: If your rooftop solar panels make extra electricity, net metering lets you share that power with the utility company for bill credits.

q: Governments banned the production and use of what group of chemicals because of the damage they do to the ozone layer.
e: Old spray cans leaked chlorofluorocarbons, so governments banned them before these troublemaking chemicals could chew up our friendly ozone shield.

q: Seismographs, used to keep track of earthquakes, use which of the following variables to measure earthquakes?
a: The amplitude and frequency of water waves
The rotational motion of the recording drum
The differential motion between two vibrating structures
The differential motion between a free mass and a supporting structure anchored to the ground
e: A seismograph tracks quakes by comparing its anchored frame, which shakes with the ground, to a heavy weight hanging quietly still inside.

q: Which of the following is the term for a downward shift of the Earth's surface caused by excess removal of ground water?
e: When we slurp up too much underground water, the empty soil squishes and sinks downward in a slow slump called subsidence.

q: A conglomerate rock belongs to which of the following groups of rocks:
e: Conglomerate is a clastic sedimentary rock because nature cements it together from tumbled gravel and pebbles, just like a rocky scrapbook.

q: Which of the following is NOT a mechanism of erosion?
e: While wind and water hustle rocks away, photolytic breakdown only uses sunlight to split chemicals, so it cannot erode dirt.

q: Which of the following is the most notable product of the hydrolysis of feldspar:
e: When water chemically weathers tough feldspar through hydrolysis, it gently transforms the hard rock into soft, earthy clay minerals.

q: Where is the Volga River?
e: Winding like a giant watery ribbon, the mighty Volga River flows across the vast, chilly lands of Russia.

q: In which of the following locations would a preponderance of actively-produced pillow lavas be found:
e: Deep underwater along the mid-Atlantic ridge, erupting lava touches icy ocean water and puffs into giant, rounded rocky pillows.

q: Which of the following is a characteristic of an area with Karst topography?
e: In karst landscapes, underground water secretly dissolves soft limestone until the ground caves in, creating surprise bowl-shaped sinkholes.

q: Which of the following is the only ocean current that flows nearly unimpeded around the Earth:
e: With no land blocking its path around Antarctica, this mighty current circles the entire globe on one nonstop, watery merry-go-round.

q: The Principality of Sealand is an unrecognized micronation off the coast of what country?
e: Tiny Sealand perches on a rusty metal tower out in the waves, looking right back at the United Kingdom.

q: Which of the following scales is used to rate hurricanes?
e: The Saffir-Simpson scale measures a hurricane's roaring winds, rating how powerful and pushy the storm gets from Category 1 to 5.

q: Which of the following statements is true about glaciers?
a: Glaciers are generally full of rocks and sediments and can move these objects far from their sources
When a glacier retreats, it moves backwards
Humans did not exist when glaciers were covering much of North America
There is more glacial ice today than there has been in the past 100 years
e: Glaciers act like giant frozen bulldozers, scooping up dirt and heavy boulders to carry them miles away on an epic, slow road trip.

q: Which of the following is the largest unit of time on the geologic time scale?
e: An eon is the grandest chapter of all on Earth's calendar, bundling up billions of years into one giant stretch of time.

q: Which of the following greenhouse gases is the longest-lived in the atmosphere?
e: Nitrous oxide is a tough greenhouse gas that stubbornly floats in the sky for over a century, outlasting all the others.

q: Which technology is the largest source of carbon-free renewable electricity in the United States?
e: Mighty rushing rivers spin giant dam turbines, making rushing water the heavyweight champion of clean, carbon-free energy here.

q: Which of the following is closest to the ratio of the energy released by a magnitude 5 earthquake to that of a magitude 4 earthquake?
e: Every whole step up on the earthquake scale packs a punch, releasing about thirty-two times more ground-shaking energy.

q: A cubic meter of H2O has the greatest amount of energy in which of the following situations?
a: Ice in a Rocky Mountain glacier
Water vapor in an air mass over Kansas
Water in the Gulf of Mexico
e: Invisible water vapor floating in the air is packed with excited, zooming molecules, giving it far more energy than liquid or ice.

q: Which of the following is considered a non-metallic mineral resource?
e: Unlike shiny metals, quartz is made of silicon and oxygen, making this sparkly crystal a proud non-metallic mineral found in sand and glass.

q: Most continents contain large central areas in which very ancient rocks are exposed. What are these areas called?
e: Cratons are like the tough, ancient bones at the heart of each continent, holding Earth's oldest rocks safely together for billions of years.

q: Why are there no deep-sea trenches off the east coast of the United States?
a: There are no trenches in the Atlantic Ocean; trenches exist only in the Pacific Ocean
The Appalachian Mountains are volcanic mountains and trenches are not associated with volcanism
The eastern coast of the United States is in the middle of the North American Plate, not at a plate margin where trenches can occur
The deep ocean trenches have been filled with sediments from the many rivers that drain the U.S.
e: Sitting peacefully in the middle of the North American plate, this calm coast avoids the crashing edges where deep trenches hide.

q: Which of the following is NOT true of the Cretaceous [kri-TAY-shuhs] geologic time period?
a: It is the last period in the Mesozoic era
It was a period of relatively warm climate
The period began with a large mass extinction
e: The Cretaceous period actually ended with that famous asteroid crash, rather than beginning with a giant extinction.

q: Which of the following types of fossil fuels is created primarily from the remains of vegetation?
e: Millions of years ago, ancient swamp plants and leafy ferns got squished underground, slowly baking into the dark, chunky rock we call coal.

q: What is the approximate minimum temperature difference in degrees Celsius required between deep and shallow waters for an Ocean Thermal Energy Conversion (OTEC) system to be commercially viable?
e: To spin those ocean power generators, you need a temperature gap of about twenty degrees Celsius between the sunlit surface and chilly deep water.

q: Which of the following describes the relationship between water particles and ocean waves?
a: Waves move water particles effectively along the surface of water
Waves have no impact on the motion of water particles
Water moves in vertical orbits in the direction of waves
Water particles are fragmented in the white caps of waves
e: Water drops ride a rolling underwater Ferris wheel, looping in circles as the wave dances across the sea.

q: Which of the following best describes how the frequency of an ocean wave changes as its wavelength changes?
a: It increases as the wavelength increases
It increases as the wavelength decreases
It decreases as the wavelength decreases
It decreases as the wavelength increases
e: When wave crests squeeze closer together with shorter wavelengths, more of them rush past every second, making their frequency shoot up!

q: Oceanic crust being formed at spreading centers is primarily made of:
e: When underwater cracks push out fiery lava, the chilly ocean cools it into dark, heavy basalt to build brand-new seafloor.

q: Which of the following is a type of chemical weathering?
e: When sneaky oxygen nibbles on iron inside a rock, it turns it into crumbly rust through oxidation.

q: On a topographic map, you see a feature represented by a set of concentric circles. The outermost circle is labeled 1,000, and the innermost circle is labeled 1,300. You are most likely looking at which of the following features?
e: As you step inward, the ground climbs higher like a giant layer cake, making this cozy bump a hill.

q: Which of the following sets of states are included as a part of "tornado alley"?
e: Warm southern air and chilly northern winds love crashing together over Texas, Kansas, and Missouri, spinning up wild storms in Tornado Alley.

q: Which of the following seas of the Arctic Ocean has observed the greatest loss of ice since 1990?
e: The Chukchi Sea has warmed up fast, watching more of its thick ice melt away than any other Arctic sea since 1990.

q: Glaciers can have quite an effect on Earth's surface. They can:
a: Sink to the bottom of the ocean then grow until they reach the surface
e: Glaciers creep like heavy frozen bulldozers, grinding against solid mountains and scooping out giant, bowl-shaped valleys with ease.

q: Which of the following is the coldest and densest water in Earth's oceans?
e: Antarctic bottom water gets so icy-cold and salty near the South Pole that it sinks straight to the ocean floor.

q: Which of the following rocks is NOT metamorphic?
e: Limestone never got squished and baked deep underground like metamorphic rocks; it gently settled from ancient sea shells instead.

q: When exposed to the atmosphere, iron begins to rust. This surface process represents what type of reaction?
e: When shiny iron hugs oxygen in the air, it goes through oxidation, wearing a crumbly red coat of rust!

q: The city of Los Angeles is famous for its hazy "smoggy" days. Which of the following pollutants is a major contributor to smog?
e: Down here where we breathe, ozone teams up with sunlight and car fumes to wrap cities in hazy smog blankets.

q: Which of the following best describes how geysers form?
a: Spontaneous eruption from a pressurized, confined aquifer
Separation of water-rich magma from molten rock as it cools and crystallizes
Superheating of groundwater by a nearby magma chamber
Squeezing of groundwater out of fractured rock by tectonic forces
e: Deep underground, fiery magma superheats trapped groundwater like a giant whistling tea kettle until it bursts toward the sky!

q: Which of the following describes one way that changes in land use may exacerbate global warming?
a: By increasing the pH of the oceans
By sequestering carbon from the atmosphere
By releasing stored carbon to the atmosphere
e: When people clear ancient forests, trapped carbon escapes into the sky, wrapping our planet in an extra-thick warming blanket.

q: Which of the following sedimentary rocks is often formed in a tropical ocean?
e: In warm tropical waters, billions of tiny sea creatures leave behind their shells, slowly packing together to make limestone.

q: Which of the following is the BEST example of a littoral ocean current:
e: Hugging the sandy beach, a rip current is a nearshore rush of water that playfully zips straight back out to sea.

q: Which of the following contain the most groundwater?
e: Instead of swimming in giant caves, most underground water quietly hides inside billions of tiny pores and cracks in rock!

q: Which of the following silicate mineral groups has a single-chain silicate structure?
e: Pyroxenes build their crystal homes by linking silica building blocks into one neat, single chain, like holding hands in line.

q: Scientists from two DOE labs, Pacific Northwest and Oak Ridge National Labs, have developed new methods for extracting uranium from seawater. Which of the following would this be used to fuel?
e: Fission reactors split heavy uranium atoms in half to unleash huge bursts of power, making electricity for our bustling world!

q: It is estimated that the temperature of the Earth's core is:
a: as hot as the surface of the sun
much hotter than the surface of the sun
much cooler than the surface of the sun
e: Right at Earth's cozy center, the core glows blazing hot, matching the fiery surface of the sun itself.

q: On which of the following types of volcanoes is scoria commonly found?
e: Steep cinder cone volcanoes spit bubbly lava that quickly cools into dark, crumbly rocks called scoria, piling up like sprinkles.

q: SunStop is a flexible film developed at the National Renewable Energy Lab that is capable of preventing what form of energy from entering a building through its windows?
e: This clever film blocks invisible infrared light, turning away invisible heat rays at the window so rooms stay refreshingly cool.

q: Which of the following features is created by a volcano?
e: When a volcano erupts with a mighty boom, its emptied belly collapses inward, leaving behind a giant bowl called a caldera.

q: Which of the following is the thickest layer of Earth's interior?
e: Earth wears the mantle like a giant, super-thick sweater beneath its crust, making it the thickest layer of all!

q: Which of the following will typically be BEST preserved as a fossil:
e: Marine and desert critters get swiftly tucked under sand or mud, keeping them safe from rot so they become wonderful fossils.

q: Which of the following best explains why Triton can hold an atmosphere?
a: Its atmosphere is primarily composed of massive gases
Its atmosphere is primarily composed of light gases
e: Triton is so freezing cold that its gas molecules move too sluggishly to escape, letting this chilly moon keep its atmosphere!

q: Which of the following describes how sea ice is different from continental ice?
a: Continental ice is denser than sea ice
Sea ice is saline while continental ice is fresh
Sea ice floats on the water while continental ice sits on land
Sea ice is constantly changing while continental ice remains the same
e: Sea ice bobs gently on ocean waves, while grand continental ice rests its heavy feet firmly on solid land.

q: Oceanic crust ranges in age from newly formed to about 200 million years old. In what area of the ocean floor would you find the oldest crust?
e: As fresh seafloor bubbles up in the middle, it pushes older, sleepy rock all the way to continental coastlines for a long rest.

q: The title of the 1969 film "Krakatoa, East_of Java" is incorrect, as Krakatoa is in fact west of Java.
e: That Hollywood movie got its compass totally backwards, because fiery Krakatoa actually sits to the west of Java!

q: Which one of these countries borders with Poland?
e: Up in the northeast, friendly Lithuania snuggles right up against Poland's border to share a cozy hello.

q: The salinity of ocean water is often determined from its conductivity, measured against the conductivity of which of the following substances dissolved in water?
e: Scientists test sea water against trusty potassium chloride, using its steady electric spark like a ruler to see just how salty our ocean really is.

q: Burning rock refers to which of the following energy sources?
e: Oil shale is packed with so much trapped fuel that you can actually set this fiery stone ablaze like a giant matchstick!

q: Which of the following types of volcano usually covers the most acreage on the surface of the Earth?
e: Shield volcanoes gently spill runny lava that travels for miles, spreading out like giant, sleepy pancakes across the land.

q: Which of the following is closest to the percentage of electricity produced in the US using renewable energy sources?
e: Green energy was just getting rolling here, with breezes and sunshine powering a modest ten percent of our giant electrical grid.

q: What is the state capital of South Dakota?
e: Sitting quietly along the Missouri River, the friendly little town of Pierre proudly serves as South Dakota's state capital.

q: Which of the following events are associated with the highest tides?
e: When the sun and moon team up in a straight line, their combined gravity pulls ocean water into giant, joyful leaps called spring tides!

q: Which of the following features is not usually associated with Shield Volcanoes?
a: Made primarily of Highly Fluid Basaltic Lavas
They are commonly considered to be the most explosive and dangerous type of volcano.
Fissure eruptions are common on the flanks of these volcanoes.
e: Shield volcanoes are gentle giants that slowly ooze runny lava, making them far less explosive than their fiery mountain cousins.

q: What is the capital of British Columbia, Canada?
e: Vancouver gets lots of big-city buzz, but Victoria sits happily by the ocean as the province's true capital.

q: Hot springs are sources of which of the following types of energy?
e: Deep rocks boil with Earth's natural underground heat, bubbling up into hot springs full of clean geothermal energy.

q: Scientists at the National Renewable Energy Lab are studying magnesium batteries as an alternative to current lithium-ion technology. What is the charge on the magnesium ions in these batteries?
e: Magnesium happily gives away two tiny negative electrons, leaving each busy ion with a cheerful plus two electric charge to power our gadgets.

q: What type of volcano is Mt. Fuji in Japan?
e: Mount Fuji built its gorgeous cone by stacking layer upon layer of hardened ash and lava, making it a classic stratovolcano.

q: What draws the charged particles from the solar wind to the polar regions of the Earth?
a: Jet stream currents in Earth's upper atmosphere
e: Earth acts like a cozy giant magnet, using its invisible magnetic field to guide wild solar particles straight to the snowy poles.

q: What is the smallest country in South America by area?
e: Suriname is a quiet, jungle-filled gem that takes up less land than any other country in South America.

q: 70% of all the Fresh Water on Earth is found in:
e: Chilly Antarctica keeps most of our planet's fresh water tucked away, locking it up inside giant, sparkling sheets of ancient polar ice.

q: Which of the following sets of two variables controls how fast a soil forms?
a: Type of parent rock and climate
Type and age of parent rock
e: Climate and the parent rock work together, deciding how quickly tough stones crumble into soft, rich soil.

q: Which of the following is an effect of El Nio on the southern United States' climate?
e: El Nino nudges stormy winds across the South, spinning up wild weather that brings an increase in tornadoes.

q: Which of the following Appalachian Mountain provinces is the eroded remnant of a folded mountain belt?
e: Huge ancient forces crumpled this land like a wrinkled blanket, carving out the wavy, folded landscape of the Valley and Ridge belt.

q: Argonne National Lab researchers are studying iridium [ih-RID-ee-um] oxide nanoparticles as a catalyst for the water-splitting reaction. Which of the following has the highest concentration of iridium?
e: Long ago, Earth's iridium sank deep into its core, leaving roaming space meteorites packed with the biggest cosmic stash of this rare metal.

q: Which of the following igneous rock textures would NOT be considered an intrusive texture?
e: Lava cooling fast on Earth's surface forms fine-grained aphanitic rock, unlike coarse rocks trapped growing slowly deep underground.

q: Artes [a-reets] and drumlins are formed by what agent of weathering?
e: Giant, creeping glaciers act like icy bulldozers, carving sharp rocky ridges called arêtes and shaping smooth little hills called drumlins as they crawl.

q: Scientists at Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory have built an observatory to study how rocks fracture, a process that influences greenhouse gas emissions, impacts groundwater, and induces seismicity[size-MIH-sih-tee]. In particular, this research is most relevant to the harvesting of what energy resource?
e: To harvest shale gas, workers crack open tight underground rocks so the trapped fuel can finally escape and power our world.

q: Which of the following rocks likely formed from the lowest temperature melt?
e: Granite cools from a cozy, silica-rich magma that can melt at much lower, gentler temperatures than tough rocks like basalt.

q: The connection scheme used to connect a renewable energy source to the utility grid is usually called which of the following?
e: Instead of one giant plant, little solar roofs share their power from all over, making distributed generation a wonderful team effort!

q: Which of the following is true about the 2012 North Atlantic hurricane season?
a: Two of the tropical storms occurred before the official June 1 beginning of hurricane season
Four major hurricanes, categories 3 through 5, struck the East Coast
The exceptionally weak jet stream over the eastern portion of the nation could not push hurricanes off the East Coast
El Nio proved to be a major influence in suppressing overall storm activity
e: In 2012, two eager tropical storms decided not to wait for summer and spun to life before the official June first kickoff!

q: Which of the following energy sources is considered a fossil fuel?
e: Crude oil is made from tiny ancient sea creatures that got squished deep underground for millions of years, making it a true fossil fuel.

q: What mineral is used in its molten state as a necessary part of the Hall-Heroult process?
e: Melty cryolite acts like a hot bath that dissolves aluminum ore, helping us zap out pure aluminum without needing crazy-high heat.

q: Which of the following would NOT contribute to sea level rise?
e: Floating sea ice already takes up space in the water, just like ice cubes melting in a full glass!

q: According to the EPA, which of the following is closest to the percentage of U.S. greenhouse gas emissions in 2009 that resulted from the provision of food?
e: Growing, shipping, and cooking our meals whipped up thirteen percent of America's greenhouse gases in 2009.

q: If convection currents in the mantle stopped, which of the following would likely happen?
a: The number of earthquakes would increase
The number of earthquakes would stay the same
The number of earthquakes would decrease
e: Earth's restless mantle churns like boiling soup to push plates around. If it stopped moving, the ground would quiet down and earthquakes would decrease.

q: Which of these Mediterranian islands is under the sovereign rule of France?
e: With its wild mountain peaks rising from the sea, Corsica is the island that belongs to France.

q: What is the largest non-continental island in the world?
e: Greenland wears a giant, sparkling coat of ice and easily beats every other island in pure size.

q: The wavelength of an ocean wave is defined by which of the following?
a: The distance from crest to trough
The height of the wave from crest to trough
The height change from trough to trough
e: If you hopped from the tippy-top crest of one wave straight to the very next crest, you just measured its wavelength!

q: Which of the following is believed to be the process that causes Earth's tectonic plates to move:
a: gravitational influence of the Sun and Moon directly on continental plates
e: Deep down, Earth's mantle slowly churns like hot porridge, creating swirling currents that carry our giant crust puzzle pieces around.

q: Which of the following is a measure of a mineral's resistance to scratching?
e: Hardness shows how tough a rock is when another mineral tries to scratch its proud, shiny face.

q: Which of the following language families is the most controversial amongst modern linguists?
e: Altaic stirs up big debates because language detectives cannot agree if all those spoken words truly share one ancestor.

q: Which of the following statements is NOT true about the Inga Falls?
a: They are in the Democratic Republic of Congo
They are on the Zambezi River
They are the largest waterfall by volume in the world
A plant planned there would potentially generate twice as much electricity as China's Three Gorges Dam
e: These thundering, energetic falls do not rush along the Zambezi River, because they actually call the mighty Congo River home!

q: Suppose you find a rock with angular clasts. Which of the following is the correct classification?
e: Breccia is packed with sharp, jagged rock bits that broke off and got glued together before water could smooth them down.

q: How many countries are larger than Australia?
e: Only five giant countries, including Russia and Canada, are bigger on the map than sunny Australia!

q: Which of the following is NOT a reasonable line of evidence for a global cooling event?
e: When Earth gets super chilly, ocean water freezes into giant glaciers, so sea levels actually drop instead of rising!

q: Which of the following describes a typical profile of dissolved oxygen concentration with increasing depth in the North Atlantic ocean?
a: Low at the surface, increases with depth
High at the surface, decreases with depth, then increases with depth
High at the surface, decreases with depth
Low at the surface, little change with depth
e: Waves mix oxygen at the sunny surface, critters breathe it up mid-way, but chilly polar currents deliver fresh air deep down!

q: Which of the following best describes an advantage of using an incinerator for solid waste?
a: It helps to reduce air pollution
It reduces the volume of materials that go to landfills
It allows waste products to be recycled
If operated as permitted, it is not at all hazardous to plants, animals, and people
e: Incinerators gobble up mountains of trash and turn them into tiny piles of ash, leaving way more room in our landfills.

q: What is the largest lake in the African continent?
e: Lake Victoria is so enormous it feels like an inland sea, making it the biggest, splashiest lake in all of Africa.

q: Which of the following statements best describes a benefit of using alternative energy resources?
a: It reduces the amount of fossil fuels that must be used
It reduces the amount of renewable resources used
It reduces the costs of producing energy
e: Catching sunshine and wind gives us clean power, helping our planet by reducing how much smoky fossil fuel we must burn.

q: Scientists at Savannah River National Lab are studying new ways of separating and storing tritium [TRIH-tee-um] gas. Which of the following correctly describes the constituent particles in a nucleus of tritium?
e: Inside tritium's cozy atomic heart, a single proton cuddles up with two quiet neutron buddies.

q: As you are swimming in a river, you find two cobbles made of the same rock, but one is angular and one is rounded. Which of the following best explains this observation?
a: The angular cobble was transported further
The rounded cobble was transported further
The rounded cobble was formed in shallower water than the angular cobble
The angular cobble was formed in shallower water than the rounded cobble
e: That smooth, rounded stone went on a much longer river ride, bumping and tumbling until every sharp corner vanished!

q: Which of the following is a type of volcanic eruption that does not build up into the typical cone shape normally associated with volcanoes, even though it erupts huge volumes of fluid lava:
e: Instead of piling into a pointy mountain, fissure eruptions crack open the ground like a zipper, letting runny lava spill out everywhere!

q: Which of the following coasts in North America contains the most pronounced fjords:
a: the west coast from Puget Sound to Alaska
the west coast from Oregon to Mexico
the east coast from Maine to Florida
e: Ancient, frosty glaciers carved dramatic, watery canyons called fjords all the way from Puget Sound up to icy Alaska.

q: Sometimes compared to a slow-moving glob of toothpaste extruding from a tube of toothpaste, which of the following has formed several times within the crater Mount Saint Helens since its 1980 eruption:
e: Bits of cooling lava piled up inside the crater, building steep cinder cones like crunchy little volcanic hills.

q: Which of the following is NOT a likely impact of continued global warming:
a: polar ice could melt enough to raise the sea levels
e: Global warming messes with our air and oceans, but the deep underground magma making volcanoes could not care less about the weather.

q: In the United States, where does most of the hydropower production originate?
e: Mighty rivers rushing down near oceanic coastal regions pack tremendous energy, creating most of America's water power before meeting the sea.

q: Which of the following is the distance of one degree of longitude?
a: It varies from 111 kilometers to a point
e: Longitude lines are like watermelon stripes, spreading wide at Earth's belly but pinching together into a point at the icy poles.

q: In which of the following comparisons would you least expect the speed of sound to change?
a: Whale songs travelling through Arctic water compared to whale songs travelling through equatorial waters
Sounds made at the surface of the ocean compared to sounds made at a depth of 100 meters
Frog calls made in the spring when its 4 degrees Celsius compared to calls made at 28 degrees Celsius
Dog barks with low frequency compared to high frequency, excited dog barks
e: High squeaks and low growls travel through the same air at the exact same speed, no matter their pitch!

q: Bodies of water that do not flow into a sea, sometimes accumulating salts over time to become saline, are known as what type of lake?
e: Endorheic lakes are cozy little basins where water sneaks in but can never flow out to sea, slowly becoming salty over time.

q: Which of these would lead to the formation of a deep ocean trench?
e: When giant pieces of crust squeeze together with compressional force, one dives downward to carve an impossibly deep ocean trench.

q: The Earth's mantle is approximately how many miles thick:
e: Wrapped under Earth's thin crust, the toasty, rocky mantle is an enormous blanket stretching down about 1,800 miles.

q: Which of the following statements is NOT true about weather or climate?
a: The terms weather is used to describe atmospheric conditions over a short period of time in a particular area
Climate is the average weather pattern over many years in a particular area
Climate variability can be related to periodic changes such as El Nio or La Nia
e: Climate does not cause the weather; it is simply the ocean-sized scrapbook recording decades of daily rain and sunshine.

q: Which of these countries is not written in its native language?
e: Folks in Slovakia actually call their home Slovensko, while Slovaško is the special name their Slovenian neighbors use for them.

q: Crater Lake in Oregon is an example of a caldera [kahl-DARE- ah]. Which of the following statements best describes how this caldera formed?
a: A lava dam blocked a river and later broke free, forming the caldera
A mega-eruption blew off the side of Mount Mazama [mah-ZAH-mah]
A lava dome formed in the crater and later eroded leaving the caldera behind
The summit of Mount Mazama collapsed into the empty magma chamber below
e: Mount Mazama blasted out so much melted rock that its giant tummy went completely empty, causing the whole mountaintop to tumble right inside!

q: Which is the largest of these 4 islands?
e: Borneo stretches out so far across the ocean that it easily outgrows Madagascar, Cuba, and Great Britain.

q: Which of the following is the correct term for a large crack in ice:
e: When a giant, creeping glacier stretches and cracks open, it yawns into a deep, icy canyon called a crevasse!

q: Which of the following is a calcite-rich carbonate rock:
e: Limestone is like nature's cozy blanket, baked from countless ancient seashells packed full of a creamy mineral called calcite.

q: What is the capital of Seychelles?
e: On a tiny, sun-drenched island, the cheerful seaside city of Victoria serves as the proud capital of Seychelles.

q: Which of the following is an example of diagenesis [dye-ah-JEN- eh-sis]?
a: Chemical conversion of dinitrogen gas to fixed nitrogen
e: Diagenesis is the Earth gently squeezing and warming soft layers of mud until they cuddle tight and turn into solid rock!

q: How many counties in the Republic of Ireland.
e: Like puzzle pieces across a bright green quilt, twenty-six lovely counties fit together to make the Republic of Ireland.

q: A rock is described as a bioclastic sedimentary rock. Of which of the following could it be composed?
e: Bio means life and clastic means broken bits, so this rock is made of ancient shell fragments glued together over time.

q: Most gemstones belong to what class of minerals?
e: Most sparkling gemstones are silicates, built from silicon and oxygen holding hands to weave nature's favorite dazzling treasures.

q: A semidiurnal tidal pattern is more typical of which of the following locations:
a: the East Coast of the U.S.
the West Coast of the U.S.
e: Along America's East Coast, the ocean loves a steady dance, rolling in and out twice every day in a neat semidiurnal rhythm.

q: Which of the following types of rocks typically exhibits stratification?
e: Sedimentary rocks love stacking up their memories in neat, colorful stripes, just like a giant stack of ancient pancakes!

q: DOE researchers have been studying metastable materials, such as diamond. These materials are not thermodynamically stable but take a long time to be converted to more stable forms. Which of the following best explains why?
a: The products have higher delta G values
The products have lower delta G values
The activation energy for conversion is very high
The activation energy for conversion is very low
e: A diamond needs a giant hill of activation energy to break its super-tight bonds, so it stays sparkly forever!

q: Dimethylsulfide [dy-meth-uhl-SUHL-fyd], or DMS, is a byproduct of biological activity in sea ice and a major source of cloud nuclei [NOO-klee-eye] to the atmosphere. Which of the following is true?
a: DMS levels in ice-free regions of ocean are higher than in ice-laden regions
The Antarctic atmosphere receives the highest amounts of atmospheric DMS during the spring to early summer months (November through December)
Dissolved DMS concentrations are highest in Southern Ocean waters during the winter (July through August)
Release of DMS into the Antarctic atmosphere reduces the amount of regional cloud cover during the start of the summer season
e: When summer warmth greets Antarctica in November and December, melting ice wakes up happy algae that release the most DMS.

q: Local water table levels vary over time in response to a variety of factors. Which of the following statements best describes the cause of the formation of a "cone of depression?"
a: Pumping rate exceeds recharge rate in an aquifer
Water flows out of the aquifer into a gaining stream
Permeability [pur-mee-ah-BIL-ih tee] decreases due to a drought
A flowing artesian well remains upcapped for a long period of time
e: Slurping water out through a well faster than underground rain can refill it creates a cone of depression, like a dimple in a drink!

q: The presence of which of the following is evidence that 2 valley glaciers have or had at one time joined into a larger glacier:
e: When two icy glaciers hold hands and merge, their dirty edges blend together down the center to form a stripe called a medial moraine.

q: There exists an island named "Java".
e: Java is indeed a real, bustling island in Indonesia, full of rumbling volcanoes and millions of friendly neighbors!

q: Where can most deserts be found?
a: In the horse latitudes and on the lee side of mountains
At the equator and on the lee side of forests
Wherever humans use too much water
e: Deserts love hiding in the horse latitudes or behind tall mountains, where sinking dry air stubbornly refuses to drop any rain.

q: Which of the following intrusive rock deposits is largest in size?
e: Deep underground, massive batholiths cool into colossal rock giants, easily dwarfing smaller dikes and sills.

q: Which of the following is similar to a delta but forms when a steep mountain stream spreads out from a mountain canyon onto a flat, broad valley:
e: Rushing out of a tight mountain canyon, a stream happily spreads its rocky gravel across the flat valley like a giant alluvial fan.

q: In which of the following ways is firn formed on glaciers:
a: the partial melting and refreezing of snow crystals into ice grains
the polishing of rocks and boulders by abrasion in stream beds
layers of sand and sediment originating in glaciers that are transported upslope by strong winds
friction between bedrock along the base of a glacier
e: Fluffy snow gets a cozy makeover as it partly melts and refreezes into crunchy little ice grains called firn!

q: In which of the following types of rocks would you be most likely to find a fossil?
e: Shale forms from gentle mud that tucks ancient plants and bones into safe, cozy layers, preserving them as fossils.

q: Iceland is very tectonically active; which of the following does NOT contribute to its interesting geologic and tectonic past and present?
a: Location adjacent to a subduction zone
e: Iceland loves tearing apart and bursting with hot lava, but its plates never slide beneath one another in a subduction zone.

q: Which of the following processes increases salinity in surface waters of the ocean?
e: When the sun drinks up fresh water through evaporation, it leaves all the salty bits behind, making the sea extra salty!

q: Most groundwater is stored in pore spaces that are typically how big?
e: Underground rocks squeeze groundwater into tiny, cozy pockets just one to five millimeters wide, like drops hiding between sand grains.

q: Which of the following is the BEST reason why the Earth's inner core is solid and the outer core is not:
a: inner core is further removed from the influence of hot magma
e: Earth hugs its center so fiercely that the giant underground pressure squeezes the inner core completely solid.

q: Kuala Lumpur is the capital of which country?
e: Kuala Lumpur shines with giant twin towers reaching for the clouds, proudly serving as Malaysia's bustling capital city.

q: Water is released into the atmosphere by plants through a process know as.
e: Through transpiration, thirsty plants breathe water vapor straight from their leaves into the sky like a refreshing sigh.

q: Rocks that are produced when magma cools and solidifies deep below the Earth's crust are called:
e: Magma that sneaks deep underground cools slowly inside Earth, quietly building intrusive igneous rock like a hidden treasure.

q: Moraines, drumlins, and eskers are depositional features caused by which of the following?
e: Glaciers creep across the land like icy bulldozers, piling up dirt into bumpy hills called moraines and drumlins.

q: Fossils found in the deep ocean are cemented in what kind of rock?
e: Deep sea mud and shells settle together on the ocean floor, slowly squishing over time into cozy sedimentary rock.

q: Meandering streams are most commonly noted to form which of the following specific bodies of water:
e: When a twisty river gets tired of looping around, it takes a shortcut and leaves behind a sleepy, U-shaped oxbow lake.

q: Which of the following is NOT considered one of the major volcano types?
e: Runny basalt lava spreads out flat instead of building a puffy dome, so basalt domes are not real major volcanoes.

q: Which of the following ocean waters typically has the LEAST pronounced thermocline layer:
e: Polar waters are chilly from top to bottom, so they lack a big temperature jump called a thermocline.

q: If high tide occurs at noon, which of the following is the most likely time that the same beach will experience a low tide:
e: The ocean's water gently sloshes back and forth every six hours, so noon's high tide drops to low tide by six PM.

q: Which of the following is a metamorphic rock:
e: Under intense heat and squishing pressure, ordinary limestone transforms into smooth, elegant marble like a caterpillar becoming a butterfly.

q: Tasmania is an island state of Australia.
e: That is true! Tasmania sits right off the southern coast like a wild, green island state belonging to Australia.

q: How many rivers are in Saudi Arabia?
e: This warm, sandy desert land has zero permanent rivers running through it all year long.

q: Which of the following is an example of an island arc collision zone:
e: Japan was born when giant moving puzzle pieces under the ocean bumped together, pushing up a lively curved chain of volcanic islands.

q: Humans introduce 30 billion tons of carbon dioxide into the atmosphere each year. DOE National Lab scientists have found that plants and oceans can absorb carbon dioxide and convert it to which of the following types of rock?
e: Oceans drink up carbon dioxide, helping sea critters build shells that eventually pack together into sturdy limestone rock.

q: What is the term for an underground layer of permeable rock or loose sediments whose pore spaces are filled with water?
e: Deep underground, rocks and sand hold water like a cozy hidden sponge called an aquifer.

q: Which of the following conditions could result from overgrazing of livestock?
e: When livestock munch every last plant, protective soil blows away, causing desertification as green pastures turn into dry, sandy wastes.

q: Gibraltar, located just south of the Iberian peninsula, is a territory of which West Europe country?
e: Even though it sits under sunny Spanish skies, that famous rocky cliff belongs to the United Kingdom.

q: Which of the following minerals constitute approximately 60% of the Earth's crust:
e: Meet feldspar, the crust's busiest rock builder, quietly making up over half of the ground beneath our feet.

q: What is the only country in the world with a flag that doesn't have four right angles?
e: Nepal shows off a playful flag shaped like two stacked mountain peaks instead of a simple rectangle.

q: What type of drainage pattern is commonly found associated with volcanoes?
e: Rainwater rolls off a cone-shaped volcano in every direction like spokes on a bicycle wheel, creating a neat radial pattern.

q: Which of the following general statements is NOT true regarding the Arctic?
a: It is a smaller continent than the Antarctic
It is warmer than the Antarctic
It is at a lower elevation than the Antarctic
It is less isolated from other landmasses than the Antarctic
e: The Arctic is actually a frozen ocean framed by continents, so calling it a smaller continent is totally upside down!

q: Materials that compose the Earth's crust have densities that are different from the bulk density of the Earth. Which of the following is closest to the average density, in grams per cubic centimeter, of Earth's continental crust?
e: Our continental crust stays light on its feet, weighing just 2.7 grams for every little sugar cube of rock.

q: Beside batteries, which of the following is another way to store energy from renewable energy systems for later use?
e: Ultracapacitors act like energetic sponges, soaking up bursts of electricity in a flash and saving it for later chores.

q: Which of the following is NOT a key step in the rock cycle:
e: Rocks love melting, cooling, and squeezing together, but evaporation is just water's trick for vanishing into the air!

q: Which of the following rock types is most likely to preserve fossils?
e: Soft mud gently tucks ancient critters into bed, hardening into shale that keeps their fragile shapes safe for millions of years.

q: Compared to continental crust, oceanic crust melts at which of the following?
e: Dense oceanic crust is made of heavy rock that needs much higher temperatures to melt than softer continental crust.

q: Which of the following was NOT cited by Wegner as evidence for continental drift?
a: Fossils are similar on South America and Africa
Matching paleoclimate indicators on South America and Africa
Similar bathymetry of the sea floor on opposite sides of the Mid-Atlantic Ridge
e: Wegener matched up puzzle-piece continents and ancient fossils, but deep ocean floors had not been mapped yet in his day.

q: The World Health Organization headquarters is located in which European country?
e: Switzerland is home to the World Health Organization, where doctors watch over the world's well-being from peaceful Geneva.

q: As ancient seas evaporate, thick layers of which of the following minerals can be formed and later mined for economic use?
e: When ancient seas dried up under the sun, they left behind giant sparkling blankets of rock salt called halite.

q: What is the capital of Senegal?
e: Dakar sits proudly on Africa's western edge, serving as Senegal's colorful, music-loving capital city.

q: Which of the following layers of the atmosphere is closest to earth's surface?
e: Out of these high layers, the stratosphere sits lowest down, resting just above the fluffy weather clouds we see outside.

q: "Mongolia" was a part of the now non-existent U.S.S.R.
e: While Mongolia was close friends with the Soviet Union, it always stayed its own proud, independent country.

q: Studies using which of the following processes is BEST used for calculating the age of Earth:
e: Radioisotopes tick like steady little clocks, using their half-life decay to reveal Earth's true, ancient birthday.

q: Which of the following best describes why Earth has a magnetic field?
a: The inner core contains solid iron
The outer core contains liquid iron
The Moon exerts a gravitational pull
The Sun exerts a gravitational pull
e: Deep inside Earth, the outer core swirls with liquid iron, spinning like a fiery generator to power our magnetic shield!

q: Which of the following countries is within the Eurozone but outside of the Schengen Area?
e: Sunny island Cyprus spends euro coins at the market, but it sits outside the passport-free Schengen zone.

q: Which of the following situations could produce an artesian spring?
a: An aquifer underlain by an impermeable layer and overlain by a permeable one
An aquifer surrounded by permeable layers
e: Water trapped in a confined aquifer gets squeezed tight beneath heavy rock, building pressure until it bubbles up into an artesian spring!

q: What type of fault is characterized by two tectonic plates that slide past one another horizontally?
e: Imagine two giant puzzle pieces gently sliding past each other. That sideways glide makes it a transform fault!

q: Which of the following is NOT a type of sediment load carried by a river?
e: Rivers roll heavy rocks and float muddy flakes, but they never pack anything officially called a drifting load.

q: What is the capital of Chile?
e: Nestled right beside the towering Andes mountains, bustling Santiago acts as the proud capital city of long, skinny Chile.

q: Ground source heat pumps, a form of geothermal energy, are most similar to which of the following renewable energy applications?
e: Just like a heat pump sips gentle warmth from the dirt, a solar water heater gathers cozy heat from the sun to warm water.

q: In the coming years, most of the increases in U.S. natural gas production is expected to come from hydraulic fracturing in which type of sedimentary rock?
e: Shale is like a tightly closed stone book, trapping natural gas inside until hydraulic fracturing gently cracks its pages open.

q: Which of the following is true about deep mid-ocean ridge ecosystems?
a: There are no primary producers, only consumers and decomposers
The organisms are highly mobile, ascending daily to the ocean surface to feed
The source of energy is chemical energy from hydrothermal vents of the seafloor
The organisms have the most dynamic and complex coloring on their bodies so they can be visible at depth
e: Down where sunlight never shines, hydrothermal vents act like steaming underwater kitchens, feeding bizarre creatures with rich chemical energy!

q: Which of the following is a volcanic rock that is so lightweight that it can sometimes float on water:
e: Pumice is packed with bubbly air pockets from frothy lava, making it light enough to take a bath and float like a duck!

q: Which of the following is sometimes called volcanic glass because of its shiny appearance:
e: When fiery lava cools in a giant hurry, it freezes into shiny, dark volcanic glass named obsidian.

q: In which of the following depositional settings will sedimentary rock layers be deposited non-horizontally?
e: As a prograding delta marches into deep water, it dumps sandy blankets down a steep slope, tilting the layers sideways!

q: Which of the following is NOT an advantage of using high- voltage direct current electric power transmissions for the bulk transmission of electrical power?
a: It is more reliable than AC current
It has lower energy losses than AC current
It can synchronize AC produced by renewable energy sources
It can increase the power of an existing grid where additional wires are difficult to install
e: Direct current travels great distances efficiently, but its complicated parts mean it is not more reliable than steady alternating current.

q: Which of the following is a period on the Geological Time Scale that is part of the Paleozoic Era:
e: The Devonian period belongs to the ancient Paleozoic era, back when adventurous fish first ruled the oceans!

q: About how many million metric tons of methane do cattle emit into the atmosphere per year in the U.S.?
e: With every grassy burp, American cattle puff an astonishing 5.5 million metric tons of warming methane into our sky each year!

q: Earth's atmosphere contains several different layers that are most often defined according to:
e: Earth stacks its atmosphere like a giant cake, drawing layer boundaries wherever the temperature flips between warming up and cooling down.

q: Isotopes of which of the following elements would allow you to determine the age of the oldest rocks on Earth?
e: Uranium is an ancient rock clock that ticks super slowly, keeping time across billions of years to date Earth's oldest stones.

q: Which of the following countries is an island?
e: Cyprus sits all by itself in the blue sea, splashing happily as a true island surrounded by water.

q: The ozone layer is most effective as a defense against which of the following kinds of radiation?
e: Earth wears the ozone layer like invisible sunglasses, shielding our skin by soaking up harmful UV-B rays before they reach us!

q: At a depth of 2,900 kilometers below the Earth's surface, P seismic waves slow down rapidly and S seismic waves disappear. This indicates that 2,900 kilometers is the beginning of which of the following layers?
e: S-waves vanish because they cannot swim through liquids, proving this deep layer is a swirling puddle of liquid iron and nickel.

q: Which of the following is the best explanation of how rift valleys are formed?
a: The scouring of bedrock as glaciers retreat
The accumulation of glacial deposits deposited as glaciers retreat
A wide river scours out the land then shifts direction
e: When giant plates pull apart in tectonic divergence, the land between them slowly sinks down to create a lovely rift valley!

q: Which of the following is NOT an environmental concern associated with hydraulic fracturing?
e: Fracking stirs up dirty water and tiny quakes deep below, but it never makes the land's surface overheat.

q: Which of the following describes the temperature and productivity of surface ocean water in an upwelling zone?
e: Deep, chilly water bubbles up packed with tasty nutrients, turning the cold surface into a bustling buffet for ocean life.

q: The dominant component of most magma is:
e: Glowing subterranean magma is mostly made of silicon dioxide, a rock-building ingredient that makes melted stone nice and gooey.

q: Fossils are usually found in what type of rock?
e: Sedimentary rocks gently tuck old shells and bones into soft layers of mud, keeping them safe like buried treasures.

q: Which of the following is the name of the glacial deposit that is formed as a stream flows underneath a glacier?
e: When a river sneaks beneath a glacier, it dumps gravel into a long, winding ridge called an esker.

q: The law of superposition is used by geologists to predict which of the following properties of a rock:
e: Like laundry piling up in a hamper, older rocks sit at the bottom, showing their relative age compared to layers above.
