q: What determines when a tropical depression or storm is given hurricane status?
e: A storm earns its hurricane badge the moment its swirling winds spin fast enough to cross the official speed limit!

q: Pegmatites are examples of what kind of rock that can be formed by cooling processes within the earth?
e: Pegmatite is an intrusive rock because it bakes and cools slowly deep underground, giving its crystals time to grow huge.

q: The Svalbard Archipelago is a dependency of which country?
e: Norway lovingly looks after icy Svalbard, an Arctic wonderland where polar bears roam across snowy glaciers.

q: Which of the following is LEAST accurate about minerals:
a: calcite has a hardness of 3 on most of its surfaces but a hardness of 4 along the crystal face perpendicular to its long axis
the Moh's scale measures the absolute hardness of minerals
a mineral's chemical composition largely determines its crystal shape and cleavage pattern
a mineral's color is the same as its streak
e: Minerals love wearing colorful disguises, so scraping one across a tile often reveals a powder color totally different from its outside.

q: Strike-slip faults MOST commonly occur in which of the following:
e: Transform margins are where Earth's giant rocky plates scrape sideways past each other, creating classic slide-by strike-slip faults.

q: What principle of geology states that sedimentary beds originate as continuous layers that extend in all directions and eventually grade into different sediments or thin out?
e: Lateral continuity means muddy layers spread out in every direction like flat pancake batter until they finally thin out.

q: Which of the following choices is an example of a transform plate boundary?
e: California's famous San Andreas Fault is a transform boundary because two giant plates are slowly sliding horizontally past one another.

q: Which of the following assumptions is typically made when performing potassium-argon dating?
a: Some percentage of argon-40 produced by decay leaks out of the rock
Potassium-40 has a half-life of 1.3 million years
All argon-40 in a rock was produced by potassium-40 decay
e: Scientists assume a fresh rock starts with zero trapped argon-40, meaning every bit found today came from decaying potassium.

q: Which of the following metamorphic rocks cannot originate from shale?
e: Shale cooks into rocky friends like slate, but anthracite is shiny coal born purely from squished swamp plants!

q: According to the International Energy Agency, third-generation technologies for energy production are those not yet widely demonstrated or commercialized. Which of the following is NOT a third-generation technology for energy production?
e: Rooftop solar heating has been warming our bathwater for decades, making it an older, well-proven friend rather than brand-new tech.

q: Which of the following statements regarding Earth's core is NOT true?
a: It contains a liquid outer core and a solid inner core
The inner core has a higher temperature than the outer core
The inner core is responsible for Earth's magnetic field
The inner core has a greater density than the outer core
e: Earth's magnetic shield actually comes from the churning liquid outer core spinning like a giant dynamo, not the solid inner ball.

q: Which of these island countries is located in the Caribbean?
e: Barbados sparkles like a sunlit jewel right in the warm, crystal-blue waves of the Caribbean Sea.

q: Which of the following minerals has four planes of cleavage?
e: Meet fluorite, a clever crystal that snaps cleanly in four neat directions to make its very own little gem pyramids!

q: In geologic mapping, what term describes the angle between a rock layer and a horizontal plane?
e: Dip is just the playful tilt of a sleepy rock layer sliding down from a flat, level surface.

q: What chemical, produced by planktonic algae, is the major source of cloud-condensation nuclei over the open oceans?
e: Tiny ocean algae breathe out dimethyl sulphide, a busy little gas that helps water droplets gather together to build fluffy clouds.

q: Kilauea [kee-lou-AY-ah] and Mauna Loa [MOU-nuh LOH-uh], are examples of which of the following types of volcanoes?
e: These gentle giants are shield volcanoes, spreading runny lava far and wide until they look like enormous warrior shields resting on Earth.

q: How many islands does Kuwait have?
e: Kuwait dips its toes into the Persian Gulf with a neat little collection of nine offshore islands soaking up the sunshine.

q: Which of the following correctly describes the weather phenomenon rime?
a: A tornado that spins clockwise in the Northern Hemisphere
e: When chilly fog kisses freezing tree branches, it instantly turns into spiky white coats of ice called rime!

q: Given the current climatic conditions on Earth, at which of the following locations would a glacier most likely form?
a: 0 latitude at an elevation of 6,000 meters
15 N latitude at an elevation of 4,000 meters
30 N latitude at an elevation of 3,000 meters
45 N latitude at an elevation of 1,000 meters
e: Even at Earth's warm middle, climbing six thousand meters into the sky gets so freezing cold that snow packs into a glacier!

q: Which of the Milankovitch [mil-AYN-koh-vitch] cycles account for climate changes over a 41,000 year period?
e: Earth likes to stretch and nod over forty-one thousand years, and this slow, rhythmic tilt of its head is called obliquity.

q: Which of the following types of lifting mechanisms would most likely occur near a mountain range?
e: When wind bumps into a giant mountain, it gets shoved straight up the slopes, a climb scientists call orographic lifting.

q: Which of the following statements is NOT true about upwelling?
a: It is associated with good fishing
Water that rises to the surface as a result of upwelling is typically colder and richer in nutrients
It is caused when offshore wind causes surface water to build up along a coastline
It occurs in the open ocean and along coastlines
e: Upwelling needs winds to push water away, not pile it up, inviting cold, nutrient-rich deep water to rise and feed the fish.

q: Which of the following rocks can be biogenic?
e: Limestone is a cozy rock often built from ancient sea creatures who left their tiny seashells behind to cuddle together forever.

q: Which of the following was the evidence that Alfred Wegener did not have that would have convinced the scientific community that his theory of continental drift was correct:
e: Wegener saw continents fit like puzzle pieces, but he lacked paleomagnetic studies to track ancient magnetic footprints locked in ocean rocks.

q: Petroleum comes from:
a: Meteorite rocks that impacted the Earth millions of years ago found deep underground
Organic sediment transformed over time by bacteria, pressure, and temperature
e: Tiny sea critters got squished under heavy mud for millions of years, slowly baking into petroleum with help from heat and bacteria.

q: Which of these is NOT a city in India?
e: Islamabad is busy running things next door as Pakistan's capital, which means it is not in India at all!

q: What property of diatoms make them useful as climate proxies?
a: The chemical makeup of their shells reflects the water chemistry at their time of formation
The narrow temperature range in which they exist makes them markers for paleo0ocean temperatures
Their well-preserved digestive system provide ample evidence for ancient food webs
Their limited diversity and low adaptability make them key indicators of specific aquatic environments
e: Tiny diatoms build glass shells that lock in clues about ancient ocean water, like little time capsules telling old climate secrets.

q: A location contains deposits of poorly-sorted mixtures of sediment and rocks, including large boulders. Which of the following geological processes is most likely responsible for these deposits?
e: Giant glaciers act like clumsy bulldozers, dragging along tiny pebbles and huge boulders together, dumping them in one big, messy pile!

q: Tsunamis are most likely to be generated in which of the following oceans?
e: Surrounded by a lively ring of rumbling volcanoes and earthquakes, the vast Pacific Ocean stirs up most of our planet's giant tsunamis.

q: Lithium-ion batteries are generally built in the discharged state, then recharged after construction. Which of the following best explains why this is done?
a: The materials in the discharged state can be exposed to the atmosphere safely
In the charged state, the raw materials pose a risk of dendrite formation
Lithium dendrites cannot form in the discharged state
Lithiated manganese materials are particularly unstable in the presence of humidity
e: Discharged materials stay calm and safe in open air, so makers build the battery safely before charging it up with sparky energy.

q: Which of the following does NOT describe the asthenosphere?
e: The asthenosphere is actually in the upper mantle, where warm, squishy rock lets Earth's giant puzzle plates glide right over it.

q: Hematite belongs to which of the following mineral groups:
e: Hematite is an oxide mineral because iron hugs oxygen tightly, making a lovely rusty red rock!

q: Mammals first evolved during what geologic period?
e: Our tiny, furry mammal ancestors first scampered about during the Triassic period, playing hide-and-seek with the earliest dinosaurs.

q: The Earth's atmosphere contains roughly what percentage of oxygen by volume?
e: Take a deep breath! About twenty percent of the air dancing into your lungs is life-giving oxygen.

q: What is the second-largest city in Lithuania?
e: While busy Vilnius takes first place, lovely Kaunas proudly sparkles as Lithuania's second-biggest city, hugging two meeting rivers.

q: What type of earthquake wave is associated with ground roll?
e: Rayleigh waves roll along the ground just like giant ocean waves, making the surface wobble like jelly.

q: An unpowered open truck is coasting horizontally with a constant velocity along a frictionless track underneath a grain bin when grain falls vertically into the truck, partly filling it as it moves along. Which of the following will happen to the horizontal momentum of the truck with the accumulating grain?
a: It will first increase and then decrease
e: Because the grain falls straight down without pushing sideways, the truck's horizontal momentum stays exactly the same.

q: The emblem on the flag of the Republic of Tajikistan features a sunrise over mountains below what symbol?
e: High above the glowing mountain sunrise, a royal golden crown shines right at the center of Tajikistan's flag.

q: Which of the following sedimentary rocks has a clastic composition?
e: Shale is clastic because it is made of tiny, broken bits of mud squeezed together like a rock sandwich.

q: In a cooling magma chamber, which of the following minerals will crystallize first?
e: In super-hot cooling magma, green olivine crystals form first because they just cannot wait to freeze!

q: Which of the following surfaces has the lowest albedo?
e: The dark ocean absorbs sunlight like a giant blue sponge instead of bouncing it away, giving it the lowest albedo.

q: Scientists at Pacific Northwest National Lab are studying soil. What soil horizon is primarily unweathered bedrock?
e: Deep below your feet rests the R layer, a solid bed of unweathered rock that hasn't broken down yet.

q: Which of the following is NOT a mechanism of physical and chemical weathering?
e: While weathering breaks rocks in place, mass wasting is gravity pulling whole piles of earth downhill on a slide.

q: From 1980 to 2009, 48 weather-related disasters have caused at least 1 billion dollars in economic losses each. Of these 48 instances, the greatest losses have been attributed to which of the following weather disasters?
e: Creeping quietly across vast farmlands, devastating droughts dry up crops and cause the greatest money losses of all.

q: Scientists at Pacific Northwest National Lab are studying humus. What process produces most humus?
e: Tiny underground microbes break down fallen leaves through fermentation, brewing up dark, nutritious humus for plants to enjoy.

q: Which of the following greenhouse gases has the greatest 100-year global-warming potential?
e: Hydrofluorocarbons are champion heat-trappers, holding in far more warmth than other gases over a whole century!

q: Which of the following ways will allow you to increase the capacitance of a parallel-plate capacitor?
a: Decreasing the surface area of each plate
Increasing the charge on the plates
e: Decreasing the space between the plates lets the charges pull on each other more tightly, increasing the capacitor's storage.

q: Which of the following is closest to the average denisty, in grams per cubic centimeter, of Earth's core?
e: Deep down, heavy iron gets squished together super tightly to about 12.8 grams per cubic centimeter inside Earth's core.

q: Which of the following is true about radiometric dating?
a: All parent material in a mineral is converted to the daughter product
When the quantities of parent and daughter products are equal, two half-lives have transpired
The number of radioactive atoms that decay during one half life is always the same
The percentage of radioactive atoms that decay during one half life is always the same
e: Like a dependable clock, the exact percentage of decaying radioactive atoms is always the same during each half-life!

q: Which of the following is NOT a major process for mechanical weathering of rock?
e: Oxidation uses oxygen to chemically rust rocks, making it chemical weathering rather than mechanical cracking.

q: Scientists at Los Alamos National Lab are measuring the positron flux in Earth's upper atmosphere. Which of the following is NOT TRUE concerning positrons?
a: They can interact with electrons to generate two gamma rays
e: Positrons are already tiny and light, so they cannot decay into heavier particles called muons.

q: Which of the following best describes the tectonic location of a passive continental margin?
e: Passive margins sit snoozing safely inside a plate's quiet interior, miles away from the rumbling edges where plates crash together.

q: Which of the following components is the greatest contributor to no-load losses on transformers?
a: Eddy current losses in the core laminations
Heat losses due to no-load current
e: Even when resting, a transformer works hard flipping its tiny magnetic bits back and forth, making hysteresis the biggest energy waster.

q: Which of the following pairs of metamorphic rocks both result from the parent rock shale?
e: When cozy mud shale gets squished, it becomes slate, and when toasted by magma, it bakes into tough hornfels!

q: Which of the following minerals occurs in small amounts in many igneous rocks, is black and shiny, often occurs in small hexagonal blocks, and is soft with good cleavage:
e: Biotite is the glittery black mineral that loves to peel apart into neat, shiny little sheets inside bubbly volcanic rock.

q: Which of the following is NOT true of isotherms:
a: they are more widely spaced over the equatorial regions
they are more closely spaced over North America in the summer than in the winter
they tend to be linear in form in the Southern Hemisphere south of 40 latitude
they are lines that connect places with the same average temperature
e: Temperature lines actually bunch up tighter in chilly winter, because freezing north winds clash dramatically with warm southern breezes.

q: Which of the following internal layers of the Earth allows for isostacy [eye-SOS-tuh-see] of the crust?
e: The asthenosphere is like warm, gooey taffy, letting Earth's heavy crust float and bob comfortably on top.

q: Cayes [KAYS] are small sandy islands formed on the surface of coral reefs in tropical areas like the coast of Belize. The sand on these cayes is primarily composed of which of the following?
e: These sunny beaches are made of calcium carbonate, built from countless tiny sea shells and crushed coral skeletons.

q: Which of the following statements is true about the Andes mountains?
a: They are near a spreading center
They are found along a transform boundary
e: Deep underground, sinking ocean rock melts into magma, feeding the mighty line of smoking volcanoes that built the Andes.

q: What is the most populous Muslim-majority nation in 2010?
e: Spread across thousands of sunny islands, Indonesia is home to the world's biggest community of Muslim families.

q: Which of the following minerals are present in pelitic rocks, resulting from the metamorphism of aluminous sedimentary rocks such as shales and mudrocks?
e: Sphalerite grains form inside these ancient squeezed mudrocks as rich mineral soups bake under deep, toasty Earth pressures.

q: Which of the following BEST describes a fold in a layered rock that arches into a downward, trough-shaped fold:
e: A syncline is like Earth smiling, bending giant rock layers downward into a cozy, bowl-shaped trough.

q: What type of mass wasting event is created when many different sediment sizes channelize and begin to move in a fluidized mass down slope?
e: A debris flow rushes downhill like a messy, wet river, carrying everything from tiny pebbles to giant boulders together!

q: Which of these is NOT true about ultramafic rock?
a: The Earth's mantle is composed of ultramafic rock
Ultramafic rocks are usually dark colored
Ultramafic rock crystallizes at higher temperatures than felsic rock
Andesite is a type of ultramafic rock
e: Andesite is actually an intermediate rock from volcanic arcs, not an ultramafic rock from Earth's deep mantle.

q: Which of the following is a rock that is commonly made of microscopic shells:
e: Limestone is built like a secret castle, made from billions of tiny sea creatures' shells piled on the ocean floor.

q: In the early stages of formation, river valleys exhibit which of the following characteristics?
e: Eager young rivers carve straight down into the bedrock, cutting sharp V-shapes before they slow down and widen.

q: Frost wedging or freeze-thaw weather is most prominent in which of the following locations?
e: Chicago constantly hops above and below freezing, letting water melt into cracks and freeze to split rocks wide open!

q: The San Andreas Fault and collision of India with Asia occurred in what geologic period?
e: During the Oligocene, Earth threw a giant party where India crashed into Asia and the famous San Andreas Fault cracked awake.

q: What is the name of the Canadian national anthem?
e: With voices lifted high across snowy forests, Canadians proudly sing O Canada to celebrate their sweeping, beautiful homeland!

q: In which of the following locations would you typically expect the average salinity of surface sea water to be the HIGHEST:
a: at the mouth of the Mississippi River
in the waters above the Arctic Circle
e: Under the hot sun, water quickly evaporates from the landlocked Dead Sea, leaving behind heaps of super salty water!

q: According to Bowen's reaction series, which of the following minerals would crystallize at the highest temperature?
e: Olivine is the toughest mineral kid on the block, crystallizing first out of magma when it is scorchingly hot!

q: What will likely happen to the amount of dissolved oxygen in a river downstream of a tributary that brings sewage effluent?
a: The amount of oxygen will be depleted
The amount of oxygen will stay the same
More oxygen will diffuse into the water
e: Hungry little bacteria gobble up the messy sewage and gulp down all the river's dissolved oxygen, leaving the poor fish gasping.

q: Much of Tibet lies in altitudes above 17,000 feet. At such altitudes, which of the following best approximates the percentage of the atmosphere below the Tibetans?
e: High up where clouds tickle your toes, Earth's cozy blanket of air thins out so much that half of it is resting below you.

q: Continental margins facing the edges of diverging tectonic plates are called:
e: Since these peaceful coastlines drift away from plate collisions without any grumpy earthquakes, scientists call them passive margins.

q: Which of the following is NOT true about Earth's water:
a: more fresh water exists underground than in streams and lakes
the total amount of water in the global system varies greatly from year to year
ground water can take thousands or millions of years to recharge naturally
a rock is permeable if water can pass through it
e: Earth is a master recycler, endlessly swirling the very same water around, so the total amount never wildly changes from year to year.

q: Which of these cities is NOT in England?
e: Castle-topped Edinburgh does not sit in England at all; it proudly serves as the historic capital of neighboring Scotland!

q: An electroscope is negatively charged, with the leaves at an angle of about 45. When a negatively charged rod is slowly brought near the plate of the electroscope, the leaves do which of the following?
e: Like charges are shy and push away! The extra negative energy scampers down into the metal leaves, making them repel each other even more.

q: Which of the following is not a unit used by oceanographers to describe sea water salinity?
e: A siemen actually measures how easily electricity zips through water, not the salty pinch of the ocean itself.

q: Which of the following steps in atoll formation is the most mature?
e: After an old volcano sinks beneath the waves, only a glowing, peaceful lagoon inside a coral ring remains at the very end.

q: The key glacier structure formed through annual layering of ice through cycles of melting and snowfall is called what?
e: Just like frosting on a birthday cake, fresh snow stacks into neat yearly layers called primary stratification as the glacier grows.

q: Which of the following is a major concern introduced with demand response programs and smart grids in general:
a: Increased flow of energy in distribution and power systems.
Decrease in system reliability due to intermittency of generation of renewable energy sources
Increased rates of cost of electricity
Hackers can gain access to smart grid control software
e: Connecting our city's power to smart computers helps save energy, but sneaky hackers might try to break into the controls.

q: Which of the following is a sedimentary rock that forms as a result of precipitation during evaporation of seawater?
e: When the hot sun drinks up shallow seawater, leftover minerals sparkle and clump together to build soft gypsum rock.

q: Under which of the following circumstances does ocean depth affect ocean wave motion?
a: When ocean depth falls below half the wavelength of a wave
When the ocean wave has a period exceeding 20 seconds
When the ocean waves are impacted by tides
When the ocean floor has high relief, regardless of the depth
e: Waves drag their watery toes on the seafloor as soon as the water gets shallower than half their wavelength!

q: Which of the following is NOT true regarding seismic waves through the Earth:
a: P-waves travel through the outer core
S-waves travel through the outer core
e: S-waves are strictly solid lovers—they completely stop and cannot swim through Earth's melty, liquid outer core.

q: Which of the following types of lava flows results when a volcano erupts underwater?
e: Chilly ocean water quickly cools the sizzling magma into smooth, puffy stone cushions known as pillow lava.

q: Which of the following types of rock is likely to cap a layer of rock rich in oil?
e: Tightly squished shale acts like a tight lid, trapping wandering oil underground so it cannot escape.

q: Which of the following is closest to the top speed, in miles per hour, of a tsunami?
e: Out in deep water, these giant waves can zoom along at six hundred miles per hour, just like a roaring jetliner!

q: Which of the following statements is NOT true about the Gulf of Maine?
a: A gyre [JYUHR] circulates nutrients and pollution through the Gulf
It is among the deepest gulfs in the world
It is sub-arctic, but has a wide range in water temperature
e: While it is packed with lively sea creatures, the Gulf of Maine sits on a shallow shelf and is definitely not super deep.

q: What is the name for the type of mass wasting in which perpendicular forces due to freeze-thaw processes in the ground cause soil to lift upwards?
e: When freezing underground ice expands, it gives the sleepy soil a chilly upward shove called frost heave.

q: Which of the following composes most of the insoluble residues of limestones?
e: When rainwater washes limestone away, tough silica lumps called chert nodules stubbornly refuse to dissolve and stay behind.

q: A 500 kilogram roller coaster car rounds the top of a hill with a radius of 25 meters at a speed of 15 meters per second. Given that the acceleration due to gravity is 10 meters per second squared, what is the normal force in newtons on the car at this point?
e: Gravity pulls down with five thousand newtons, but your speedy swoop flings you up, leaving just five hundred newtons pushing from the track.

q: What radioactive element was produced during nuclear-weapons testing in the mid 1900s and is commonly used by oceanographers to date the age of water masses, but will decay to normal background levels in the coming decades.
e: Tritium hitched a ride into our oceans during bomb tests, acting like a ticking stopwatch that helps scientists tell how old water is.

q: Which of the following BEST explains why Mono Lake in California is hypersaline:
a: it has no outlet and a high evaporation rate
it is subject to extreme saltwater intrusion emanating from a vast system of underground aquifers
it is underlain by massive salt domes formed 250 million years ago
it has been subjected to periodic eruptions of volcanic ash
e: Thirsty sunshine drinks up the lake's water, but with no river exit, all the salty minerals get left behind.

q: Which of the following is a sedimentary rock?
e: Shale is made from quiet layers of squishy mud that cuddled together over millions of years until they turned into solid rock.

q: Which of the following pairs of tectonic [tek-TAWN-ik] plates does NOT constitute a primarily convergent boundary?
e: Instead of crashing together in a giant hug, the Pacific and Antarctic plates are actually drifting apart like polite dancing partners.

q: The core of the Earth is primarily made of iron and which additional element?
e: Deep down at Earth's cozy center, iron has a heavy metal best friend named nickel, and together they make our spinning core.

q: Which of the following rocks is most effective at neutralizing acid rain?
e: Limestone acts like an upset-tummy tablet for nature, using its calming minerals to fizz away the bite of grumpy acid rain.

q: Which of the following is NOT used as evidence for plate tectonic theory?
a: Deposition of glacial dropstones in Australian bedrock
Elevation and increased heat flow at the Mid-Atlantic Ridge
Correlation of fossils between Africa and South America
Successively deeper earthquakes at the Peru-Chili trench
e: Glacial stones trapped in one spot just show it was chilly there, not that giant continents were scooting across the globe.

q: What intermediate age radiotracer used by the Pacific Northwest National Laboratories allows scientists to better date groundwater between 50 and 1000 years old?
e: Argon-39 is like a gentle hourglass gas, ticking at just the right speed to tell the age of hidden underground water.

q: A rock sequence is gradually covered in sedimentary layers, causing an increase in the confining pressure, increasing the temperature to 200 degrees Celsius, and leading to the formation of zeolite minerals. Which of the following best describes this type of metamorphism?
e: Piled under heavy blankets of sand and mud, this rock got squished and warmed in a cozy process called burial metamorphism.

q: Only one country in the world starts with the letter Q.
e: This is true! Sunny Qatar stands all by itself on the world map as the only country starting with the letter Q.

q: Eddy currents are circular electric currents induced by a changing magnetic field within conductors. Which of the following is NOT an application that utilizes eddy currents?
a: Detecting counterfeit bills in vending machines
e: Swirling eddy currents only play with metal, so paper money slips past them without creating any electric loops at all.

q: In which of the following sedimentary environments would a dominantly organic sedimentary rock most likely be formed?
e: Sunny, shallow seas are bursting with happy sea critters whose leftover shells pile up into thick, organic rock blankets.

q: Which of these countries is NOT a part of the Asian continent?
e: Suriname actually lives far across the Atlantic Ocean in South America, tucked under a blanket of lush green rainforests.

q: Assuming that 1 atmosphere = 1.01 105 pascals and the density of water is 1000 kilograms per cubic meter, at what depth of water will the absolute pressure be 10.8 times the atmospheric pressure?
e: Diving 101 meters down stacks so much heavy water on top of you that the ocean presses down over ten times harder.

q: Which country is completely landlocked by South Africa?
e: Mountainous little Lesotho sits tucked snugly inside giant South Africa, like a hidden treasure wrapped entirely in a warm geographic hug.

q: What is the minimum temperature difference, in degrees Celsius, needed to develop an ocean thermal energy conversion system?
e: To make ocean power, the warm, sunlit surface needs to be at least twenty degrees hotter than the chilly depths below.

q: A poikiloblastic [poi-kil-uh-BLAS-tik] texture is characterized by which of the following?
a: Idioblasts embedded within a fine matrix
Homogeneously [hoh-muh-JEE-nee-uhs-li] xenoblastic with little to no evidence of additional alteration minerals
Fine, phyllitic [fi-LIT-ik] foliation accompanied by porphyroblasts [por-FI-roh-blasts]
Inclusions from other minerals enveloped during porphyroblast growth
e: As a big crystal grows, it scoops up smaller mineral neighbors like chocolate chips trapped inside a giant cookie.

q: Which of these African countries displays a gun on their flag?
e: Mozambique placed a rifle on its bright, colorful flag to remember the brave struggle for its independence.

q: According to Bowen's reaction series, which of these minerals is the first to crystallize in cooling magma?
e: In the super-hot magma kitchen, calcium-rich plagioclase is the very first mineral to freeze into shape before the others even start.

q: What is the capital of Mauritius?
e: Port Louis is the cheerful harbor town that serves as the sunny capital of the island of Mauritius.

q: Which of the following is the most important feature characterizing the stratosphere?
e: High above the clouds, friendly ozone gas gathers to wrap Earth in invisible sunglasses, soaking up the sun's fiercest rays.

q: Approximately how many meters would global average sea level rise if both the Greenland and Antarctic ice sheets were to completely melt?
e: If all that polar ice melted away, the oceans would swell seventy meters, tall enough to swallow a whole twenty-story building!

q: Which of the following is NOT true about tides?
a: They are long-period waves that move through the oceans in response to forces exerted by the Moon and Sun
They originate in the oceans and progress toward the coastlines
A horizontal movement of water often accompanies the rising and falling of the tide
The weakest currents occur before or near the time of the high and low tides
e: Tides are giant bulges pulled directly across the whole planet at once, not little waves born in the ocean marching toward shore.

q: Which of the following is the most abundant greenhouse gas in the atmosphere?
e: Invisible, floating water vapor is Earth's favorite warm blanket, trapping more cozy heat than any other gas in the sky.

q: Scientists at Oak Ridge National Lab are simulating the breakdown of lignocellulosic [ligno-sellyoo-LOH-sik] biomass in the presence of tetrahydrofuran [tetrah-high-droh- FYOOR-an], or THF. What purpose does THF serve in this reaction?
e: In this lab recipe, THF acts as a helpful solvent, happily dissolving tough plant bits like sugar melting into warm tea.

q: Widmanstatten [WIHD-mahn-STAH-ten] patterns are most commonly found in which of the following objects?
e: When molten iron meteorites cool over millions of chilly space years, their metal forms these gorgeous, crisscrossing crystal ribbons.

q: What type of mineral composes the green sand beaches that are found in the state of Hawaii?
e: Hawaii's volcanoes sneeze out crushed lava crystals of shiny green olivine, tumbling down to turn the whole beach into sparkling emerald sand!

q: Which of the following is a renewable, primary energy source?
e: Deep underground, Earth's fiery belly brews endless heat, giving us clean, renewable geothermal energy straight from nature's giant kettle.

q: Which of the following is closest to the average speed of the Earth's tectonic [tek-TAWN-ik] plates in centimeters of relative motion per year?
e: Giant slabs of our planet creep along at just three centimeters a year, traveling no faster than your own fingernails grow!

q: Long after ocean crust is formed and transported away from the mid-ocean ridge, the crust will become more dense and sink lower into the mantle. Which of the following is primarily responsible for this effect?
e: As hot ocean crust drifts away, it cools down and shivers, packing its rock tightly together until it gets heavy and sinks.

q: The inner core of the Earth is most similar in composition to which of the following?
e: Earth's solid heart is packed with nickel and iron, matching the exact recipe found inside space-traveling meteoric iron.

q: Which of the following major wind belts occurs between 0 degrees and 30 degrees North latitude?
e: Blowing faithfully from the northeast toward the warm equator, these trusty trade winds helped ancient sailing ships glide across the seas.

q: What type of high strain metamorphism occurs when two fault blocks rub together, breaking up rock during shearing?
e: When massive rock blocks grind against each other along a fault line, they smash into cataclastic crumbs from pure shearing force.

q: Hurricanes are rated on the Saffir-Simpson Scale. Tornadoes are rated on the Enhanced Fujita Scale. How are these ratings determined?
a: Saffir-Simpson is based on central pressure and Enhanced Fujita is based on damage
Saffir-Simpson is based on wind speed and Enhanced Fujita is based on damage
e: We clock a hurricane's wild wind speeds while it spins, but rate a tornado by inspecting the messy damage left behind.

q: Scientists at Oak Ridge National Lab are studying compounds produced by rhizobial bacteria. These bacteria are typically found associated with the roots of what plants?
e: Friendly rhizobial bacteria cuddle up inside the root bumps of legume plants like peas, sharing nutritious nitrogen with their leafy pals.

q: The only continent without conditions favorable for the formation of tornadoes is
e: Chilly Antarctica is way too cold and dry to brew the warm, humid air clashes that twirling tornadoes need to dance.

q: How is the ratio of oxygen-18 to oxygen-16 useful in serving as a proxy for paleoclimatic [pay-lee-oh-kly-MAH-tik] temperatures in ice-core samples?
a: Oxygen-16 is preferentially stored in ice and only released during warmer periods
Oxygen-16 changes into oxygen-18 at higher temperatures
Oxygen-18 is released from water molecules at higher temperatures
Water with oxygen-18 freezes at lower temperatures than water with oxygen-16
e: Lighter oxygen-16 easily floats into clouds to get locked in ice, only rushing back out when the planet warms up.

q: Surface temperature of the Earth is NOT dependent upon which of the following?
a: Heat loss from the interior of the Earth
e: Earth's deep inner heat barely tickles the surface; our warmth almost entirely comes from sunshine wrapping around the atmosphere outside.

q: Which of the following best explains the dryness of the Atacama desert?
a: It is located in the rain shadow of the Andes
It is primarily located in the horse latitudes
Low pressure over the Pacific prevents raincloud formation
Warm Pacific waters carry away rain clouds
e: The towering Andes mountains cast a huge rain shadow, wringing out clouds so no rain can ever reach the thirsty Atacama.

q: Which of the following is produced by gas-to-particle conversion in the atmosphere?
e: Floating invisible gases can chemically link hands, teaming up to form brand-new solid specks called secondary particulate matter.

q: Which of the following compounds is NOT a common cement in sedimentary rocks?
e: Minerals love sticking sand together like superglue, but Mg2SiO3 never joins the party! It just is not a common rock cement.

q: OTEC is which of the following?
a: A method of producing hydrogen gas using solar energy
A form of tidal energy that harnesses the ebb and flow of ocean water
A method of energy generation from the thermal gradient of ocean waters
e: The ocean makes clean power by playing with temperature! OTEC turns the heat difference between warm surface water and chilly deep water into electricity.

q: In which of the following locations would you expect to find lava with the lowest silica content?
e: Iceland's fiery volcanoes bubble up runny, dark basalt straight from Earth's deep mantle, which naturally holds the very least sticky silica.

q: In which city is the Big Nickel located in Canada?
e: Sudbury, Ontario is so proud of its rich nickel mines that it built a gigantic, shiny coin for everyone to admire!

q: Which of the following coasts parallels a nearby tectonic plate boundary?
e: South America's west coast hugs an active plate edge, where sliding slabs crunch together to push up giant mountains.

q: Santorini is an island belonging to what European Country?
e: Santorini belongs to Greece, gleaming brightly over the sparkling sea with its famous whitewashed cliffs and blue church domes.

q: Which of the following BEST describes a small lake in an arctic environment that is likely to be surrounded by a ring of so-called drunken trees leaning toward the lake:
e: When icy ground melts, the collapsing soil makes a thermokarst lake, tilting the dizzy trees along its rim!

q: Which of the following most directly determines whether a rock will develop foliation during metamorphism?
a: Grain size of primary mineral assemblage
e: When heavy forces squeeze a rock from one special direction, this uneven pressure lines up its minerals into neat stripes.

q: A typical speed for a lithospheric plate is which of the following per year?
e: Earth's giant puzzle pieces creep along at three centimeters a year, about as fast as your fingernails quietly grow!

q: Under the Cascade Mountains, some upwelling magma has cooled below the surface, forming plutons. Which of the following is true of these plutons?
a: They are older than the surrounding bedrock
They are younger than the surrounding bedrock
e: Squeezing into an existing neighborhood makes you the newest kid on the block, so these magma blobs are younger than the rock around them.

q: What quality is represented by isobars when looking at a weather map?
e: Isobars are winding lines that connect spots sharing the exact same air pressure, showing us where breezy winds want to race.

q: Which of the following is true about the Antarctic ice sheet?
a: It covers all land features in Antarctica
It is over 4.2 kilometers thick in some areas
It is approximately 10 times as large in area as the Greenland ice sheet
It is nearly as large as the contiguous U.S.
e: Antarctica wears a frosty white blanket that piles up astonishingly deep, stretching over 4.2 kilometers thick in its deepest spots.

q: What is the largest city and commercial capital of Sri Lanka?
e: Colombo is the giant, energetic port city that keeps Sri Lanka humming with busy markets and seaside cheer.

q: Which of the following is NOT a feature produced by wave erosion?
e: While crashy waves carve away rocky cliffs, a sandy shoal is gently built up when moving water drops its sand.

q: Which of the following minerals does not have cubic cleavage?
e: Calcite loves to break into slanted, diamond-shaped blocks called rhombohedrons, so it never splits into neat little cubes.

q: Scientists at Oak Ridge National Lab are developing methods to deuterate [DOO-tur-ate] benzene. One of their reactions adds four deuterium [doo-TEER-ee-um] atoms to benzene, resulting in what molecule?
e: Benzene has three double bonds, but adding four hydrogen cousins erases two of them, leaving just one bond in cyclohexene!

q: If you were hiking on a glacier in the summertime, which of the following is the BEST way to recognize if you were walking on the zone of accumulation:
a: large amounts of rocks eroded from the nearby mountainsides have accumulated
you were walking mostly on exposed, bare ice
last year's snow is still covering the glacial ice
a bergschrund delineates the start of the accumulation zone
e: High up where glaciers grow, last winter's snow stays cozily tucked in, surviving the summer heat without melting away!

q: Which of the following areas exhibits the highest total relief?
e: Hawaii's giant volcanic mountains start way down on the deep ocean floor, giving them the biggest bottom-to-top height around.

q: Researchers at Oak Ridge National Lab use pulsed laser light to induce thermal stress. This enables them to study the behavior of what type of excitation that plays an important role in many of the physical properties of solids?
e: When heat shakes up a solid, tiny sound ripples jitter through its atoms like a merry dance, creating phonons!

q: Which of the following is NOT a common mineral in igneous rock but rather an accessory that typically occurs in small amounts:
e: Shiny muscovite mica is just a shy guest in most igneous rocks, appearing in tiny pinches rather than huge helpings.

q: In order to replenish the supply of steam at the geothermal plant called The Geysers, which of the following does an underground pipeline deliver?
e: Treated wastewater travels deep underground to touch super-hot rocks, turning our old shower water into clean, whistling steam.

q: Which of the following is NOT true about ocean tides:
a: the Moon's influence on Earth's tides is about 2-times greater than the Sun's influence
a complete tidal day is about 24 hours 50 minutes long
some coastlines have 2 high tides and 2 low tides each lunar day whereas some have only have 1 high tide and 1 low tide each lunar day
spring high tides typically have greater ranges in the Northern Hemisphere during summer than during winter
e: Earth snuggles closest to the sun during winter, which gives winter's spring tides a much bigger gravitational pull than summer ones.

q: Which of the following processes help to form new mountains?
e: Fiery volcanic eruptions stack melted rock and ash higher and higher until a brand-new mountain reaches for the sky.

q: In which country is Tallinn located?
e: Perched right by the sea, the storybook city of Tallinn proudly serves as Estonia's capital.

q: Which of the following best approximates the number of separate cinder cones located on the flanks of Newberry Volcano?
e: This giant volcano wears a bumpy blanket of about four hundred tiny cinder cone hills all across its wide slopes.

q: Tombolos are associated with which of the following?
e: A tombolo is nature's sandy bridge, stretching through the waves to tie a lonely offshore island to the mainland.

q: Which of the following is the age of the most abundant surface bedrock in the Finger Lakes region of New York State?
e: Back in the Devonian period, ancient shallow seas laid down the muddy rock blankets that still cuddle the Finger Lakes today.

q: The "dead zone' that has been occurring off the central Oregon coast since 2002 and recently expanding is thought to be caused by which of the following:
a: toxic sulfur gas from undersea vents
abnormal upwelling processes due to highly variable winds
an increased presence of invasive predatory species
toxic release of waste products from oil refineries
e: Fickle coastal winds trigger unusual upwelling that feeds huge algae blooms, which rot and suffocate the sea into a dead zone.

q: Which of the following rocks is MOST porous:
e: Limestone is like a stony sponge, packed with tiny, secret holes that easily soak up water.

q: Which of the following volcanoes form in ocean- continent and ocean-ocean convergent plate boundaries?
e: When colliding ocean plates dive deep, their melting rock bubbles up to build steep, mighty stratovolcanoes along the edges.

q: If a metamorphic rock was subjected to high temperature and pressure deep in the crust long enough to reach equilibrium with its environment, which of the following would be most useful for determining the temperature and pressure range at which it formed?
e: Different minerals only grow at specific heats and squeezes, acting like tiny name tags that reveal where the rock formed.

q: Which of the following minerals would scratch all of the others?
e: Topaz is the toughest crystal in the bunch, hard enough to scratch all its softer mineral neighbors without a problem.

q: What type of smog in the boundary layer of the atmosphere contains sulfur dioxide?
e: Reducing smog is a gloomy, damp blanket of coal smoke that carries lung-tickling sulfur dioxide through the chilly air.

q: If Earth's axial tilt was 28 in the opposite direction, which of the following would be true?
a: There would be more extreme seasonal variations
The eastern and western hemispheres' seasons would reverse
e: Tilting farther to twenty-eight degrees leans Earth deeper toward the sun and farther away, making our seasons much more extreme.

q: Which of the following is nearest the percentage of the South American continent drained by the Amazon River?
e: Like a giant tree, the Amazon stretches its watery branches across South America to drain forty percent of the whole continent.

q: Severe weather events are most commonly associated with which of the following types of weather front?
e: A chilly cold front bulldozes under warm air, shoving moisture high into the sky to brew up rowdy, severe storms.

q: Which of the following BEST describes the downward movement of typical alpine glaciers:
a: they move by mass wasting and surface creep
they move much like a brick sliding down a board
they flow fastest where the ice is thinnest
they slide along the base and flow like a fluid
e: Heavy alpine ice creeps and flows like slow honey, while wet ground lets its frozen belly slide right downhill.

q: Ouagadougou is the capital of which African country?
e: With its wonderful, bouncy name, Ouagadougou proudly serves as the bustling capital city right at the heart of Burkina Faso.

q: One of the experiments at Brookhaven National Lab, PHENIX, is attempting to measure the temperature of quark-gluon plasma. Which of the following is closest to the known lower limit of this temperature?
a: The temperature of the Sun's chromosphere
The temperature of the Sun's core
2500 times the temperature of the Sun's core
250,000 times the temperature of the Sun's core
e: This particle soup needs unbelievable heat to exist, sizzling at a wild two hundred fifty thousand times the sun's core.

q: Pangaea [pan-JEE-uh] formed by the end of what geologic period?
e: The giant puzzle pieces of land finally locked together to make Pangaea right before the ancient Permian period came to an end.

q: Which of the following best describes where the salt in ocean water comes from?
e: Rain gently tickles mineral salts out of rocks on land, and rushing rivers carry them straight to the ocean's big soup pot!

q: Why was the 2010 Haiti earthquake registered so high on the Mercalli Intensity Scale despite smaller ratings on the Richter and Moment Magnitude scales?
a: The earthquake produced a large tsunami
The initial earthquake was followed by many aftershocks
Haiti is underlain by thrust faults
Haiti has a poorly developed infrastructure
e: The Mercalli scale measures real-world damage, and Haiti's fragile buildings tumbled easily because they were not built strong enough to withstand big shakes.

q: Which of the following pairs of minerals could be contained in the rocks gabbro and granite?
e: Mica and amphibole are versatile mineral buddies that happily squeeze into both dark gabbro rocks and bright granite rocks.

q: Which variable affecting the speed of sound in the ocean dominates at very large depths?
e: Way down in the pitch-black ocean, crushing water pressure squeezes everything so tightly that sound waves zip along faster than ever.

q: Which of the following minerals is a crystalline form of silicon dioxide?
e: When silicon and oxygen lock hands in neat, shiny little patterns, they grow up into sparkling crystals called quartz.

q: Groundwater flows according to what law that, in its simplest form, is given by the equation Q = kIA:
e: Darcy's Law acts like a rulebook, showing how groundwater secretly oozes and trickles through squishy soil and sand.

q: When Oak Ridge National Lab physicists use the term "doubly magic," it describes atomic nuclei [NEW-klee-eye] that have greater stability than their neighbors due to having shells that are fully occupied by both protons and neutrons. What nuclear property is maximized to create this effect?
e: When protons and neutrons pack into neat, complete shells, their nucleon binding energy peaks, gluing the tiny atomic family super tight.

q: Which of the following is a coarse-grained igneous rock primarily containing plagioclase feldspar, amphibole and biotite:
e: Diorite is a speckled rock packed with dark amphibole, biotite, and pale feldspar, looking just like cookies-and-cream ice cream!

q: The wet bulb of a psychrometer [sigh-KRAW-met-er] is used to measure which of the following properties of the atmosphere?
e: That wet cloth chills as water evaporates away, cleverly revealing just how humid the surrounding air really is.

q: Which of the following does NOT represent a potential benefit of smart grids?
a: Facilitation of the use of plug-in hybrids and electric vehicles
e: Smart grids want two-way chatter, so old one-way metering is actually a limitation that holds clean energy back.

q: Which of the following policies allows users with renewable energy sources to sell excess electricity generated to the utility grid and receive compensation?
e: A net metering agreement lets your rooftop solar panels spin the electric meter backward when you share extra sunshine power!

q: As an airmass ascends into the atmosphere, its water vapor capacity changes, causing which of the following?
e: As warm air floats upward, it chills out and drops its extra moisture, huddling together into puffy clouds and rain.

q: What is the term for minerals that are indicators of the metamorphic environment in which the rock was formed?
e: Index minerals act like little detective clues, showing scientists exactly how hot and squished a rock got long ago.

q: Which country was NOT formerly part of Yugoslavia?
e: While its neighbors joined together to form Yugoslavia, independent Albania always marched to the beat of its own drum.

q: Which of the following is NOT a geologic period?
e: The Cenozoic is actually a giant era made of smaller periods, like a whole chapter book instead of just one page.

q: What is the name of rocky region that spans most of eastern Canada?
e: Like a sleeping giant carved of ancient stone, the vast Canadian Shield blankets most of eastern Canada.

q: A mineral with the chemical formula Ca2Mg5Si8O22(OH)2 belongs to which of the following mineral groups?
e: With its recipe of magnesium, calcium, and double-chain silica, this mineral belongs right inside the amphibole family.

q: In a landlocked area with multiple playas and sparse low-lying vegetation, what type of research would best reveal how the local climate has changed over the past several thousand years?
e: Palynology lets scientists hunt for ancient, trapped pollen grains in dry lake mud to see which plants lived there long ago.

q: What is the largest freshwater lake by volume?
e: Lake Baikal is so incredibly deep that it holds more sparkling fresh water than any other lake on Earth.

q: Which of the following typically requires warm, clear, shallow water characterized by low nutrient concentration and a hard coastal substrate to develop:
e: Coral reefs are bustling underwater cities that need bright sunshine, clean shallow water, and hard ground to anchor their colorful homes.

q: How many countries border Kyrgyzstan?
e: High in the clouds, mountainous Kyrgyzstan shares its borders with four close neighbors: China, Kazakhstan, Tajikistan, and Uzbekistan.

q: Suppose a capacitor holds a charge Q and voltage V but is currently NOT connected to a voltage source. If a dielectric with dielectric constant 10 is inserted between the plates, then which of the following is TRUE?
a: The voltage between the plates is multiplied by a factor of 10
The voltage between the plates is multiplied by a factor of 1/10
The charge on the plates is multiplied by a factor of 10
The charge on the plates is multiplied by a factor of 1/10
e: Trapped electric charges cannot escape, but sliding this cozy material inside calms their push down to one-tenth of its original voltage.

q: Which of the following is closest to the mean free path of a nitrogen molecule at room temperature air at sea level?
e: A busy nitrogen molecule zips along, bumping into its friends after traveling just about one hundred nanometers through the air.

q: Which of the following correctly generalizes how crystal size compares between extrusive and intrusive rocks?
a: Extrusive and intrusive rocks have comparable sizes of crystals
Crystal size is variable and unpredictable
e: Deep underground, cozy melted rock cools very slowly, giving sparkly crystals plenty of time to grow big and proud.

q: Which of the following volcanoes in the Cascade Volcanic Arc is a shield volcano?
e: Unlike its pointy neighbors, Newberry gently poured out runny lava to build a giant mound shaped like a warrior's shield.

q: Scientists at Oak Ridge National Lab have designed a particular implementation of a controlled-NOT, or CNOT, gate to enable future work in quantum information processing. In general, if the TARGET qubit is ket 1, which of the following is a transformation that can be performed by the CNOT gate?
a: If the CONTROL qubit is ket 0, the target qubit will remain ket 1
If the CONTROL qubit is ket 0, the target qubit will become ket 0
e: The control switch holds a sleepy zero, meaning it does nothing, so our little target qubit happily stays a one.

q: Which of the following desert landforms is NOT formed through the process of abrasion?
e: Instead of wind scraping rocks down, gentle breezes simply swept away loose sand, leaving behind a neat stone floor called desert pavement.

q: Which of the following is NOT true of an El Nino:
a: when an El Nino is present, fish are less abundant off the west coast of South America
El Ninos typically come along every 4 to 5 years
during a peak El Nino, strong high pressure will be present in the eastern Pacific with lower pressure to the west
El Nino affects global weather patterns
e: During an El Nino, warm ocean water brings stormy low pressure to the eastern Pacific, not a strong high-pressure blanket.

q: Which of the following types of smog in the boundary layer of the atmosphere contains sulfur dioxide?
e: When chilly air traps smokestack fumes full of sulfur dioxide, it brews a gloomy, damp blanket known as reducing smog.

q: Switzerland has four national languages, English being one of them.
e: That is false! Switzerland speaks German, French, Italian, and Romansh, so English is not one of its national languages.

q: What is the capital of Wisconsin, USA?
e: Madison sits snugly between two sparkling lakes, serving as the proud capital city of Wisconsin.

q: What two minerals contribute to the Earth's magnetic field?
e: Deep inside rock, iron oxides and magnetic magnetite team up like tiny compass needles to help build Earth's magnetic shield.

q: Which of these is NOT a real tectonic plate?
e: There is no Atlantic Plate, because that giant ocean floor is carried by other drifting puzzle pieces of the Earth.

q: Which of the following is an ocean current that predominately travels in an EASTERLY direction:
e: Whirling around icy Antarctica, this mighty ocean river gets chased by howling winds, pushing its waters continuously eastward.

q: Which of the following earthquake waves travels the slowest?
e: While other earthquake waves speed ahead, rolling Rayleigh waves take their sweet time, rippling the ground like ocean waves.

q: Approximately what percentage of the Earth's surface is covered by ocean?
e: If you peek down from space, a sparkling blue ocean blanket wraps around roughly seventy percent of our home planet.

q: You find a chunk of granite that you conclude, via radiometric dating, is 3.2 billion years old. The granite also contains inclusions of quartzite. Which of the following is a reasonable conclusion based on this data?
a: The quartzite likely formed less than 3.2 billion years ago
Because the quartzite is contained in the granite, it also formed 3.2 billion years ago
The quartzite likely formed more than 3.2 billion years ago
The sandstone from which the quartzite came is likely older than 3.2 billion years, but the quartzite itself is younger than that
e: Because melted granite swallowed up bits of solid quartzite like chocolate chips in dough, the quartzite had to exist first!

q: When the spent fuel is removed from a nuclear power plant, which of the following immediately occurs?
a: It is placed in dry cask storage at the nuclear reactor site until it is safe to handle, and then it is sent to the permanent storage facility
It is sent to Yucca Mountain to be stored in the National Repository
It is stored under water in a spent fuel pool at the reactor for several years
It is sealed in 50 gallon drums and allowed to cool
e: Freshly used fuel rods are blazing hot, so workers immediately dunk them into deep pools of cool water for a years-long rest.

q: Which of the following geologic eons lasted the longest?
e: The Proterozoic eon was the ultimate champion of patience, stretching across nearly two billion years while early life blossomed.

q: Which of the following surface reservoirs on Earth contains the most carbon?
e: Our vast ocean is Earth's greatest carbon treasure chest, holding far more dissolved carbon than all the soil, plants, or air combined!

q: Which of the following are thought to form the mantle of the Earth:
e: Deep beneath our feet, Earth hugs itself with a thick, iron-rich blanket made of heavy ultramafic rocks.

q: If the magnitude of a magnetic field is multiplied by 4, by what factor is the magnitude of the energy difference E [delta E] between electron states ms = 2T 1 multiplied? 2
e: When the magnetic field flexes four times stronger, the electron's energy gap stretches open four times wider too!

q: Which of the following metamorphic products forms from impact metamorphism?
e: When a speedy meteorite crashes into Earth, its giant crunch squeezes ordinary quartz into an ultra-dense crystal named stishovite.

q: The ocean floor can be mapped by altimeters [all-TIH-meh-durs] on satellites. Which of the following best describes how this method functions?
a: The altimeter maps the ocean surface with radar, which is affected by underlying topography
The altimeter maps the floor using sonar beams attached to the body of the altimeter
The altimeter communicates with an underwater remotely operated vehicle, which maps the ocean floor beneath it
The altimeter communicates with a manned submersible, which maps the ocean floor beneath it
e: Deep underwater mountains pull sea water toward them, creating gentle ocean bumps that satellite radar can map from space.

q: Which of the following changes has NOT contributed to the current warming trend for Earth's atmosphere?
e: Our trusty sun has kept shining at a steady pace, so incoming solar energy is not driving today's warming fever.

q: Consider two beaches, both with source material from the same granitic mountains. The beach located further from the mountains would have:
e: On their long river adventure, traveling pebbles get polished and tumbled into fine, rounded, light-colored sand grains.

q: What is the name of the formerly rich fishing grounds off the island of Newfoundland, Canada?
e: The foggy Grand Banks off Newfoundland were once bursting with so many codfish that sailors could practically scoop them up!

q: What country is not a part of Scandinavia?
e: Finland is a lovely Nordic neighbor, but Scandinavia officially belongs only to Norway, Sweden, and Denmark.

q: Which of the following is the soil horizon that contains a mixture of organic matter and highly altered mineral matter and is dark in color:
e: Right near the surface, the dark A-horizon happily blends crumbled minerals with rich old leaves to feed hungry plants.

q: If a climate report shows the difference in surface air pressure between the Azores and Iceland, what phenomenon is it measuring?
e: Air pressure plays a breezy see-saw between Iceland and the Azores, a dance we call the North Atlantic Oscillation.

q: Which of the following is a ubiquitous trace mineral found in many igneous, metamorphic and clastic sedimentary rocks, and has been used to date Earth's oldest rocks at 4-plus billion years:
e: Tiny, tough zircon crystals survive billions of years like little time capsules, telling tales of Earth's very first birthdays.

q: What year is on the flag of the US state Wisconsin?
e: Wisconsin stitched 1848 onto its flag to celebrate the wonderful year it officially became a US state!

q: Which of the following best explains why eliminating one trophic level in an ecosystem often results in a decrease in organisms two trophic levels down?
a: Abundance of prey in the eliminated trophic level
Increased predation by organisms one trophic level down
Increased predation by organisms two trophic levels down
e: Without top hunters on patrol, middle predators throw a party, booming in number and eating the creatures down below.

q: A rock on the end of a string is being swung in a circle above a child's head. The string breaks. Neglecting gravity, in what direction does the acceleration of the rock now point?
a: Inwards towards the center of the circle
Outwards away from the center of the circle
e: Once the string snaps, nothing is tugging the rock anymore, so its acceleration instantly becomes zero.

q: What is the land connecting North America and South America?
e: The Isthmus of Panama acts like a skinny bridge of land, holding two giant continents together in a warm embrace!

q: What coordinate is the celestial-sphere equivalent of latitude?
e: Just like latitude maps lines north and south on Earth, declination guides stargazers up and down across the sky.

q: Where is Timbuktu located?
e: Timbuktu sits like an ancient treasure chest full of stories, tucked right into the warm desert sands of Mali, Africa.

q: Which of the following rocks would most likely be created within a fluvial environment?
e: A bustling river tumbles smooth pebbles together and glues them into a chunky rock called conglomerate.

q: Which of the following is an example of a plate boundary that may have both deep- and shallow-focus earthquakes?
e: When an ocean plate dives deep under a continent, it grinds along, triggering both shallow rumbles and super-deep quakes.

q: A group of small volcanoes, called the petit spot volcanoes, was recently found. What makes this find so unusual is they are believed to be formed:
a: from asthenosphere material squeezing through cracks caused by bending in Earth's crust
from plumes rising rapidly from the boundary between Earth's core and mantle
e: As the seafloor bends, tiny cracks pop open, letting gooey mantle magma squeeze through like toothpaste to build these volcanoes.

q: In which of the following locations is oceanic crust converging with oceanic crust:
e: Deep underwater, two ocean plates play bumper cars, crumpling together to push up the foggy Aleutian Islands.

q: What layer of the Earth's atmosphere varies in depth with the time of day and reflects radio waves long distances?
e: The sun tickles the ionosphere by day, puffing it up so it can bounce secret radio tunes right around the world!

q: Which of the following is igneous and pyroclastic in nature, and is of variable composition:
e: When an erupting volcano sneezes out hot ash and gravel, all that mixed-up stuff glues together into a rock called tuff.

q: Which of the following processes created the volcano Mount Nyiragongo [nee-ira-gong-oh] in the Democratic Republic of Congo?
e: Africa is slowly unzipping, and this continental rifting tore the ground open so Mount Nyiragongo could rumble awake.

q: The United States has the highest frequency of tornado occurrences of the world's nations. To the nearest order of magnitude, how many tornadoes touch down in the United States each year?
e: Every single year, about one thousand dizzy windstorms touch down across the United States, twirling like giant tops.

q: Which of the following rock types would be from the depositional environment with the lowest energy?
e: In quiet, sleepy waters where currents barely nudge a thing, tiny bits of mud gently drift down to build siltstone.

q: Which of the following is a characteristic of an intrusive, igneous rock?
e: Deep underground, cozy magma cools like molasses, giving its minerals lots of time to grow into big interlocking crystals.

q: The source of energy that drives a tsunami wave onto a shore originated:
a: From the gravitational attraction between the Earth and the Moon
e: A tsunami gets its giant shove from deep inside Earth's rumbling belly, where sudden shakes toss the whole ocean upward.

q: Which of the following types of volcanic eruptions is distinguished primarily by its eruption of basaltic and andesitic magma from its vent, producing incandescent bombs that fall near the vent, eventually building a small cone of tephra:
e: Strombolian eruptions pop like glowing fireworks, tossing fiery molten blobs that stack up into a neat little cone.

q: Which of the following locations has the highest annual productivity driven by coastal upwelling?
a: North America, along the eastern coast of Maine
Africa, along the northern coast of Egypt
South America, along the southeastern coast of Brazil
Asia, along the western coast of India
e: Chilly, nutrient-rich waters bubble up along Maine's coast, feeding massive crowds of hungry sea critters all year long!

q: What two layers of the atmosphere have the least influence over weather?
e: The mesosphere and thermosphere float way too high and thin above us to stir up our daily rain and snow.

q: Based on current scientific data, the most widely accepted cause of past ice ages is which of the following?
a: Volcanic aerosols in the atmosphere from major eruptions
Increased absorption of carbon dioxide by the oceans and land masses
A decrease in solar intensity such as during the Maunder Minimum
e: Earth wobbles like a spinning top as it orbits, and these Milankovitch cycles slowly tipped our world into chilly ice ages.

q: Which of the following is considered the principal volcanic gas:
e: When a fiery volcano opens wide to burp, most of that steamy breath is actually plain old water vapor!

q: Which of the following statements is TRUE of lateral and medial moraines [mah-RAYNS]?
a: A lateral moraine is a type of medial moraine
A medial moraine is a type of lateral moraine
Two lateral moraines can merge to form a medial moraine
Medial moraines are only present at the maximum extent of a glacier, while lateral moraines are present along the entirety of a glacier's flow path.
e: When two icy glaciers meet for a hug, their dusty side edges join right in the middle to make a medial moraine.

q: Which of the following is NOT true about geothermal gradients?
a: The gradient beneath continent crust is less steep than under oceanic crust
They are largely determined by the way that pressure and temperature vary in the Earth
The "normal" geothermal gradient in the upper part of Earth is 25C/km [twenty-five degrees Celsius per kilometer]
e: Continental crust actually warms up more quickly with depth than ocean floors do, making this statement totally backward.

q: Which of the following minerals is not a carbonate?
e: Pretty purple fluorite is built from calcium and fluorine, completely skipping the carbon and oxygen ingredients that carbonate minerals must have.

q: What ocean water mass has the oldest carbon-14 age, meaning it has spent the most time isolated from the atmosphere?
e: North Pacific Deep Water takes an epic ocean journey, hiding in the dark so long it has the oldest carbon-14 age.

q: Which of the following is NOT true of basalt and gabbro:
a: they formed from magma at the same temperature
they are derived from basaltic magma
they formed from magma with the same silica content
they are both intrusive igneous rocks
e: Gabbro stays underground to cool, but basalt escapes to the surface as lava, so they cannot both be intrusive rocks.

q: Consider the track of the 2005 Hurricane Katrina. Alabama's Dauphin Island suffered more extreme damage than other islands exposed to the storm. Based on the nature of hurricanes, what quadrant of the storm pounded Dauphin Island?
e: Spinning counterclockwise, a hurricane packs its fiercest winds and highest waves in its northeast corner, clobbering Dauphin Island the hardest.

q: Plate divergence is responsible for all of the following formations, EXCEPT:
e: Instead of plates pulling apart, plates crashed together here, piling up the Indonesian Islands through fierce subduction.

q: According to the US Energy Information Administration, which of the following is closest to the percentage of worldwide electricity produced using renewable sources in 2011?
e: Back in 2011, green energy like spinning wind and tumbling water powered about twenty percent of our world's buzzing lights!

q: Which of the following types of volcanic vents creates wide-spread basalt deposits called flood basalts?
e: Giant cracks called fissures opened wide, letting runny lava spill out like pancake batter to pave huge flood basalts.

q: Orthoclase feldspar primarily weathers by which of the following processes to form clay minerals:
e: Water gently sips and reacts with hard feldspar rocks through hydrolysis, softening them right into squishy, moldable clay.

q: When a strong south wind occurs along the west coast of North America, Ekman transport causes water to move to which of the following?
e: When winds blow from the south, Earth's spin steers the traveling waves to the right, pushing ocean water straight onshore toward the beach!

q: How does the Sound Fixing and Ranging (SOFAR) channel support our study of climate change?
a: The deep SOFAR channel is populated with organisms extremely sensitive to ocean temperature change
World War II submarines gathered rich and extensive data sets about the SOFAR channel that can be compared with current data
Video monitoring of marine mammal mating behavior is useful because mating behavior in this region is impacted by temperature
Speed of sound is temperature-dependent in the SOFAR channel
e: Sound zips through warm water faster than cold water, so listening to deep ocean echoes tells scientists how much the sea is warming up.

q: When spreading centers reach above the ocean's surface, they typically form which of the following types of volcanoes:
e: When runny lava oozes gently from spreading seafloor cracks, it builds wide, gently sloping shield volcanoes shaped just like a warrior's fallen shield.

q: In which of the following lakes in North America would you typically find a thriving community of halophiles and alkaliphiles:
e: California's Mono Lake is super salty and bubbly with baking-soda minerals, making it paradise for tough little microbes that love alkaline water!

q: What country used 100% renewable energy for 75 consecutive days in 2015?
e: Costa Rica's gushing rivers and steaming volcanoes worked overtime in 2015, powering the whole country cleanly for seventy-five sunny days straight.

q: Where is the city of Haarlem located?
e: Haarlem is a lovely old town tucked among the famous windmills and blooming tulip fields of the Netherlands.

q: The evolution of oxygenic photosynthesis marked a significant change in Earth history that led to permanent changes in the redox state of Earth's atmosphere and had lasting impacts on Earth's organisms. Which of the following best describes when the evolution of oxygenic photosynthesis occurred relative to the Cambrian Explosion?
a: One billion years after the Cambrian Explosion
The same time as the Cambrian Explosion
Two billion years before the Cambrian Explosion
Three billion years before the Cambrian Explosion
e: Tiny bacteria puffed out oxygen two billion years before the Cambrian explosion, baking the air long before complex critters arrived to breathe it.

q: Which of the following is the name given to soil that forms over millions of years from weathering of crystalline bedrock?
e: Just like a wise old tree, soil that spends millions of peaceful years slowly growing from bedrock is called mature soil.

q: What must be the capacitance in farads of a capacitor storing 10 joules of energy and having 1 volt potential difference between its plates?
e: To pack ten whole joules of spark into just one volt, this little energy vault needs a capacitance of twenty farads!

q: In what part of Wales will you find the village Llanfairpwllgwyngyllgogerychwyrndrobwllllantysiliogogogoch?
e: This wonderfully tongue-twisting village makes its home on the lovely Welsh island of Anglesey.

q: Why did Charles Keeling's carbon dioxide graphs show an up and down pattern each year?
a: More carbon dioxide was generated by heating processes during the winter
The air is denser in the winter, causing carbon dioxide to become diluted
Carbon dioxide is absorbed during the growth season and released through decay during the fall and winter
Warmer summer continents release more carbon dioxide than during colder winters
e: Earth breathes in carbon dioxide as leafy trees bloom in spring, then breathes it back out when fallen leaves crumble in winter.

q: Scientists at Oak Ridge National Lab have designed a fuel rod cladding alloy made of iron, chromium, and aluminum to replace current zirconium alloys. Which of the following must be a property of this cladding?
a: Converts fast neutrons into thermal neutrons
Converts thermal neutrons into fast neutrons
e: The metal jacket must have a low neutron cross-section so zooming nuclear particles can slip right past without getting trapped inside.

q: Which of the following is the most abundant sediment in the oceans?
e: Mud and sand washed from dry land—called terrigenous sediment—make up the biggest pile of cozy blankets on the seafloor.

q: Southeasterly tradewinds in the Indian Ocean, near the tropical convergence zone, become which of the following type of winds due to the Coriolis Effect?
e: As wandering southeast winds cross into the northern hemisphere, Earth's gentle spin curves them right into gusty southwest breezes.

q: Which of the following represents a metasomatic change from a protolith?
e: When boiling fluids cook limestone and inject fresh minerals into it, the rock magically transforms into a brand-new treasure called skarn!

q: The Philippines formed from tectonic activity at which of the following plate boundary types?
e: Two heavy ocean plates crashed into each other, pushing underwater volcanoes up until they peeked out as the sunny Philippine islands.

q: As the Atlantic Ocean began to open around 200 million years ago, which of the following regions was most directly adjacent to the crust that now underlies the eastern margin of the United States?
e: Long ago, the United States was snuggled right against northwest Africa like two puzzle pieces before the Atlantic Ocean drifted between them.

q: To produce better containment vessels for commercial fusion power, scientists at Oak Ridge National Lab are working with what material that has the highest melting point of all metals?
e: Super-tough tungsten laughs at fiery heat, boasting the highest melting point of all metals to bottle up wild fusion energy.

q: Which of the following natural phenomena are associated with a patterned seasonal occurrence that ranges from May 15 to November 30?
e: Right on schedule every May 15 to November, the East Pacific waters wake up to spin giant, blustery hurricanes across the sea.

q: Which of the following is the BEST example of a non-point source pollution:
a: chemical spills at a mining site
e: Rain washes farm fertilizer across miles of open fields, making this runoff impossible to pin down to a single leaky spot.

q: Which of the following ocean currents does NOT flow from higher latitudes toward the equator?
e: Instead of swimming toward the warm equator, the Brazil Current flows south toward colder polar seas.

q: Mount Vesuvius in Italy is a typical:
e: Mount Vesuvius is a composite volcano, stacked high like a giant layer cake made of hardened ash and fiery lava.

q: Felsic rocks are rich in silicate, while mafic rocks are rich in iron. Which of the following rock types would be felsic?
e: Granite is packed full of pale, glass-like silicates, making this speckled rock a classic member of the felsic family.

q: At the National Renewable Energy Lab, scientists are using sunlight to split what chemical compound during photoelectrochemical processes that employ stacks of light-absorbing semiconductors immersed in an acid-water solution?
e: Sunlight acts like tiny scissors, snipping everyday water molecules apart to free clean hydrogen fuel.

q: The mountainous Khyber Pass connects which of the two following countries?
e: The rugged Khyber Pass carves a winding secret doorway straight through giant mountains, connecting Afghanistan and Pakistan.

q: Walden Pond in Massachusetts is a famous example of a kettle lake. What created Walden pond?
a: A meander cut off to form a lake
e: A slow-moving glacier buried a giant ice block here long ago, which melted into a cozy kettle lake.

q: Which of the following best describes surface airflow in a northern hemisphere middle-latitude cyclone?
e: In northern storms, winds squeeze inward together while spinning counterclockwise like a giant, swirling carousel.

q: Which soil horizon is likely to have the most organic material?
e: The topmost O horizon sits right beneath our feet, packed with fallen leaves and rich, crumbly organic goodness.

q: The Earth's core contains approximately one-third of the Earth's mass. Which of the following percentages is closest to the percentage of the core's mass that is contained within the outer core?
e: Earth's liquid outer core is so enormous that it hogs ninety-five percent of the core's total heavy mass.

q: Where do the strongest winds in Antarctica, which can reach 200 miles per hour, originate?
e: Freezing air heaps up high on the Antarctic polar plateau, then tumbles downhill into wild two-hundred-mile-an-hour winds!

q: Which of the following rankings of U.S. states by highest frequency of earthquakes (highest to lowest) is accurate?
e: Shake-happy Alaska rattles the most often, followed in line by California, Nevada, and calm Oregon.
