q: Ultramafic [ultra-MAY-fik] magma is slowly cooling. Which of the following minerals will crystalize out first?
e: Sparkling green olivine is the eager early bird, crystallizing first while the scorching magma is still crazy hot.

q: Which of the following uses would NOT be appropriate for class A biosolids?
a: Alternative daily cover at a landfill
e: Organic farms have super strict rules that say no to using treated sewage fertilizers.

q: In soil taxonomy, which of the following is a leached acidic soil rich in iron oxides and aluminum and typically found in the Eastern U.S. and Canada under forest landscapes:
e: Named for aluminum and iron, pedalfer soils soak in rainy eastern forests to become wonderfully rich and acidic.

q: Ocean thermal energy conversion systems convert solar radiation to electric power. Which of the following describes the source of energy in ocean thermal energy conversion systems?
a: The difference in temperatures between surface and deep waters
e: These systems make electricity by pairing sun-warmed surface waves with icy-cold deep ocean water.

q: Bir Tawil, an uninhabited track of land claimed by no country, is located along the border of which two countries?
e: Tucked right between Egypt and Sudan, this quiet patch of desert sand is surprisingly claimed by neither neighbor.

q: Which of the following types of sedimentary rock is never formed through biochemical processes?
e: Halite is simple rock salt born purely from dried-up salty water, without any help from living creatures.

q: The analysis of which of the following fossil types from ancient vertebrates provides important information about the diet and biota of ancient environments?
e: Coprolite is actually fossilized dinosaur poop, which lovingly preserves whatever ancient snacks a critter munched on!

q: Which of the following will NOT help crystallize magma?
a: Removing water to raise the melting point
e: Magma needs to cool down to freeze into crystals, so turning up the heat keeps it melted like gooey soup!

q: The Spallation Neutron Source at Oak Ridge National Lab is used to study material properties. Which of the following best describes neutron spallation?
a: High-energy protons collide with a nucleus, which then emits neutrons
High-energy neutrons collide with a nucleus, which then emits protons
Low-energy neutrons are absorbed by a nucleus, which splits and emits neutrons
High-energy neutrons are absorbed by a nucleus, which splits and emits neutrons
e: Speedy protons smash into an atom's heart like tiny bowling balls, knocking a burst of neutrons right out!

q: Which of the following is a medium or coarse-grained rock that consists primarily of plagioclase feldspar and pyroxene and is essentially the plutonic equivalent of basalt:
e: Deep underground, the same melted rock that makes basalt cools very slowly, growing chunky crystals into gabbro.

q: Which of the following types of coal is metamorphic?
e: When soft coal gets squeezed and baked deep underground, Earth transforms it into super shiny, hard anthracite.

q: Oak Ridge National Lab scientists are using the Spallation Neutrons and Pressure Diffractometer to collect diffraction data under pressure conditions as high as 120 gigapascals. Which of the following is closest to the number of atmospheres that these pressures are equivalent to?
e: Each gigapascal packs ten thousand atmospheres, so this giant squeeze equals over a million times our normal air pressure!

q: Which of the following best describes the composition of Earth's core?
e: Right at Earth's center spins a scorching, heavy metallic heart made of iron hugging tightly to nickel.

q: A ship accidentally loses a cargo of floating rubber balls off the East coast of Japan. If they follow the prevailing currents, in which of the following locations will most of them likely FIRST wash on shore:
a: the western coast of North America
e: The Pacific ocean current acts like a giant watery conveyor belt, happily carrying floating toys straight toward North America!

q: Which of the following is NOT a greenhouse gas?
e: Lighthearted helium drifts right into the sky without trapping heat, so it cannot act like a warm greenhouse blanket.

q: In which of the following locations would you MOST easily find a treasure-trove of rhyolitic rock:
a: evaporate deposits in Death Valley, California
e: Yellowstone sits atop an ancient supervolcano that blasted out oceans of thick, sticky lava, leaving behind mountains of rhyolite.

q: Which of the following is NOT a symptom of desertification?
a: Increased salinity in natural waters and soils
e: When dry lands lose their plant blankets, winds strip bare dirt away, so erosion actually speeds up instead of slowing!

q: Addition of which of the following compounds may promote carbon sequestration in the ocean?
e: Potassium hydroxide helps seawater become alkaline, allowing the ocean to safely drink up and lock away extra carbon dioxide.

q: Trees growing on the edge of a river's meander are most likely to fall into the river due to:
a: Deposition on the inside of the meander
Deposition on the outside of the meander
Erosion on the inside of the meander
Erosion on the outside of the meander
e: Water zooms fastest around the river's outside curves, chewing away the bank until nearby trees tumble right in!

q: A monocline is an example of which of the following?
e: Like a rug draped over a stair step, Earth gently bends flat rock layers into a single wave called a fold.

q: Which of the following best describes cataclastic metamorphism?
a: Ultrahigh pressures generated by impact with an extra-terrestrial body
High temperature alteration accompanied by moderate pressures in the presence of hydrothermal fluids
Mechanical deformation that can result from rocks sliding along a shear zone
Shallow burial with temperatures exceeding 300oC, similar to diagenesis [dy-uh-JEN-uh-sis]
e: When giant slabs of rock slide and grind past each other, the brutal friction crushes them into cataclastic rock.

q: Most terrestrial plants grow best in soil with a pH range of:
e: Plants are happiest when soil is just slightly acidic to neutral, from 6.0 to 7.0, for sipping up tasty nutrients.

q: Oak Ridge National Laboratory is producing actinium-225 [ak-TIN-ee-um two twenty five], which decays via alpha decay, for cancer treatments. Which of the following best explains why alpha particle radiation is effective in cancer treatment?
a: Alpha particles are large and can kill an entire cancer cell given a direct collision
Alpha particles have a short range in matter and therefore deposit a large amount of energy directly in the tumor
Alpha particles are helium nuclei and can thus readily escape from the patient's body without accumulation
Alpha particles can travel long distances within the human body and are more likely to reach the tumor than other types of radiation
e: Alpha particles travel only tiny distances before stopping, which lets them dump all their cancer-fighting energy right inside the tumor.

q: Welded tuff is composed primarily of what material?
e: During fiery eruptions, scorching volcanic ash rains down and glues itself together into a solid blanket called welded tuff.

q: Which of the following would lead to the formation of an emergent coast?
e: Growing ice sheets lock ocean water on land like frozen sponges, lowering sea levels to reveal brand new coastlines.

q: Which of the following is NOT characteristic of currents found on the western boundary of oceanic gyres, relative to other ocean currents?
e: Western boundary currents are the speed racers of the ocean, zooming swiftly along instead of moving slowly.

q: What is the most common climbing route for the second highest mountain in the world, K2?
e: Brave climbers tackling giant K2 mostly march up the icy ridge called the Abruzzi Spur to reach the clouds.

q: The Volcanic Explosivity Index rated the Toba eruption as an 8, the highest rating. Which of the following environments was the most likely tectonic setting for this eruption?
e: At a subduction zone, one heavy ocean plate dives beneath another, melting rock and trapping fiery gas for Earth's biggest, most explosive blasts.

q: Which of the following is true about the Labrador Sea Water mass (LSW)?
a: It is formed in the western Labrador Sea in the late spring
It travels south along the western edge of the North Atlantic Basin
It has decreased in temperature in recent decades
It does not enter the subtropical gyre of the North Atlantic
e: Like a chilly deep-sea traveler, this cold water sinks up north and journeys south along the western edge of the Atlantic Ocean.

q: In which of the following locations could a paleontologist hope to find sedimentary rocks containing trilobites ?
e: Long ago, Manitoba was covered by a warm, ancient sea where little hard-shelled trilobites scuttled around, leaving their fossils behind in sedimentary rock.

q: The reasons why the earth's core is believed to be largely molten iron do NOT include which of following?
a: Abundance of iron in the universe
e: Earth's blazing center is far too scorching for iron to stay magnetic, so its magnetic properties cannot prove what the core is made of.

q: Which of the following best defines biodiesel?
a: Alternative diesel fuel produced from renewable resources
e: Biodiesel is a clever, cleaner fuel made from renewable goodies like vegetable oils and plant fats instead of old underground petroleum.

q: Which of the following theories describes the random movement of small particles in the atmosphere?
e: Tiny specks perform a nonstop zigzag dance called Brownian motion because bouncing air molecules keep bumping into them from every side!

q: The Black Hills of South Dakota is a large dome that has been exposed due to upwarping followed by erosion. Which of the following rocks would we expect to find in the innermost core of the Black Hills?
e: Right in the dome's deepest heart rests pegmatite, an ancient underground rock famous for growing giant, sparkling mineral crystals.

q: How much energy in tons of coal equivalent can be released by using deuterium in 50 cups of sea water in a deuterium - tritium fusion reactor?
e: Just fifty cups of ocean water hide enough fusion fuel to unleash the mighty energy of two whole tons of burning coal!

q: According to the discontinuous side of Bowen's reaction series, which of the following is likely to first crystallize as basaltic magma cools:
e: As scorching magma begins to cool, pretty green olivine is the very first eager mineral to freeze into solid crystals.

q: Which of the following clay minerals forms from the weathering of feldspar and is the main component of most porcelain?
e: When gentle rainwater breaks down feldspar rock, it creates soft white kaolinite clay, the magical ingredient used to bake smooth porcelain.

q: Which of the following is the International Energy Agency's stance on energy subsidies?
a: There should be greater international collaboration on subsidies
Subsidies are necessary for energy sustainability
Subsidies are necessary to reduce greenhouse emissions
e: Energy leaders believe subsidies should be phased out so fossil fuels stop getting unfair discounts, helping our planet breathe easier.

q: Which of the following is a fine-grained silica-rich sedimentary rock that is made primarily of microcrystalline quartz:
e: Chert is a tough, super-smooth rock built from microscopic quartz crystals that snap into wonderfully sharp edges.

q: Aeolian sandstones are produced primarily by sand grain motion as a result of:
e: Rushing river currents push and roll tumbling grains of sand downstream, piling them together until they squeeze into sandstone.

q: Waves of energy that come from an earthquake:
a: Travel through and along the surface of the earth
Can be felt at every single point on the surface of the earth
Travel only along the surface of the earth
Are unrelated to movements of magma beneath the surface
e: Earthquake waves are energetic travelers that ripple both deep through Earth's rocky belly and right along its bumpy surface.

q: Which of the following is a man-made coastal structure that causes coastal erosion by blocking oceanic longshore drift:
e: A jetty is a human-built stone wall that blocks drifting ocean sand, starving the beach downstream and causing it to wash away.

q: In which sphere is the "bad" ozone, a volatile compound that contributes to smog, located?
e: The troposphere is the lowest air layer where we breathe, so when tricky smog ozone hangs out down here, it harms our lungs.

q: Which of the following landlocked countries is entirely contained within another country?
e: Tiny Lesotho sits cozily tucked inside the giant belly of South Africa, completely hugged by its big neighbor.

q: Researchers at SLAC [slack] are currently working on mining methods to expand proven resources of uranium. Which of the following contains the largest amount of uranium?
e: Vast ocean water holds billions of tons of dissolved uranium, making the big blue sea Earth's giant treasure chest of nuclear fuel.

q: Tephrochronology [TEF-roh-krah-NAWL-ah-jee] deals with age- dating what type of material?
e: Tephrochronology uses fallen layers of volcanic ash like dusty clock timestamps to figure out exactly how old different rock beds are.

q: The Earth's greenhouse effect is primarily caused by which of the following:
a: incoming solar ultraviolet light is absorbed by the ozone layer
outgoing infrared solar radiation is trapped by the lower atmosphere
incoming infrared solar radiation is trapped by the magnetic field
outgoing X-rays are absorbed by the troposphere and reflected to the Earth's surface
e: Earth tries to radiate cozy heat back into space, but our lower atmosphere catches it like a giant blanket.

q: There is 47 prefectures in Japan.
e: Japan is neatly organized like a giant puzzle into forty-seven special regions called prefectures!

q: Thermohaline [thuhr-moh-HAY-lyn] circulation in the ocean is controlled most by which of the following?
e: Deep ocean water travels on a giant conveyor belt powered by two things: how warm it feels and how salty it tastes.

q: Global warming leads to positive feedbacks that accelerate the greenhouse effect. Which of the following is an example of this?
a: Plants photosynthesize more efficiently in a CO2-rich atmosphere
Reduced snow cover allows more solar radiation to warm the ground
More CO2 is sequestered by rock weathering in a warmer atmosphere
A warmer Earth loses more radiation to space
e: When bright snow melts away, the dark ground absorbs more sunshine and gets even warmer, speeding up the melt!

q: Does a heavy wet snowfall in Buffalo, New York necessarily mean that Boston, Massachusetts will experience the same weather?
a: Yes, because they are geographically close and the Westerlies drive storm systems across the U.S. towards the East
Yes, because airmasses hitting New England are always impacted by their proximity to the ocean and, therefore, pick up moisture that will be dumped as snow
No, because Buffalo, New York, is subject to lake-effect snows; the airmass may be "dried out" by the time it gets to Boston
No, because weather in the U.S. is driven by the Westerlies which push storm systems from east to west across the continent
e: Buffalo gobbles up wet lake-effect snow first, leaving the clouds too tired and dry to dump that same blizzard on Boston.

q: What gas can be found in volcanic emissions and has a characteristic rotten egg smell?
e: When volcanoes burp, they release hydrogen sulfide, a stinky gas that smells just like rotten eggs!

q: In 2012 the German-speaking microstate "Liechtenstein" in Central Europe had a population of how many inhabitants?
e: Tucked high in the Alps, cozy Liechtenstein was home to just 36,600 people in 2012, like one big mountain neighborhood.

q: Andesitic magmas typically erupt above:
e: Where one giant slab of Earth dives beneath another at a subduction zone, melting rock bubbles up to erupt as andesitic magma.

q: Which of the following gases varies the most by volume within the planetary boundary layer?
e: Floating near the ground, water vapor is a total shapeshifter, changing from dry desert air to swampy humidity day by day.

q: Which of the following low pressure systems typically has the weakest sustained wind speed?
e: A tropical wave is just a gentle, breezy ripple in the sky, blowing with the calmest winds of the bunch.

q: Which of the following establishes renewable energy use goals for the U.S. by a specific date?
e: Renewable Energy Portfolio Standards act like a shared calendar, giving states specific deadlines to plug into clean green power.

q: Llanfair­pwllgwyngyll­gogery­chwyrn­drobwll­llan­tysilio­gogo­goch is located on which Welsh island?
e: That village with the tongue-twisting name lives happily on the Welsh island of Anglesey, where even the train signs need extra room!

q: Which of the following mountain ranges in the state of Oregon is an accreted terrain?
e: The Wallowa Mountains were once wandering islands that crashed into Oregon long ago, sticking around as glued-on accreted land.

q: The La Brea Tar Pits of Los Angeles, California, are famous for the quantity and diversity of fossils of extinct Pleistocene animals. Which of the following is closest to the number of years ago that these pits formed?
e: Around 40,000 years ago, sticky black tar started bubbling up, trapping ancient animals like living time capsules.

q: What is the capital of Suriname?
e: Nestled beside a grand river, Paramaribo is the cheerful capital city where Suriname comes together.

q: Which of the following is a term specifically given to water that replenishes an aquifer?
e: Rain trickles deep underground into thirsty rock, giving the aquifer a fresh recharge just like a plugged-in battery!

q: What type of fault created the Loma Prieta earthquake in 1989?
e: Earth's rocky plates tried to slide sideways past each other along a strike-slip fault, suddenly snapping and shaking everything.

q: Which of the following is the largest global reserve of carbon on Earth:
e: The deep blue oceans act like Earth's biggest treasure chest, quietly holding more stored carbon than trees, soil, or air!

q: Conditions for tornadoes are favorable in which of the following mountain ranges?
e: Warm air clashes with chilly winds along the rolling Appalachians, spinning up the perfect storm recipe for tornadoes.

q: Which of the following processes would most likely lead to the formation of a metamorphic rock?
a: Precipitate forming at the bottom of the oceans
High speed ejection from a cone
e: When continents collide to build mountains, the intense crushing squeeze and deep heat bake ordinary rocks into metamorphic marvels!

q: What is the capital city of Bermuda?
e: Bright and colorful Hamilton wears the crown as Bermuda's capital, happily bustling right beside the sparkling island waters.

q: The Montreal Protocol effectively reduced the use of CFCs that damage the ozone layer. One group of replacements for CFCs has no effect on the ozone layer but is now recognized as greenhouse gases whose use must also be phased out. What group of gases is this?
e: HFCs swooped in to save the ozone, but these sneaky gases trap heat like an extra cozy blanket, warming up our planet!

q: What type of metamorphism occurs when magma is injected into crustal rock and the heat of the intrusion causes the crustal rock to metamorphose?
e: When super-hot magma hugs chilly rocks, that fiery touch bakes them into new shapes through contact metamorphism!

q: Greenschists and blueschists both derive from mafic parent rocks. Why do they have different mineral compositions?
a: They formed at different pressures and temperatures
e: Rocks bake like cookies! Greenschist likes a gentle squeeze, while blueschist forms under crushing pressures and cooler temperatures.

q: Flood basalts, such as the Cretaceous Deccan Traps in Siberia, may have had a major impact on which of the following past events?
e: These giant lava floods burped tons of trapped gases into the sky, triggering wild climate change that reshaped our world.

q: Which of the following is most directly associated with Andean-type plate margins?
e: When one heavy plate slides under another, melted rock bubbles up into a mighty marching line called a volcanic arc!

q: Which is not a country in Africa?
e: Guyana is having sunny adventures across the ocean in South America, so it is not an African country at all!

q: What was the primary reason that US and European markets adopted E85 as the maximum blend to be used in flexible fuel vehicles?
a: Higher ethanol blends are too expensive
Higher ethanol blends are unable to ignite in cold weather
Higher ethanol blends cannot be safely stored
Higher ethanol blends release more CO2 into the atmosphere through deforestation than they conserve
e: Ethanol hates freezing mornings! Adding too much makes it refuse to ignite, leaving chilly car engines fast asleep in cold weather.

q: In which period of the Geological Time Scale did trilobites first appear:
e: Way back in the busy Cambrian period, tiny armored trilobites scuttled across ancient seafloors for the very first time!

q: If the ambient air cools 8 degrees Celsius for each kilometer of vertical elevation you gain as you ascend a low mountain in Tennessee, which of the following most likely describes the stability of the local atmosphere?
e: At eight degrees per kilometer, the air is conditionally unstable, waiting for rising moisture before it decides to brew storms.

q: Calcite belongs to which of the following mineral groups:
e: Calcite is a proud carbonate mineral, made of carbon and oxygen building blocks that fizz happily in a drop of vinegar.

q: According to the Saffir-Simpson scale, a hurricane with maximum sustained winds of 67 meters per second is considered to be what category?
e: Roaring along at sixty-seven meters per second, these fierce, howling winds pack enough punch to earn a mighty Category 4 badge!

q: Which of the following is a problem that affects most plants growing in very acidic soil:
a: accumulation of excess salt in their foliage
excess calcium and magnesium ion uptake
e: Sour, acidic soil dissolves hidden aluminum, which acts like a nasty poison that pinches and hurts thirsty plant roots.

q: An oligotrophic (read as: oh-lig-oh-TROW-fick) lake is one that is BEST defined as:
e: Think of an oligotrophic lake as a deep, cold giant that stays crystal-clear because it is nutrient-poor!

q: An igneous [IG-nee-us] rock sample is characterized as being composed of crystals of olivine, calcium-rich plagioclase, and augite, and has a phaneritic [fan-er-IT-ik] texture. Which of the following four rocks is it?
e: Gabbro cools slowly underground, giving crystals of olivine and augite plenty of time to grow big and visible!

q: The Andaman and Nicobar Islands in South East Asia are controlled by which country?
e: Though drifting far out in the blue sea, the tropical Andaman and Nicobar Islands proudly belong to the nation of India.

q: Which city is the capital of Michigan?
e: While big Detroit gets lots of attention, cozy Lansing is the proud capital where leaders meet to guide Michigan.

q: Which of the following is closest to the percentage of the ocean area that is represented by continental shelves?
e: Continental shelves are shallow porches hugging our coasts, covering just about ten percent of the vast, splashing ocean.

q: Which of the following minerals would be found in least abundance in a typical gabbro [gab-roh]?
e: Gabbro loves dark, heavy minerals, so pale, flaky muscovite is almost never found hanging out in this rock family.

q: Which of the following is NOT true about the outer core of the Earth?
a: It is composed of iron and nickel
It is highly viscous and ductile
Its temperature is greater than 4000 degrees Celsius
It is the source of Earth's magnetic field
e: Earth's outer core is actually a swirling sea of runny liquid metal, not a thick, sticky, ductile paste!

q: Which of the following describes the carbonate compensation depth (CCD)?
a: Varying by latitude: deeper near the equator, shallower near the poles
Restricted to waters near the poles in both hemispheres
The depth at which carbonates start to form at nearly two times the rate of formation in shallower water
e: Warm, sunny waters near the equator protect sinking shells much deeper down, while chilly polar seas dissolve them closer to the surface.

q: Which of the following is closest to the pre-industrial concentration of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere?
e: Long before smoky factories woke up, carbon dioxide was a gentle whisper in our sky, dotting the air at just 275 parts per million!

q: What type of volcanic vent is Wizard Island, the only resurgent dome of Crater Lake that breaks the surface of the water line?
e: Wizard Island popped right out of the water when bubbly blobs of lava cooled into a neat, crunchy hill called a cinder cone!

q: Which of the following thermal reactors was found in the Three Mile Island reactor complex?
e: This plant used a pressurized water reactor, which squeezes super-hot liquid under tight control so it cannot boil while making energy.

q: What layer of the Earth's atmosphere contains approximately 75% of its air mass?
e: The cozy troposphere hugs closest to the ground, packing in three-quarters of Earth's entire blanket of air where all our weather plays.

q: The majority of Earth's freshwater is found in which of the following?
e: Most of Earth's fresh water is not splashing in rivers, but is snoozing peacefully inside giant, chilly blankets of ice and snow!

q: Reverse faults commonly form as a result of which of the following tectonic forces:
e: When giant pieces of Earth give each other a big, squeezing hug, compressive forces push and shove rock upward into a reverse fault!

q: Which of the following is a castle?
e: Elizabeth Castle is a real, historic stone fortress standing guard on a rocky islet near Jersey.

q: In which of the following ways does the mineral biotite [BY-uh-tyt] differ from the mineral muscovite [MUHS-kuh-vyt]?
a: Biotite contains silica while muscovite does not
Muscovite contains potassium while biotite does not
While both contain aluminum, only biotite contains magnesium
While both contain sodium, only muscovite contains aluminum
e: While these two shiny mineral cousins both invite aluminum to the party, only dark biotite brings magnesium along for the ride.

q: Into which basin does the Jordan River flow into?
e: The Jordan River finishes its long journey by tumbling straight into the super salty Dead Sea, where you can float like a cork!

q: When corals bleach due to warming seas they expel what symbiotic organisms, leaving them vulnerable to starvation and disease?
e: Stressed by warm water, corals wave goodbye to their colorful microscopic algae buddies, zooxanthellae, leaving the reef pale and terribly hungry.

q: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of a good index fossil?
e: Great index fossils zip through history quickly, so slow evolution would make it much too tricky to pinpoint a rock's exact birthday.

q: Which of the following geologic phenomena led to the formation of submarine canyons?
e: Underwater avalanches of swirling sand, called turbidity currents, race down the seafloor like muddy rollercoasters to carve out giant submarine canyons!

q: Which of the following is a geothermal process that has mostly led to concentrated stores of copper and zinc in the Earth's crust:
e: Super-hot water dissolves metals deep underground, cooling off to drop shiny treasures of copper and zinc through hydrothermal precipitation.

q: Which of the following phenomena are responsible for orange and red sunsets?
e: Tiny dust particles floating in the air scatter away restless blue light, letting cozy red and orange rays paint the evening sky.

q: Which sedimentary rock is impacted by ocean acidification as pH values fall?
e: Souring ocean water loves to nibble away at limestone, because this soft rock is built from seashell minerals that easily dissolve in acid.

q: Which of the following is characteristic of a deep residual soil?
a: Soil that has been weathering for a long period of time
Soil derived from rocks exposed to the hydrosphere and atmosphere
e: Deep residual soil is an old, patient dirt that has rested in place, weathering and crumbling rock over a very long time.

q: Which of the following is closest to the percentage of incoming solar radiation that is absorbed by the ocean and land?
e: Earth's land and oceans soak up about 50 percent of the sun's golden rays, while the rest bounces away into space.

q: A transgressive stratigraphic sequence can be related to which of the following events?
e: When sea levels rise, creeping ocean waters tiptoe farther inland and pile up deep-water rock layers in a transgressive sequence.

q: During what eon did visible life start to appear and resulted in abundant fossils?
e: The Phanerozoic eon is when Earth burst with visible life, filling the rock layers with wonderful fossil treasures for us to discover!

q: Which of the following systems of climate classification is the best-known and most used?
e: The Köppen system is our favorite weather map, cleverly sorting our planet's climates using temperature and the plants that grow there.

q: A dam is holding back a lake that has a water level of 80 meters. A large crack forms at the base of the dam. In meters per second, which of the following is closest to the water speed through the crack?
e: With eighty meters of lake pressing down, gravity gives that escaping water a mighty shove, blasting it out at forty meters per second!

q: Alfred Wegener believed that which of the following caused the continents to move?
a: The rotation of the Earth's magnetic field
e: Wegener imagined our spinning planet twirled fast enough to push huge continents sliding across the globe like giant rafts.

q: Because of Earth's rotation and shape, ocean currents are intensified along which of the following borders of all oceans:
e: Earth's spin crowds moving water toward western borders, squeezing ocean currents into speedy, powerful ocean highways.

q: Which of the following tectonic environments would lead to the formation of the most felsic, silica-rich magma?
a: Subduction associated with the Andes Mountains
e: Yellowstone's underground hot spot bakes thick continental rock like an oven, melting it into sticky, silica-rich magma.

q: Two years after carbon dioxide was sequestered by the Pacific Northwest National Lab near Wallula, Washington, the material was converted into mineral substances resembling what type of sedimentary rock?
e: Trapped deep underground, the carbon gas bonded with rock minerals, transforming into solid, carbonate-rich limestone.

q: Which of the following BEST explains how a radium isotope with a half-life of about 1,600 years can be found in the crust of the Earth that was formed millions of years ago:
a: its decay is slowed by the pressure of the Earth
the radium is replenished by decay of longer lived radioactive elements
the radium was replenished by meteors and asteroids over the millennia
the radium is recycled from the Earth's core where magnetic fields slow the decay
e: Older elements like uranium keep decaying slowly, constantly making fresh radium to replace what faded away long ago.

q: Which of the following is true of ocean wave energy?
a: It is the frictional effect of wind
It is the strength of surface ocean currents
It transfers energy to the top 200 meters of the ocean
It occurs in shallow water and migrates outward
e: When playful wind drags across open water, its friction tickles the surface and pushes waves to life!

q: Which of the following surface ocean currents transports warm water to higher latitudes?
e: The Gulf Stream acts like a warm bathwater express, carrying tropical heat northward toward chilly lands.

q: Which of the following percentages is closest to the percent of U.S. electricity generated from fossil fuels in 2014?
e: Back in 2014, fossil fuels did the heavy lifting, powering about seventy percent of America's buzzing electric grid.

q: Which of the following is a compressional elastic seismic wave that causes rock particles to move back and forth parallel to wave direction:
e: A P-wave scampers through rock like an accordion, squeezing and stretching the ground in the direction it travels.

q: Which of the following rocks typically has the SMALLEST grains:
e: Shale is made of super tiny mud specks squeezed together, giving it smaller grains than sandy rocks.

q: What is the capital of Burkina Faso?
e: With a name that rolls right off your tongue, lively Ouagadougou is the proud capital of Burkina Faso!

q: Which of the following is a brief yet destructive windstorm marked by cool moist air descending from a thunderstorm that is sometimes mistaken for a tornado because of the damage it produces:
e: A microburst drops a cool, sudden blast of air from a thunderstorm, flattening trees like a runaway freight train!

q: Which of these is NOT a province in China?
e: The mighty Yangtze is actually a legendary river winding like a giant dragon across China, not an official province.

q: The prefix Sino- (As in Sino-American) is used to refer to what nationality?
e: Whenever you spot Sino-, imagine China's great lands, because that ancient word has always meant Chinese.

q: The time interval between the generation of P and S waves from its arrival at a seismometer is BEST translated as:
a: the wave height of a potential tsunami
the distance to the nearest fault zone
e: Because speedy P-waves beat slower S-waves, the time gap between them reveals the distance to the earthquake's epicenter.

q: Which of the following environments would form foliated metamorphic rock?
a: At the surface of an active volcano
In the accretionary [uh-kree-shun-UH-ri] wedge above a subducting plate
e: In an accretionary wedge, colliding tectonic plates squish rocks under enormous pressure, squeezing their minerals into neat, flat layers.

q: As Earth's temperature rises, sea levels will also rise due to the melting of continental ice. Why won't this effect be canceled by increased evaporation of seawater from the oceans?
a: The thermohaline [thermo-HAY-line] circulation will slow down
When ice sheets melt, they release latent heat
Saltwater evaporates much more slowly than freshwater
The atmosphere is a much smaller water reservoir than the ocean
e: The air is just a tiny bucket compared to the giant ocean, so it cannot hold all that melted water.

q: Some individual minerals in metamorphic rocks are bounded by their crystal faces. What adjective identifies this type of rock?
e: When metamorphic crystals grow freely with their own sharp, handsome crystal faces, scientists call them idioblastic.

q: Which of the following is NOT among the criteria that define a substance as a mineral?
e: Minerals follow strict recipes and crystal shapes, but nature lets them melt over a cozy range of temperatures instead of just one point.

q: Which of the following is TRUE regarding the Hadley cell:
a: it creates an area of high pressure along the equator
it is an open ocean circulation at 30 north and south latitudes
it originates at the equator with strong solar heating
it is the only air circulation that is not affected by the Coriolis effect
e: The tropical sun bakes the equator, sending warm air soaring up like a hot air balloon to start this giant wind loop!

q: Karst topography is generally formed in regions with which type of rock?
e: Raindrops slowly nibble away soft limestone underground, carving out secret caves and sinkholes like holes in Swiss cheese.

q: Which of the following stream types best describes the Columbia River along the Columbia River Gorge?
e: An antecedent river was there first, stubbornly slicing right through mountains as they slowly grew up around it!

q: Which of the following factors does NOT directly impact the climate of a geographic location?
e: Longitude lines just show how far east or west you are, which does not change the sun's warmth or weather.

q: In the Canadian province of Alberta, the city of Calgary is located further north than the city of Edmonton.
e: Look at the map and you will see Edmonton sits up north, while friendly Calgary relaxes further south.

q: Ganymede is more massive than Titan, but only Titan has an atmosphere. Which of the following correctly explains this?
a: Titan's atmosphere is mostly made of heavy gases, like sulfur dioxide, which cannot escape its gravitational pull
Titan is significantly colder than Ganymede, preventing its atmosphere from escaping
Titan actively replenishes its atmosphere, while Ganymede does not
Titan absorbs atmospheric gases from Saturn, while Ganymede does not absorb gases from Jupiter
e: Titan is so freezing cold that gas particles slow down and stay trapped, hugging the moon like a frosty blanket.

q: Blue-green algae produces mats that trap and bind microcrystalline carbonates as incoming tides sweep over the sand, producing what kind of carbonate rock structure?
e: Tiny algae work like patient bakers, sticking sand and minerals into wafer-thin sheets called laminations.

q: Compared to felsic igneous rocks, mafic igneous rocks contain greater amounts of which of the following elements?
e: Mafic rocks pack lots of iron, making them dark and sturdy like nature's own cast-iron skillets.

q: Scientists at Oak Ridge National Laboratory are researching ways to generate electricity from waste heat. What is the name of the effect they are taking advantage of?
e: The Seebeck effect cleverly turns leftover warmth into electricity, waking up trapped energy from waste heat!

q: Which of the following minerals has only one plane of cleavage?
e: Biotite peels along one single direction, shedding flat sheets just like pages in a tiny stone notebook.

q: The lack of transmission of earthquake S-waves through what layer of the Earth is evidence that it is liquid?
e: Wiggle waves cannot travel through liquid, so vanishing at the outer core proves that layer is melted soup!

q: Ocean tides of diminished range are called:
e: Neap tides happen when the sun and moon tug in different directions, giving the ocean a gentle, smaller wave.

q: Which of the following is NOT a mineral?
e: Coal grew from squished ancient plants, and true minerals can never be made from living things!

q: What is special about Lake Titicaca?
e: Lake Titicaca sits so high up in the mountains that big boats practically sail among the clouds!

q: Which of the following changes has the potential to reduce the damage expected to be done by a hurricane with a particular Saffir-Simpson rating?
a: Increased formal and informal education for the public about hurricane safety
Reduction in the amount of paved surfaces
Construction of sea walls around coastal cities
More rigorous building codes for robust construction of frame houses in coastal regions
e: Building homes with stronger walls and sturdy roofs helps coastal towns stand tall against fierce hurricane winds.

q: Increasing the silica content in rock melts results in an increase in the melt viscosity. Which of the following SI derived units would be used to describe melt viscosity?
e: Viscosity measures how sluggishly gooey melted rock crawls, and scientists count that sticky thickness in Pascal seconds.

q: A combination of technologies called the Sahara Forest Project with the potential to produce commercial quantities of food and energy crops, fresh water, and electricity in the desert, has all of the following components, EXCEPT:
e: This desert project uses clever saltwater greenhouses and solar power, leaving out switchgrass entirely.

q: Which of the following is commonly accepted as the engine that most directly drives plate tectonic motion:
a: gravitational pull of the Moon and Sun
e: Deep inside Earth, hot rock swirls like boiling oatmeal in mantle convection, slowly steering the giant plates around!

q: Which of the following is closest to the percentage of the Earth's total surface water contained in ice caps, glaciers, and permanent snow?
e: Most of Earth's water splashes in oceans, leaving just about two percent locked up in frozen ice caps.

q: The Chinook winds that come from the west and move air down the eastern face of the Rocky Mountains are known as "snow eaters", because:
a: The winds bring moist warm air from California, causing the snows to melt and "disappear" from the Front Range region of Colorado
The airmass brings cold, dry winds from the peaks of the Rockies, causing the snow to freeze into black ice, making it look like the snow "disappeared"
The winds blow the snow off the Front Range and onto the Plains, making the snow "disappear" from the eastern face of the mountains
The airmass warms as it descends, increasing its water vapor capacity and causing the snow to sublime and "disappear"
e: As this wind rushes down the mountain, it warms up and gulps down snow, turning it straight into vapor.

q: The two largest ethnic groups of Belgium are Flemish and Walloon.
e: This is true! The Flemish and Walloon peoples form the two biggest cultural families happily sharing Belgium's cities and famous chocolate.

q: Which of the following is the most abundant mineral group found in the Earth's crust?
e: Silicates are rock royalty, teaming up to make up most of Earth's crunchy outer crust.

q: Methane hydrate is a cage-like lattice of ice inside which are trapped molecules of methane, the chief constituent of natural gas. Which of the following is NOT true about methane hydrate?
a: Deposits generally occur beneath Arctic permafrost and the ocean floor
Methane extraction from methane hydrate has been documented in large-scale field experiments
If pressures are high enough, it is stable far above the melting point of water ice
The energy content of methane hydrate is very high
e: This icy fuel is so tricky to handle that people haven't managed to harvest it in big tests yet.

q: Which of the following phenomena is a buildup of ocean water that is pushed towards land by a hurricane?
e: A storm surge happens when a fierce hurricane shoves a giant wall of sea water right onto land.

q: Which of these is an official currency of the Cook Islands?
e: These sunny South Pacific islands team up with their friendly neighbor New Zealand, using the New Zealand dollar for buying coconut treats.

q: Which of the following rock types would be most susceptible to chemical weathering by tropical rainfall?
e: Basalt breaks down fastest because its rich minerals cannot resist the dissolving power of warm tropical rains.

q: During an El Nio period, sea surface temperatures along the west coasts of North and South America are relatively warm and upwelling is suppressed. What effect does this generally have on fish catches along these coasts during El Nio winters?
a: Fish catches increase followed by a sudden decrease
e: Without chilly, food-filled water bubbling up, hungry fish swim away, so coastal catches drop.

q: What type of geologic fault is characterized by upward displacement of a footwall?
e: When Earth's crust stretches, a normal fault lets one block drop while the footwall stays lifted.

q: Which of the following is a common mineral that is composed entirely of silicon and oxygen?
e: Sparkly quartz is a pure rock recipe made entirely of silicon holding hands with oxygen.

q: Which of the following best describes why ocean water at 30 degrees latitude has higher salt content than water at the equator?
a: Most rivers flow into the ocean at the equator
Ice formation at high latitudes increases salinity
Precipitation exceeds evaporation at the equator
Low-salinity water upwells at the equator
e: Endless rainstorms dump so much fresh water on the equator that the salty ocean gets watered down.

q: The tectonic environment of Iceland is:
e: Iceland sits right over a mid-ocean ridge, where tectonic plates split apart to let fresh lava bubble up.

q: What is the official German name of the Swiss Federal Railways?
e: In German, Switzerland calls its speedy trains Schweizerische Bundesbahnen, zipping passengers happily through the snowy Alps.

q: Which of the following tectonic plates is largest?
e: The mighty Pacific plate is Earth's biggest puzzle piece, carrying a whole giant ocean on its back.

q: What pair of natural phenomena contribute the most to the release of interstitial water from sediment into lake water columns?
e: Gusty winds stir up lake currents, tickling the muddy bottom so trapped water squeezes right out.

q: Clays such as kaolinite [KAY-uh-luh-nyt] form when H+ [H plus] ions combine with which of the following?
a: Primordial water emitted directly from volcanic eruptions
e: Eager hydrogen ions nibble on tough old minerals like feldspar, crumbling them into smooth, squishy clay.

q: What type of volcano is characterized by gentle eruptions and large, gently-sloped landforms?
e: Shield volcanoes gently ooze runny lava, spreading out wide and flat like a sleepy warrior's shield.

q: Which of the following is generated from temperature changes in the atmosphere?
e: Sensible heat is the cozy warmth you can actually feel and measure with a thermometer as temperatures rise.

q: Which of the following is NOT used in determining relative geologic time:
e: Radioisotope half-lives reveal a rock's exact birthday in years, not just which rocky layer is older.

q: Which of the following is NOT a property of pyroclastic (read as: py-re-KLAHS-tik) flows?
a: Hot rock and ash flow like a turbulent blanket over the ground
They glow red at night but appear grey in the daytime
e: These fiery clouds of ash never move slowly; they roar down mountains faster than a racecar!

q: Which of the following sedimentary rocks is most likely to be changed to slate during regional metamorphism?
e: Soft, muddy shale gets squished deep underground by enormous heat and pressure, magically transforming into smooth, tough slate!

q: Which of the following is the mechanism by which strain energy is released during earthquakes?
e: Like a stretched rubber band suddenly snapping back, rocks bend until elastic rebound sets all that trapped energy loose with a shudder!

q: In which of the following regions of the world's oceans are you most likely to find the greatest uniformity in density changes with increasing depth:
e: Near the chilly poles, high-latitude waters stay freezing cold from top to bottom, keeping their density wonderfully uniform all the way down.

q: Which of the following transport agents is generally associated with creating the most poorly sorted sediment deposits?
e: Glaciers act like messy giant bulldozers, shoving huge boulders and tiny grains into one big, unsorted jumble without cleaning up!

q: Which of the following is NOT a role that large-scale batteries could play in a power generation portfolio based on renewable energy sources?
e: Big batteries love storing sunshine for later, but frequency modulation belongs to radio broadcasts, not giant energy storage!

q: When does Finland celebrate their independence day?
e: December 6th is the cozy winter night when people across Finland light candles in their windows to celebrate their nation's birthday.

q: Which of the following pairs correctly matches the U.S. geographic location and its typical tidal pattern?
e: The sleepy Gulf of Mexico dances to a slow rhythm, getting just one high and one low diurnal tide each day.

q: A soil sample is extracted from a soil monolith in a temperate forest environment. The sample contains a relatively high concentration of sand and silt as well as leached minerals. What soil horizon does the sample represent?
e: Rainwater washes away colorful minerals like a gentle rinse, leaving behind the pale, sandy E horizon.

q: Striations, U-shaped valleys, and fjords are all landscape features formed by what process?
e: Heavy glaciers scrape down mountains like giant ice scoops, carving out wide valleys and fjords through powerful glacial erosion.

q: Which of the following air masses is responsible for causing lake-effect snow in the Great Lakes region?
e: Chilly continental polar air sweeps over warm lake water, slurping up moisture to dump mountains of fluffy snow!

q: When geologists find pillow basalts in ancient rock sequences, which of the following BEST explains their presence:
a: volcanic bombs and lapilli landed on snow or ice and quickly cooled
they hardened in mid-air, sometimes forming a tear-drop shape
nearby volcanoes erupted enormous quantities of ash
e: When fiery lava bubbles up underwater, the chilly sea quickly cools it into puffy, cozy-looking pillow rocks!

q: Gabriela is studying a map showing rivers flowing through a mountainous region. She notices that the V-shaped river valleys are often much wider than the rivers themselves. Which of the following statements best explains her observation?
a: The rivers carried more water in the past
The valleys were formed by glaciers and were later replaced by rivers
A series of cut-banks and point-bars formed as the rivers developed, widening the valley
Mass wasting and stream erosion have widened the valley
e: While busy rivers dig straight down, crumbling hillsides slide inward through mass wasting and erosion, widening the valley walls.

q: Which of the following is best classified as a plutonic intrusive rock:
e: Granite cools super slowly deep underground, giving its pretty crystals plenty of cozy time to grow together.

q: What is the term for a fluidized mixture of solid to semi-solid fragments and hot expanding gases that flows under gravity down the flanks of a volcano during an eruption?
e: A super-hot, racing avalanche of ash and glowing gas charging down a mountain is called a pyroclastic flow!

q: Which of the following is one of the main reasons why geologists believe that the second greatest earthquake risk to the U.S. lies along the New Madrid Fault in Kentucky, Mississippi and Tennessee:
a: the underlying geology is loose sand and mud deposited by the Mississippi River
it overlies a deep transform fault margin much like the San Andreas fault
it lies over a fast-moving modern plate boundary
it lies over a deep, subterranean hot spot
e: The Mississippi River left behind loose mud and sand that wiggle like jelly during an earthquake, making shaking much worse!

q: Which of the following statements is NOT true about shallow living coral reefs?
a: They serve as centers of biodiversity
They are generally found in temperate waters
They are threatened by climate change
They can be assessed using towed diver surveys
e: Sun-loving shallow corals crave toasty tropical waters, so they cannot thrive in chilly temperate seas!

q: Which of the following rock types is thought to originate in the deep mantle and is an economically important source of diamonds?
e: Blasting up from the deep mantle like an express elevator, kimberlite rock delivers sparkling diamonds toward the surface!

q: Which of the following BEST determines the maximum height of open ocean waves and is the point where breaking white caps form in a fully developed sea:
a: the cohesive forces in water molecules are overcome and the waves break apart
the waves are losing as much energy as breaking white caps as they are receiving from the wind
the trough moves a little bit faster than the crest and the wave becomes unstable
the waves have reached a maximum period
e: Waves reach their limit when whitecaps tumble, losing energy just as fast as gusty winds can push it in.

q: What is the Finnish word for "Finland"?
e: While travelers say Finland, the cozy folks who actually live there call their land of forests and lakes Suomi.

q: What is the world's smallest country by population?
e: Tiny Vatican City has fewer than a thousand residents, making it the coziest, least-populated country on Earth.

q: What is the administrative centre and largest settlement on the Norwegian archipelago of Svalbard?
e: Up near the chilly North Pole, colorful Longyearbyen serves as the cheerful capital hub where humans live alongside roaming polar bears.

q: Oak Ridge National Lab researchers are developing better N95 respirators by testing the permeability of masks made of different materials. To test the permeability to SARS- CoV-2 virus particles, they used aerosols of sodium chloride with particle sizes closest to which of the following?
e: The virus is teeny-tiny, around 100 nanometers across, so scientists used matching bits of salt to test the mask!

q: Which of the following minerals is NOT typically found in the rock granite?
e: Olivine loves super-hot, deep lava too much to show up in granite's cooler, sparkly neighborhood.

q: Which of the following statements about limestone and dolostone is true?
a: The primary cation [KAT-eye-uhn] present in dolostone is magnesium, while in limestone, it is calcium
Both limestone and dolostone have high solubility in HCL, making them difficult to distinguish in the field
Dolostone's primary mineral compound has two CO32-anions while limestone's primary mineral compound has only one CO32- anion
Unlike limestone, which is composed primarily of the mineral calcite, dolostone is considered both a rock and a mineral
e: Dolostone packs two carbonate groups into its mineral recipe, while limestone settles for just one.

q: Which of the following BEST describes the dynamics of a typical alpine glacier:
a: the relative position of particles within the ice remains stationary
retreating glaciers carve out V-shaped valleys
high pressures created by the mass movement of ice can produce meltwater deep within a glacier
they move downhill primarily under the influence of ice avalanching
e: A heavy glacier squeezes down so hard that the ice deep inside melts into a slippery puddle!

q: Which of the following is NOT a consequence of the apparent stretching of the crust during extension in order to form fault-block mountains?
e: Accretion only happens when land crashes together, not when the crust stretches apart like warm taffy.

q: A sedimentary deposit consists of three layers: a base layer of gravel-sized grains, an intermediate layer of sand, and a top layer of silt and other fine particles. Assuming the deposit has not been overturned, what type of grading does the deposit represent?
e: Heavy gravel sinks first while tiny dirt floats to the top, which is nature's normal way of tidying up!

q: About what percent of all glaciers in the world are retreating today:
e: Our warming world has every icy giant on the run, meaning all of them are shrinking backward today.

q: Which of the following glacial features are deposited in annual layers and can be used by geologists to determine seasonal variations during past ice ages:
e: Varves are striped mud layers painted year by year, just like tree rings telling tales of frosty winters!

q: What was the original name of Ho Chi Minh City?
e: Before taking its modern name, this buzzing Vietnamese city filled with speeding scooters was famously known to the world as Saigon.

q: Which of the following atmospheric gases is created naturally by the action of sunlight on molecular oxygen:
e: Sunlight breaks ordinary oxygen apart and stitches it back together into protective ozone high in the sky.

q: A red breccia contains a high percentage of large angular feldspar grains. In what type of depositional environment would you expect it to have formed?
e: Sharp, chunky stones tumbled straight off a steep mountain and landed nearby on a wide alluvial fan!

q: Tree growth is often very stunted and gnarly at the tree line of high mountains in North America. Known as Krummholz formations, this is primarily caused by:
e: Fierce, howling mountain winds shove the little trees around until they grow up short, bent, and tough!

q: Which of the following is a terminal moraine that resulted at the climax of the Wisconsin ice sheet:
e: A giant ice sheet bulldozed rocks across the land and dumped them at the edge, building Long Island!

q: Which of the following metamorphic index minerals is typically FOUND in the metamorphic facies [FAY-sheez] granulite?
e: Granulite rocks bake in extreme underground heat, which is the perfect fiery home for tough sillimanite crystals.

q: There are caves found in Bend, Oregon, just east of Mt. Jefferson. Based on their location, what type of rocks do you suspect make up these caves?
e: Lava poured onto the surface and cooled into extrusive igneous rock, leaving magical hollow tubes behind!

q: A high-energy river environment will most likely create which of the following deposits:
a: Poorly sorted beds with no structure
e: Wild, rushing river water tumbles heavy pebbles like a rock tumbler until they become smooth, rounded gravel!

q: Scientists at Oak Ridge National Lab are searching for a protein catalyst that can degrade plant cell walls. What is the term for a protein catalyst?
e: An enzyme is nature's speedy helper protein, racing to chop up plant walls without breaking a sweat!

q: Which of the following is characteristic of orthochemical carbonate rocks but not of allochemical carbonate rocks?
a: Ooids in a sparry calcite matrix
e: These rocks grow straight from quiet water into clear, granular crystals rather than gathering broken shells.

q: Which of the following advantages is offered by mid- and deep- ocean sequestration that is not possible at shallower depths?
e: Plunging deep into the dark sea traps carbon safely for much longer before it can sneak back out.

q: Which of the following is an application of the principle of inclusions?
a: Mineral size will decrease with increasing metamorphic grade
Any feature cutting across a layered rock must be younger than the rock it transects
Porphyroblasts [poor-feh-ROH-blasts] are older than their host rock
Xenoliths [ZEE-no-liths] are older than their host rock
e: Like chocolate chips tossed into cookie dough, xenolith rocks were already around before the hot magma trapped them inside.

q: What kind of minerals do copper ores tend to be?
e: Copper loves teaming up with carbon and sulfur underground, making carbonate and sulfide minerals its favorite homes.

q: Which of the following is an example of a U-shaped valley that is partially submerged:
e: A giant glacier carved a grand valley, and the sea happily rushed in to fill the sunken fjord.

q: What gas accounts for approximately 78% of the dry volume of Earth's atmosphere?
e: Nitrogen is the quiet champion of the sky, blanketing our world by making up nearly four-fifths of our air!

q: Organisms are sometimes assigned fractional trophic levels. Which of the following factors is least likely to complicate trophic level assignment?
a: Female black widow spiders cannibalize male black widow spiders after mating
Bullfrogs eat crayfish while crayfish eat bullfrog tadpoles
Bobcats eat rabbits while mountain lions eat both bobcats and rabbits
Gorillas eat both bamboo and fruit
e: Gentle gorillas stick purely to plants, keeping their dinner menu wonderfully simple instead of mixing up predator food webs.

q: The Sierra Nevada Mountains are composed primarily of granite. Considering that granite is an intrusive rock, how could it become visible at the surface of the Earth?
a: Intrusive rock forms on the surface
e: Wind and rain patiently washed away the thick blanket of dirt on top, uncovering the sleepy granite beneath.

q: What city is known as the Rose Capital of the World?
e: Tyler, Texas grew millions of sweet-smelling rosebushes, proudly earning its title as the world's rose capital!

q: Which of the following is NOT consistent with the Cenozoic rock record?
a: Dominance of reptiles increases with time
Dominance of mammals increases with time
e: After giant dinosaurs stepped down, mammals ruled the Cenozoic world, so reptiles definitely did not take over.

q: The zone of aeration is BEST described as pores in rock or soil that contain:
e: Right below our feet, tiny soil pores share room for both trickling water and fresh pockets of air.

q: Which of the following is NOT a result of mountaintop coal mining?
a: Increased mineral content in valley streams
e: Blasting mountaintops breaks wild woods into scattered patches, which divides forests instead of joining them together.

q: A line with alternating blue triangles and red semicircles on a weather map indicates:
e: Cold blue teeth and warm red bumps face off in an arm-wrestle, showing a stationary front that refuses to budge.

q: Which of the following BEST describes what happens to continental crust as glaciers melt and retreat?
a: Springs fill in low-lying regions left behind
The crust remains deformed, leaving large synclines
There is no impact on the crust
e: Just like a squished mattress bouncing back after a heavy nap, the crust slowly rebounds when icy glaciers melt.

q: The metamorphism of a sandstone rock will cause the rock to do which of the following?
e: Deep underground heat and pressure give sandstone a giant bear hug, squeezing its grains tightly together to become denser.

q: What is the principle characteristic of rocks that originate from volcanoes?
e: Lava cools so quickly outside that mineral crystals never get time to grow big, leaving a super fine-grained rock!

q: How is geothermal power produced?
a: Heat energy is extracted from high temperature lava after eruptions
Water from extremely hot springs is circulated in pipes in nearby homes for heating
Hot dry volcanic rocks are extracted from deep underground and processed in place at a geothermal plant
Mile-or-more-deep wells are drilled into underground reservoirs to tap steam and very hot water that drive turbines
e: Deep wells tap underground boiling water, sending hissing steam up to spin giant power turbines like breezy pinwheels.

q: Idaho National Lab researchers are studying rocks that form near rhyolitic [rye-oh-LIT-ik] eruptions with x-ray fluorescence. Which of the following statements is true regarding the magma from eruptions?
a: It contains little silica compared to basaltic magma
It is cooler in temperature than basaltic magma
It is low-viscosity compared to basaltic magma
It is high in iron content relative to basaltic magma
e: Even though it creates explosive drama, rhyolitic magma is actually hundreds of degrees cooler than runny basalt magma.

q: A meromictic lake has layers of water that typically:
a: intrtmix only when the winds are favorable
e: In this sleepy lake, the deep water and top water act like shy neighbors that never mix together.

q: If you measure the solar altitude at noon and find it to be 90, at which of the following locations could you be?
a: France, in Western Europe Round 14 Page 1
Buenos Aires, Argentina, in southeastern South America
Tokyo, Japan, off the coast of eastern Asia
e: The sun only shines directly overhead near Earth's warm equator, making the sunny Congo the perfect place to be!

q: Which country is the Taedong River in?
e: The Taedong River rolls right through the city of Pyongyang as it journeys across North Korea.

q: Volatile fossil fuels tend to have low carbon to hydrogen ratios. Which of the following fossil fuels is the most volatile?
e: With four bouncy hydrogens hugging just one carbon atom, tiny methane escapes into gas faster than any other fuel.

q: Which of the following is a warm core, low pressure system?
e: A hurricane drinks up warmth from the sea, spinning around its cozy, low-pressure heart like a dizzy dancing giant.

q: Which of the following BEST describes the largest size of sediment particle that can be transported by a particular flow in a river:
e: Competency is a river's muscle power, deciding the biggest, heaviest rock it is strong enough to push along.

q: Which of the following is NOT true regarding the ocean floor?
a: Continental shelves generally overlay oceanic crust
The continental shelf tends to be fairly featureless
Continental shelves represent less than 10% of the total ocean area
Continental shelves are saturated with water
e: Continental shelves are actually the edges of continents dipping their toes in the sea, resting on thick continental crust, not oceanic crust.

q: In the oceans, waves and surf currents are generated by:
e: Playful wind brushes across the open water, tickling the sea until rolling waves wake up and dash toward shore!

q: Which of the following statements is NOT true about tides:
a: tidal range is not the same over a whole ocean basin
tidal ranges generally increase with increasing distance from amphidromic points
tidal bores are true tidal waves
on average, tidal currents reach maximum velocity during flood current
e: Tidal currents actually rush fastest halfway between high and low tide, not all the way through the flood current.

q: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of the mixed layer of the ocean?
a: In direct contact with the atmosphere
Varied depth with latitude and season
e: Waves and breezes stir the mixed layer like a giant spoon, blending it completely instead of letting it settle into neat layers.

q: Light passes from a mineral with an index of refraction of 2.5 into air. Which of the following is closest to the smallest incident angle, in degrees, at which there will be total internal reflection?
e: Trapped light bounces right back inside this crystal once it tilts past twenty-five degrees, turning the gem into a sparkling mirror!

q: In which of the following silicate groups of minerals does olivine belong?
e: Olivine belongs with the nesosilicates because its tiny crystal building blocks love to sit alone like peaceful little green islands.

q: Isostatic rebound following the end of the most recent ice age caused which of the following?
a: Mountain formation in the eastern part of the U.S.
e: When heavy ice melted away, the relieved land popped back up like a squished sponge, making nearby sea levels drop!

q: Why are there so many more land fossils than marine fossils in early Mesozoic rocks?
a: Shorelines were inundated with terrigenous sediment from mountains
e: Crumbling mountains washed great blankets of dirt over the shores, burying land critters quickly so they could turn into lasting fossils.

q: Which of the following minerals is an industrial ore of lead and can be identified by its relative softness and three directions of cleavage?
e: Galena is a soft, heavy lead ore that loves breaking into tidy, shiny little blocks along three flat directions.

q: Which of the following geologic settings is indicative of a transgressive sequence?
a: Limestone deposited on top of shale
Sand deposited on top of limestone
Sand deposited on top of shale
Shale deposited on top of limestone
e: As rising seas creep inland, deep calm water arrives, gently laying clear-water limestone on top of older muddy shale.

q: Oak Ridge National Lab researchers are using neutron imaging to study different materials. Assuming every sample has the same dimensions, which of the following materials would give the highest contrast with the background in a thermal neutron imaging experiment?
e: Boron gobbles up passing neutrons like a hungry monster, casting a dark, sharp shadow that pops out in pictures!

q: Long-term preservation of deep sea carbonates is rare because of which of the following?
a: Most ocean crust and overlying sediments are subducted
Carbonates readily dissolve along the ocean floor when exposed to seawater
There is little carbonate-forming material occurring in ocean water
Carbonates react with silicates in the deep ocean, reducing the occurrence of carbonates along the ocean floor
e: The ocean floor acts like a giant conveyor belt, sliding deep into Earth's belly and melting ancient shells before they can stay.

q: An Ekman spiral in the surface ocean is created by the combined effect of what two influences?
e: Wind pushes the ocean surface, while Earth's spinning twist curves the deeper water into a swirling underwater staircase.

q: Which of the following pairs of metamorphic rocks can both form from shale?
e: When soft shale gets squeezed with gentle heat, it transforms into tough slate and then into shiny, silky phyllite!

q: You are mapping a flat erosional surface of an anticline fold in which no rock layers have been overturned. Which of the following describes the change in age of the rock layers in the anticline as one walks from the hinge to the limb?
a: The age of the layers is constant
e: In an arching rock fold, the oldest layers hide in the middle, so walking outward leads you to younger rocks.

q: Which of the following is LEAST accurate about the composition and structure of Earth's atmosphere:
a: at the uppermost boundary of the troposphere, air temperature begins to increase with increasing altitude
the ozone layer absorbs UV radiation from the Sun
there are about one-third as many gas molecules in the air atop Mt. Everest compared to sea level
it is divided into four distinct layers based primarily on pressure gradients
e: Earth's atmospheric blanket is actually divided by changes in temperature, not pressure, as it wraps our world in cozy layers.

q: Which of the following volcanic hazards can have worldwide climatic consequences?
e: Tiny bits of volcanic tephra shoot high into the sky, spreading a dusty sun umbrella that cools the whole planet!

q: In which of the following months is the Antarctic ozone hole the largest?
e: As spring sunshine returns to chilly Antarctica in September, chemical reactions wake up and open the ozone hole to its biggest size.

q: Which of the following is NOT considered a component of the modern theory of ice ages?
a: The Earth wobbles on its axis
The tilt of the Earth varies
Plate tectonics causes Earth's equator to change location
The Earth's orbit around the Sun varies
e: Our planet wobbles and tilts around the Sun, but its equator never moves. Continents do all the traveling instead!

q: Which of the following is an example of a negative feedback cycle?
a: The polar climate warms, permafrost melts, microbes digest vegetation and release methane, the methane further warms polar climate
The polar climate warms, sea ice melts, albedo lowers, and polar climate further warms
Global warming causes more water to evaporate from the surface, which condenses into clouds that then reflect more sunlight back to space, which cools the Earth
Global warming causes the southwestern U.S. to become even drier, reduced evaporation leads to fewer clouds so the Earth's albedo remains low, thus warming the climate
e: When Earth warms up, extra water forms fluffy clouds that bounce sunlight back to space, helping cool the whole planet.

q: Two parallel conducting plates, separated by a distance d, are connected to a battery. Which of the following is correct if the plate separation is doubled while the battery remains connected?
a: The electric charge on the plates is doubled
The potential difference between the plates is doubled
The potential difference between the plates is halved
The electric charge on the plates is halved
e: When the plates pull twice as far apart, their electric hug weakens, so half of the tiny charges wander away.

q: Oak Ridge National Lab has demonstrated that 3D-printed magnets made from recycled materials can outperform those created by traditional methods. Permanent magnets made from rare-earth lanthanoid [LAN-tha-noyd] elements have partially occupied shells of what type?
e: These super-strong magnetic elements keep their secret power tucked away in an unfinished, cozy little electron neighborhood called the f-shell!

q: Which of the following is NOT an alternative to compression in mountain formation?
a: Folding of rocks during thrust faulting
e: Folding rocks during a thrust fault is actually pure compression at work, squeezing giant stone layers together like an accordion!

q: Which of the following most accurately provides the three necessary ingredients for thunderstorm formation?
e: To brew a thunderstorm, you need damp air, unstable air eager to rise, and a helpful push upward to get started.

q: Which of the following is true of the eyewall replacement cycles of a hurricane?
a: Maximum sustained wind speeds tend to increase in the eyewall
A smaller eye expands outward and replaces a larger eye
The core of strongest wind tends to become more compact
Eyewall replacement cycles are common when a hurricane reaches a Category 5 status
e: When Category 5 hurricanes become absolute monsters, their howling eyewalls get worn out and build a brand-new outer ring!

q: Arkose contains quartz and at least 25 percent of what other mineral group?
e: Arkose is a special sandstone that loves quartz, but it must have a big scoop of feldspar crystals to earn its name.

q: The gemstones ruby and sapphire are a part of which of the following mineral groups?
e: Sparkling rubies and sapphires are made of aluminum holding hands tightly with oxygen, placing them in the colorful oxide family.

q: Glacial striations indicate which of the following?
a: The absolute age of a glacial event
e: As heavy glaciers march forward, rocks stuck in their bellies scratch grooves into the bedrock, showing exactly which way they traveled.

q: Which of the following minerals is not typically found in granite?
e: Sparkling granite loves quartz and feldspar, but olive-green olivine prefers hotter, deeper rocks and never joins the granite party.

q: Estuaries off the coast of which of the following states demonstrate the greatest nutrient pollution?
e: The mighty Mississippi River sweeps extra plant food from farms across the country straight into coastal Louisiana, creating the heaviest nutrient pollution.

q: What type of rock is found in most cave systems?
e: Dripping rainwater slowly tickles and dissolves soft limestone underground, carving out secret hollow tunnels where bats love to sleep.

q: In South Africa sedimentary rocks of Archean age have been found with rounded pyrite pebbles, which are not found in sedimentary rocks today. What is the most likely reason for this?
a: Pyrite is no longer formed on Earth's surface
Liquid water was not present during the Archean
Atmospheric oxygen levels were very low in the Archean
Atmospheric pressure was lower in the Archean
e: Pyrite quickly rusts in our air, so ancient pebbles could only roll safely down rivers because young Earth had almost no oxygen!

q: Which of the following is NOT a metamorphic rock?
e: While squished metamorphic rocks get baked underground, basalt is an igneous rock born when fiery lava cools on Earth's surface.

q: Which of the following is not a valid water mass defined by a unique temperature and salinity signature?
e: Deep ocean water forms in icy polar spots, so the warm Indian Ocean cannot make its own deep water mass.

q: Why does dolostone weather to a brownish colored rock?
a: Iron occurs in small amounts, replacing some of the magnesium in dolomite
Copper ions replace magnesium in dolostone as groundwater permeates the rock
Aluminum ions replace the calcium in the dolomite compounds, and there is a reaction between aluminum and the remaining magnesium ions
Magnesium ions replace the calcium ions in dolostone compounds
e: Tiny bits of iron sneak in to replace magnesium, and when fresh air touches them, they rust into a warm brown color.

q: Sustained periods of organic carbon burial over geologic time will most likely lead to which of the following?
e: When dead plants are buried before they can rot, oxygen is not used up, leaving extra fresh oxygen floating in the air!

q: Which of the following is a NOT a way in which scientists test the reliability of computer models of future climate?
a: Comparing model predictions of recent past climate to observed records
Comparing model predictions of distant past climate to proxy records
Checking for consistency between the outputs of many differently constructed models
Confirming that models have accurately predicted local weather events each year
e: Climate models look at big trends over decades, not whether it will rain on your local picnic this weekend.

q: Where is the fast food chain "Panda Express" headquartered?
e: Before cooking up yummy orange chicken everywhere, Panda Express set its bustling main headquarters in sunny Rosemead, California.

q: Who was the 18th century geologist who first developed the concept of uniformitarianism?
e: James Hutton was the patient thinker who realized Earth's quiet, everyday changes slowly built the grand world we see today!

q: Which of the following circumstances is linked most closely with the formation of sand dunes?
e: When a sleepy lake dries up, playful winds scoop up all that leftover sand to build giant dunes!

q: Which of the following volcanic hazards occurred from Mount Nyiragongo [nee-ir-uh-GON-goh] in 1977, killing 70 people in nearby villages?
a: Eruption of a noxious gas cloud
e: A giant, glowing lake of fiery lava suddenly cracked open and drained down the mountain in a flash.

q: Which of the following is NOT generally characteristic of a passive continental margin:
e: Quiet coasts have gentle slopes, while dramatic ocean trenches only show up where restless tectonic plates crash together!

q: Which of the following statements is NOT true about liquefied natural gas, or LNG?
a: LNG is produced by cooling natural gas to -260 Fahrenheit
If spilled at sea, LNG would evaporate quickly
e: Chilly liquefied gas won't eat through metal tanks because it actually isn't corrosive at all.

q: If the intent is to neutralize soil acidity, the mixing of which of the following materials in the soil would be the LEAST effective:
e: Gypsum can loosen packed dirt, but it lacks the special power to sweeten up grumpy, sour acid!

q: Which of the following choices describes one reason why the greenhouse effect is important?
a: It warms the Earth to a temperature necessary for life on Earth
It allows solar radiation to escape, preventing extreme radiation
It cools the Earth to a temperature necessary for life on Earth
It creates nitrogen for Earth's atmosphere
e: Like a cozy blanket tucked around our planet, the greenhouse effect keeps Earth warm enough for life to thrive!

q: The ocean floor near a midocean ridge has which of the following patterns of magnetization?
a: The same constant magnetization on both sides
Strips of alternate magnetization on both sides
It is magnetized in one direction on one side and in the opposite direction on the other side
It has no pattern of magnetization
e: Cooling seafloor rock acts like a tape recorder, freezing Earth's flipping magnetic poles into neat, matching stripes.

q: As a hurricane approaches the east coast of Florida from the east, the storm surge waves would be greatest at which of the following?
e: Because the storm spins counterclockwise, winds in the northwest corner push giant heaps of ocean water straight onto land!

q: With which country does France share its largest land border
e: Thanks to its rainforest territory in French Guiana, France actually shares its longest land border with sunny Brazil!

q: There is an igneous rock where all crystals are visible and the same size. Knowing only these two facts, what can be said about the cooling history of this rock?
a: It cooled in stages, at different levels within the crust
It cooled rapidly near the surface
It cooled on the surface and was quenched
It cooled slowly, at one time, at depth
e: Deep underground, cozy melted rock took its sweet time cooling all at once, letting matching crystals grow big!

q: Which of the following describes an electromagnet?
a: Current-carrying wire wrapped around a core
e: Twirling an electric wire around a metal core wakes up a mighty magnetic superpower on demand!
